lead_title: Trump admin still won't let Wi-Fi giant TP-Link sell its latest routers in US

evidence_pages.https://arstechnica.com/tech-policy/2026:
Trump admin still won't let Wi-Fi giant TP-Link sell its latest routers in US - Ars TechnicaSkip to content
Text settingsStory textSizeSmallStandardLargeWidth*StandardWideLinksStandardOrange* Subscribers only
TP-Link, which may be the top provider of wireless routers for US homes and small businesses, isn’t allowed to sell its latest Wi-Fi routers in the US. The Trump administrationimposed a sweeping banon foreign-made consumer routers in March 2026, and TP-Link hasn’t been able to obtain an exemption.
The rules prevent the import or sale of all new router models that are manufactured, assembled, designed, or developed outside the US. The Trump administration has control over which router makers receive special permission to import and sell new products through a waiver-review process involving the Federal Communications Commission, the Department of Defense, and the Department of Homeland Security.
While some of its competitors have obtained exemptions to the ban, TP-Link appears to be having a hard time making its case to government officials. Its routers approved before the March 2026 ban remain available for sale in the US, but its newly released Wi-Fi 8 routers cannot be imported or sold.
TP-Link’s struggle is not much of a surprise, given its history as a Chinese company and the Trump administration’s focus on reducing reliance on Chinese and other foreign technology. While TP-Link faces political challenges related to the Trump administration’s push for on-shoring, its problems go deeper: It must convince the government its routers aren’t vulnerable to foreign hacking campaigns and that its routers are not Chinese-controlled technology, as suggested at a Congressional committeehearinglast year.
TP-Link was founded in 1996 in China but has since split into two companies, with one in the US. The US-based TP-Linkestablished California as global headquartersin October 2024, months aftercompletinga “formal organizational separation” from the TP-Link entity in China.
“TP-Link has split from and no longer has any affiliation with TP-LINK Technologies Co., Ltd., which serves the mainland Chinese market. Despite having similar names, these companies have entirely different ownership, management, and operations,”TP-Link says.
Trump administration control of router sales
TP-Linkopened preordersfor its first Wi-Fi 8 router, the Archer 8 Ultra, in September, though not in the US. It’s expected toship this monthand costs £899.99 in the UK, or about $1,178. Since it’s priced like a luxury device, its unavailability in the US won’t make a difference to most consumers. But it’s unknown how long it will take TP-Link to gain permission to sell Wi-Fi 8 routers in the US, or whether it will receive permission at all.
TP-Link haspledged to assembleall new routers in the US, but convincing Trump officials that it is fully under US control is likely a difficult task. The government reviews of router makers’ requests for waivers, formally called conditional approvals, are shrouded in secrecy. From the outside, it is unclear whether the Trump administration applies consistent security criteria to all companies or whether it grants waivers to favored companies without regard to the actual security of their products.
Companies led by Trump allies Elon Musk and Jeff Bezos fared well in the reviews. SpaceX’s Starlink division obtained a waiver for its routers, while Amazon received a waiver covering routers for its Leo satellite broadband service and the devices sold by its Eero subsidiary. There have been26 waivers issued so far,covering products made by firms such as Netgear, Asus, Adtran, Calix, Nokia, Micro-Star International, Askey, Zyxel, Humax, and Vantiva.
Some US lawmakers seem to think the FCC process covers too many products. House Commerce Committee Ranking Member Frank Pallone, Jr. (D-N.J.) and Chairman Brett Guthrie (R-Ky.)proposed legislation in Septemberthat would limit the FCC’s authority to place entire categories of equipment on the list of banned products, as it did with routers.
The Pallone/Guthrie bill would also require the FCC to report to Congress a week before adding any new technology or service to what’s known as the Covered List and require new additions to include only technologies or services produced or provided by an entity controlled by a foreign adversary. That means China, Russia, North Korea, or Iran.
“The current process for identifying and barring malicious foreign technology has worked in many cases, but lacks the transparency, consistency, and clarity needed to meet our long-term national security needs as technology rapidly advances,” Pallone and Guthrie said in a joint statement.
Dramatic expansion of FCC’s Covered List
The Pentagon declined Ars’ request for comment on TP-Link’s request for an exemption. The FCC and Department of Homeland Security did not provide any comment.
The US ban on all foreign routers was part of a dramatic expansion of the Covered List, which is managed by the FCC in consultation with the Commerce Department and federal agencies with national security expertise. The Covered List was created by a 2020 law and received its first additions in March 2021. TP-Link, which may be the top provider of wireless routers for US homes and small businesses, isn’t allowed to sell its latest Wi-Fi routers in the US.
The Trump administrationimposed a sweeping banon foreign-made consumer routers in March 2026, and TP-Link hasn’t been able to obtain an exemption.
The rules prevent the import or sale of all new router models that are manufactured, assembled, designed, or developed outside the US.

The Trump administration has control over which router makers receive special permission to import and sell new products through a waiver-review process involving the Federal Communications Commission, the Department of Defense, and the Department of Homeland Security.
While some of its competitors have obtained exemptions to the ban, TP-Link appears to be having a hard time making its case to government officials.
Its routers approved before the March 2026 ban remain available for sale in the US, but its newly released Wi-Fi 8 routers cannot be imported or sold.
TP-Link’s struggle is not much of a surprise, given its history as a Chinese company and the Trump administration’s focus on reducing reliance on Chinese and other foreign technology.

While TP-Link faces political challenges related to the Trump administration’s push for on-shoring, its problems go deeper: It must convince the government its routers aren’t vulnerable to foreign hacking campaigns and that its routers are not Chinese-controlled technology, as suggested at a Congressional committeehearinglast year.
TP-Link was founded in 1996 in China but has since split into two companies, with one in the US.
The US-based TP-Linkestablished California as global headquartersin October 2024, months aftercompletinga “formal organizational separation” from the TP-Link entity in China.
“TP-Link has split from and no longer has any affiliation with TP-LINK Technologies Co., Ltd., which serves the mainland Chinese market.
Despite having similar names, these companies have entirely different ownership, management, and operations,”TP-Link says.
TP-Linkopened preordersfor its first Wi-Fi 8 router, the Archer 8 Ultra, in September, though not in the US.
It’s expected toship this monthand costs £899.99 in the UK, or about $1,178.
Since it’s priced like a luxury device, its unavailability in the US won’t make a difference to most consumers.
But it’s unknown how long it will take TP-Link to gain permission to sell Wi-Fi 8 routers in the US, or whether it will receive permission at all.
TP-Link haspledged to assembleall new routers in the US, but convincing Trump officials that it is fully under US control is likely a difficult task.
The government reviews of router makers’ requests for waivers, formally called conditional approvals, are shrouded in secrecy.

From the outside, it is unclear whether the Trump administration applies consistent security criteria to all companies or whether it grants waivers to favored companies without regard to the actual security of their products.
Companies led by Trump allies Elon Musk and Jeff Bezos fared well in the reviews.
SpaceX’s Starlink division obtained a waiver for its routers, while Amazon received a waiver covering routers for its Leo satellite broadband service and the devices sold by its Eero subsidiary.
There have been26 waivers issued so far,covering products made by firms such as Netgear, Asus, Adtran, Calix, Nokia, Micro-Star International, Askey, Zyxel, Humax, and Vantiva.
Some US lawmakers seem to think the FCC process covers too many products.

Anthropic’s 7 founders cashed out nearly $2B in record-breaking IPO
Julie Bort4:43 PM PST · November 19, 2026
Anthropic became a public company on Thursday, raising a total of $81.3 billion, including $1.95 billion for its seven founders. As we previously reported, each of themponied up about 3.4 million shares apieceto sell in the IPO.
At the upgraded IPO price of $83 per share, that means they each pocketed about $280 million before underwriting fees and taxes. It looked like they had calculated the number of shares they planned to sell to give them each around $250 million if shares hit $74. That was the midpoint price from Anthropic’s original price range. So that’s a cool $30-ish million more for each of them than perhaps they were gunning for.
Anthropic implied in its IPO filings that the founders aren’t entirely in this for the money though. The company said that each of the founders has pledged to dedicate 80% of their personal equity in the companyto philanthropy.
However, if any of them struggle to live on their quarter of a billion, they can scale back their charitable commitments. The company points out that these commitments are “voluntary, revocable expressions of each co-founder’s philanthropic intent and do not constitute legally binding obligations.”
With the IPO in the record books, there were a few other interesting numbers worth highlighting.
$104.8 billion.That’s really the amount Anthropic raised for its coffers (with a possibility of $117 billion, if the bankers buy all of their allotment of shares). In addition to selling its Class A common stock, it also sold a previously announced $26 billion worth of a special non-voting Class N stock to some of the biggest tech names in the industry.
Nvidia bought $10 billion of these Class N shares, Google bought $10 billion, and AMD, Broadcom, Micron, Microsoft, and TSMC divvied up the rest.
Just for comparison: When Facebook had its then record-breaking IPO in 2012,it raised $16 billion on IPO day.
28% stake to Amazon and Google combined.All told, at the higher IPO share price, Google wound up owning 13.4% of the company. Amazon also now has a big stake in Anthropicbecause when it previously invested in the AI lab as a startup,it was granted promissory notes that could be converted to equity. It converted a small percentage of them as part of the IPO, leaving it with a 14.6% stake. Had it converted all of them, Amazon could have owned nearly 24%.
The two large cloud providers now own 28% of Anthropic, the AI lab says.
More than$1 trillion.As mind-blowing as it is to raise nearly $105 billion, giving Anthropic nearly $230 billion of working capital available (along with capital it already had on hand), the company’s need for future capital is still far greater.
Anthropic needs about $70.7 billion just to cover its compute and infrastructure spending commitments in the next 12 months as of the quarter ended September 30, 2026. It needs $451.6 billion to cover these commitments before the end of 2030. And it has racked up hundreds of billions of other commitments that are either conditional (and may not happen) or haven’t been priced yet.
All told, the company has disclosed a ballpark of $1.05 trillion to $1.08 trillion in infrastructure commitments in its foreseeable future. This was a huge IPO. But it is a pricey business to run.

DETROW: What's interesting here is there's so many worries about AI right now, and one of the big worries is that, you know, the industry is possibly in a big bubble. Given that, why do you think investors were so eager to snap up these shares?
RUWITCH: Well, AI is changing the way people do a lot of things, from searching for the internet to developing new medicines, and Anthropic's right at the center of it - right? - with its Claude AI models. They are among the most advanced models in the world, and they're popular. Today, Anthropic became the first publicly traded big AI lab that only does AI. SpaceX is one of its AI rivals, but it does other things like put satellites into orbit. So prior to today, if the average person wanted investment exposure to AI, it was less direct. They had buy shares in companies that make chips, for instance, or software or satellites.
You're right. There is tension around AI. People are worried about data centers. They're worried about losing their jobs to AI, worried about AI going rogue or spiraling out of control. And investors have been concerned about all that money pouring into AI, whether or not it's justified.
DETROW: What did the company's leadership have to say about those risks this morning when trading got underway?
RUWITCH: Yeah. CEO Dario Amodei tackled this head-on in his remarks while ringing that opening bell at the NASDAQ. You know, he's long been outspoken about AI's risks. In fact, he and a handful of others left competitor, OpenAI, and founded this company five years ago because they were worried about AI's safety. Today, he said going public won't change that mission.
DARIO AMODEI: We will not bend to either business nor political pressure. Today puts the company in a stronger financial position, and in doing so, only strengthens our resolve to do the right thing.

DETROW: That sounds like something that's very easy to say and very hard to do. I mean...

Anthropic has committed to spending hundreds of billions of dollars on data centers to build and run powerful new AI models to try to get there, and it'll take revenue for that.
DETROW: Where will that money come from, though?
RUWITCH: You know, at the moment, most of Anthropic's revenue appears to be coming from companies. But as with every new technology, success or failure hinges on how quickly people adopt it. Radio spread quickly into American homes. Washing machines took decades. So the question is, will AI be more like the radio or the washing machine?

Anthropic’s unusual power structure gives it free rein to shape AI’s future.﻿
is The Verge’s senior AI reporter. An AI beat reporter for more than five years, her work has also appeared in CNBC, MIT Technology Review, Wired UK, and other outlets.
Today is a new beginning for Anthropic: a years-in-the-making IPO that beat out SpaceX for most valuable of all time, having raised $81.3 billion and set an important precedent for the other public AI lab debuts to come. But it’s not simply a financial milestone.
Anthropic was founded on the idea that it prioritized safety more than other labs; its founders had left executive research positions at OpenAI. As the AI race has accelerated, though, its executives have emphasized that Anthropic can only fulfill this mission by coming in first place, requiring lots of money and compute. Unsurprisingly, thoughtful, safe, and intentional AI development can conflict with the kind of sheer speed that winning this race requires. Adding in an initial public offering only complicates things further, and Anthropic’s leadership can pursue it more or less unilaterally. That’s thanks to a corporate structure focused on insulating the company from shareholder pressure to turn a profit — but one that also removes typical checks on its power.
One former Anthropic employee, who left ahead of the IPO, said he and others at Anthropic have increasingly been feeling that the current pace of AI development is “untenable under normal market structures,” particularly with the mismatched incentives at play in a powerful industry with little to no oversight.
Anthropic has spent years billing itself as different from, and more careful than, other AI companies. In theory, this extends to its plan for going public. It’s registered as a Public Benefit Corporation, which means Anthropic’s board has a responsibility to balance its mission against shareholder wealth maximization. As my colleague Robert Hart has discussed before, it has also developed ahighly unusual power structure.
Anthropic’s Long-Term Benefit Trust (LTBT), introducedin 2023, and its founders have controlling voting rights, meaning they’d never be able to be voted out by shareholders even as a public company. A special class of stock, Class T, allows a small group of trustees — the members of the LTBT — the “authority to select and remove a portion of” Anthropic’s board. They exist outside typical shareholder pressure and theoretically are a check for the founders, tasked with a mission to “balance the financial interests of our stockholders and our public benefit purpose at key junctures where we expect the consequences of our decisions to reach far beyond Anthropic.”
The reality is significantly more complicated. The LTBT technically chooses four members of Anthropic’s seven-person board, for instance, but one of those four effectively needs to be approved by Anthropic’s founders, leaving the trust short of straightforward majority control. There are also stipulations about nominating or removing a director: the LTBT must provide its decision with 30 days’ notice to the company’s “nominating and corporate governance committee,” which consists of three members: co-founder Daniela Amodei (who is chair of the committee), Netflix co-founder Reed Hastings, and Anthropic investor Yasmin Razavi.
Though the LTBT members are “financially disinterested” in the company, there’s also nothing stopping Anthropic from hypothetically hiring away a trustee and paying them a lot of money to work for the company. Mariano-Florentino Cuéllar (a former trustee) joined Anthropic in August as its Chief Global Affairs Officer, and OpenAI has in the past hired a former board member, Fidji Simo, to an executive position within the company. One could imagine a scenario in which, if a trustee was “looking a little bit too activist-y or something, they could just make that trustee an offer with millions of dollars in effective compensation that would entail stepping down from the trust, and that’s one way that they could have some oversight over this,” said Tyler Johnston, founder of The Midas Project, a nonprofit AI industry watchdog.
Although the LTBT is billed as a way to check Anthropic’s leadership, to some outside observers, the fine print looks shaky. “The trust, since it doesn’t have a financial interest in Anthropic, could theoretically use its power with three slash four directors to keep the company on mission,” says Ann Lipton, law professor at the University of Colorado Law School and an expert in corporate governance. “One might question how likely that is to occur.”
Moreover, Lipton questions whether the trust would know enough to gauge when to hit the brakes on a company plan or product even if they did have such authority. The four listed LTBT members aren’t known to be AI experts: they include former Fed Chair Ben Bernanke, foreign policy analyst Richard Fontaine, experimental physicist Christopher Stubbs, and former GiveWell executive Neil Buddy Shah, who is chair of the LTBT. “I’m not convinced that the trustees or the directors that they appoint have the insight into AI and AI development to be able to make these choices,” Lipton says. “They’re very prestigious people, but what does Ben Bernanke know about AI?”
Several experts compared Anthropic’s LTBT to OpenAI’s nonprofit board before Altman’s ouster: “The powers, or lack thereof, of the Long-Term Benefit Trust … [are] analogous in some ways to the powers that the OpenAI nonprofit has,” said The Midas Project’s Johnston. Of course, that board’s decision to oust OpenAI CEO Sam Altman ended up leading, days later, to Altman’s return as CEO and the majority of the board’s resignation and replacement.
But there’s a notable difference between that and the LTBT. Before OpenAI’s restructuring, its nonprofit board had the ability to step in and guide day-to-day decisions at the company when deemed necessary, and even after its restructuring, they retained that ability for safety and security matters, such as delaying or stopping a model release. Anthropic's stockjumped 17% in its Nasdaq debuton Thursday, closing at $97.17 per share and giving the Claude creator a market cap of roughly $1.8 trillion. That makes it the seventh-most-valuable U.S. company, despite being less than six years old.
Earlier in the day, the second floor of the Nasdaq was decorated in orange, Anthropic's signature color. Founders and backers were given Claude lapel pins that served as their ticket to the bell-ringing, which was followed by a champagne toast ahead of the opening. With the first trade, the stock shot up to $111.50.
The prior afternoon Anthropicraised $81.3 billion, toppingElon Musk'sSpaceXfor the largest IPO on record.
It was a wild feat, and Anthropic backers breathed a sigh of relief. Days earlier, Altimeter Capital's Brad Gerstner, whose firm put in an order for $5 billion of stock in the IPO, acknowledged that theelection results, the semiconductor selloff and theHuang scandalcreated "a very bad backdrop" for the offering. Nvidia shares are headed for their seventh straight weekly drop, losing 38% of their value over that stretch.
Malcolm Ethridge, managing partner at Capital Area Planning Group and a CNBC contributor, pointed to the high levels of volatility in the market as a real risk to going public. TheCboe Volatility Index (VIX)is up 46% this month, including a 16% surge on Thursday, to over 28.4.
Ethridge said that with the VIX above 25, most companies would consider "shelving" an IPO. But Anthropic decided, "this is our window," Ethridge said.

"Just truly, truly market redefining," ICONIQ partner Will Griffith, an Anthropic investor, said in an interview. "The ability to achieve this growth, at this scale, in this short of a time frame, this efficiently — the world has never seen that before."
Not a company that's 'optimizing price'
Anthropic CEODario Amodeico-founded Anthropic in 2021, after he and ahandful of other researchersdefected from OpenAI, now its chief rival, to pursue what they viewed as a safer approach to AI. The company captivated the corporate world with itsClaude AImodels and products, which fueled its unprecedented rise.
With tens of billions of dollars flooding in over the past few years from private investors and tech giants, Anthropic was able to secure the computing power needed to train frontier AI models and serve customers with an expanding portfolio of services.
Anthropic executives, includingCFO Krishna Rao, used those funding rounds as opportunities to build goodwill with the market, particularly when it came to pricing. The company opted not to squeeze every last dollar out of the ecosystem, preferring, in Amodei's words, to "underpromise and overdeliver."
"This isn't a company that's focused on optimizing price," Deeter said. "They could have priced the IPO higher. At every financing they have chosen to leave some money on the table."

Anthropic has also worked to prove itself as a company that can deploy capital responsibly. Of the more than $140 billion that the company has raised, it's only spent around $10 billion, which helped to reassure investors that it could weather a potential storm.
The companyconfidentially filedits prospectus with the Securities and Exchange Commission in June, and OpenAI, followed days later. But by August, OpenAI executives signaled that the ChatGPT maker was targeting a2027 debut, as a series ofsecurity incidentsrattled the industry andopposition to data centersswept the nation.
The market, stung by rising oil prices and the Federal Reserve's plan to raise interest rates, soured on the AI trade and lost its appetite for IPOs. Biometric ring makerOura, Australian AI data center operatorFirmusand SK Hynix's U.S.-basedSolidigmsubsidiary all postponed or abandoned plans to go public.
Gerstner said Altimeterreduced its exposureto the broader AI trade to the lowest in three years. Meanwhile, the firm aimed to put five times as much into Anthropic's IPO as it had invested in any prior initial share sale, Gerstner told CNBC.
Anthropic begantesting the waterswith investors in August, before kicking off its official roadshow last week. It was all taking place while many AI stocks were melting down.
Having successfully reached the public market, Anthropic now has a boatload of much-needed cash on hand as it continues to spend aggressively on compute capacity.
Assuming underwriters exercise their option to buy all the shares available to them, Anthropic's fundraise would total $93.5 billion in the IPO, topping the $85.7 billion raised

Global stock markets slump as Anthropic IPO fails to stem AI sell-off
Asian markets on track for their worst week since 2020, with European and US stocks also way down
Global stock markets have slumped asAnthropic’s record-breaking IPOfailed to stem a sell-off in AI-linked companies.
Asian stock markets were on track for their worst week since 2020, as shares in big chip companies fell on Friday. In Taiwan, stocks dropped 6.7% to hit their lowest point since mid-April, with the chip maker TSMC down about 6%.
The scale of the decline in Taiwan prompted the chair of its stock exchange to pledge to ensure the stable operation ⁠of capital markets, and reassure investors they should remain confident in the fundamentals of Taiwanese companies.
In Japan, the Nikkei index fell 5%, while South Korea’s tech-heavy Kospi index lost 5.5%. Shares in the tech investor SoftBank had their worst day in more than two years, down 14.5% in Tokyo, amid worries around its aggressive bets on AI.
European stock markets were heading for their worst week since March, with the pan-European Stoxx 600 dropping 1.3% in the first 90 minutes.
The sell-off followed losses on Wall Street on Thursday, where the main indices all fell by more than 2% on a day dominated byAnthropic’s IPO.
Anthropic’s shares jumped by 17% on Thursday, after briefly surging by almost 40% when trading in the frontier AI firm began. But they were heading for losses on Friday, down 6% at $91.30, falling back towards the IPO price of $83.
Chris Beauchamp, the chief market analyst at the investing and trading platform IG, said Anthropic could be “draining market liquidity”, as investors sell shares in other companies to raise funds to pay for stock in the newly floated AI firm.
“The slide from yesterday’s highs sends a message that there might be more at work here than investors realise, and while brokers are scrambling to buy more, that liquidity has to come from somewhere, and the other tech names may be the first ones to feel the pressure,” Beauchamp said.
Anthropic’s flotation has failed to ease worries around the AI trade, as investors increasingly question whether companies can deliver the returns necessary to justify the billions of dollars being poured into the AI build out.
Daniela Hathorn, a senior market analyst at Capital.com, said: “The IPO demonstrated that demand for AI exposure remains strong, but it has not been enough to overcome concerns about elevated valuations, profitability and the sustainability of investment spending.
“The broader market mood has shifted from buying the dip towards questioning whether the correction has further to run. The weakness in equal-weighted indices suggests that selling pressure is no longer confined to a handful of technology giants, while Europe’s recent outperformance has also faded.”
Britain’s FTSE 100 share index hit a five-month low on Friday morning. It has dropped by 4.8% this week, and is heading for its biggest weekly fall since the start of the Iran war.
Fears that US central bankers may raise interest rates to fight inflation have lifted the dollar to a 19-month high, and pushed down the gold price – with gold on track for its worst week since March.

fact_units.text: Anthropic's 7 founders cashed out nearly $2B in record-breaking IPO | TechCrunch
Anthropic’s 7 founders cashed out nearly $2B in record-breaking IPO
Julie Bort4:43 PM PST · November 19, 2026
Anthropic became a public company on Thursday, raising a total of $81.3 billion, including $1.95 billion for its seven founders.
As we previously reported, each of themponied up about 3.4 million shares apieceto sell in the IPO.
At the upgraded IPO price of $83 per share, that means they each pocketed about $280 million before underwriting fees and taxes.
It looked like they had calculated the number of shares they planned to sell to give them each around $250 million if shares hit $74.
That was the midpoint price from Anthropic’s original price range.
So that’s a cool $30-ish million more for each of them than perhaps they were gunning for.
Anthropic implied in its IPO filings that the founders aren’t entirely in this for the money though.
The company said that each of the founders has pledged to dedicate 80% of their personal equity in the companyto philanthropy.
However, if any of them struggle to live on their quarter of a billion, they can scale back their charitable commitments.
The company points out that these commitments are “voluntary, revocable expressions of each co-founder’s philanthropic intent and do not constitute legally binding obligations.”
With the IPO in the record books, there were a few other interesting numbers worth highlighting.
$104.8 billion.That’s really the amount Anthropic raised for its coffers (with a possibility of $117 billion, if the bankers buy all of their allotment of shares).
In addition to selling its Class A common stock, it also sold a previously announced $26 billion worth of a special non-voting Class N stock to some of the biggest tech names in the industry.
Nvidia bought $10 billion of these Class N shares, Google bought $10 billion, and AMD, Broadcom, Micron, Microsoft, and TSMC divvied up the rest.
Just for comparison: When Facebook had its then record-breaking IPO in 2012,it raised $16 billion on IPO day.
28% stake to Amazon and Google combined.All told, at the higher IPO share price, Google wound up owning 13.4% of the company.
Amazon also now has a big stake in Anthropicbecause when it previously invested in the AI lab as a startup,it was granted promissory notes that could be converted to equity.
It converted a small percentage of them as part of the IPO, leaving it with a 14.6% stake.
Had it converted all of them, Amazon could have owned nearly 24%.
The two large cloud providers now own 28% of Anthropic, the AI lab says.

More than$1 trillion.As mind-blowing as it is to raise nearly $105 billion, giving Anthropic nearly $230 billion of working capital available (along with capital it already had on hand), the company’s need for future capital is still far greater.
Anthropic needs about $70.7 billion just to cover its compute and infrastructure spending commitments in the next 12 months as of the quarter ended September 30, 2026.
It needs $451.6 billion to cover these commitments before the end of 2030.
And it has racked up hundreds of billions of other commitments that are either conditional (and may not happen) or haven’t been priced yet.
All told, the company has disclosed a ballpark of $1.05 trillion to $1.08 trillion in infrastructure commitments in its foreseeable future.

Tashima said he wanted to restore trust in FIFA, drawing parallels with ⁠2016, when Infantino took charge after acorruption scandal.

Race for the Fifa presidency: lineup revealed to challenge Gianni Infantino
Philippe Diallo and Kozo Tashima are both standing
But Ramon Vega fails to get the necessary backing
Fifa has confirmed that Gianni Infantino will face challenges fromPhilippe Dialloof France and Japan’sKozo Tashimain March’s presidential election.
The president of the French football federation and the honorary president of the Japan football association submitted nomination letters with endorsements from five member associations by Wednesday night’s midnight CET deadline. The former Switzerland and Tottenham defender Ramon Vega has not met that threshold, despite repeatedly saying he would stand.
Fifa’s World Cup TV rights documents indicate hydration breaks to stay in 2030Read more
“The candidatures have been forwarded to the electoral committee for examination and for passing a decision on the admission of the candidate,”Fifasaid.
The election in Rabat on 18 March will be the first time Infantino has faced opposition since he was first elected in 2016, when he defeated the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) president, Sheikh Salman bin Ebrahim al-Khalifa, by 115 votes to 88.
Infantino had been expected to be re-elected unopposed for a third time after declaring his candidacy in April and had receivedmore than 200 letters of endorsementfrom national associations by the time of last summer’s World Cup, but theemergence of his Fifa Forward Enterprise planhas led to a haemorrhaging of support.
Uefa has led a campaign to unseat him since July with backing from Concacaf, the North and Central American and Caribbean confederation, and initially the AFC, but with Infantino conducting a global tour to rally support from smaller nations the opposition has struggled to put up an alternative candidate.
Tashima was the first to declare last month in defiance of the AFC, which after criticising the FFE proposalis backing Infantino, having come under pressure from the region’s two major financial powerhouses, Saudi Arabia and Qatar.
As revealed by the Guardian on Monday, Diallo was belatedlychosen last weekend as the Uefa candidateafter a complex selection process. The 63-year-old’s emergence was a surprise because Uefa had initially hoped to field a more high-profile candidate, such as Arsène Wenger. The Hungarian banker Sandor Csanyi, the president of his country’s FA, had strong backers owing to his close relationship with Uefa’s president, Aleksander Ceferin.
Diallo and Tashima may yet join forces in an attempt to defeat Infantino amid concerns of splitting those opposed to the president among the 211 Fifa members. Were that to occur it is expected Tashima would stand aside, a development that would be supported by Uefa.
All three candidates will be vetted by Fifa’s governance, audit and compliance committee, chaired by the Infantino ally Bruno Chiomento, before the nominations are confirmed on 18 February.

White House fails to credit Biden role in U.S. drug deaths dropIn a statement celebrating the historic drop in drug deaths, the White House pointed to successes since President Trump took office. In fact, the biggest progress happened under the Biden administration.
As overdose deaths fall, White House makes misleading claims about who deserves credit

Families look on as President Donald Trump speaks during a ceremony to sign the "Halt All Lethal Trafficking of Fentanyl Act" in the East Room of the White House on July 16, 2025.Evan Vucci/APhide caption
When the White House announced big improvements in the number of people dying from fatal drug overdoses earlier this week, officials pointed to hopefulnew data from the Centers for Disease Control and Preventionshowing U.S. drug deaths have plunged to their lowest level in roughly a decade, saving nearly 50,000 lives each year.
NPR Exclusive: U.S. overdose deaths plummet, saving thousands of lives
But leading drug policy researchers say the White House statement also made misleading claims about the timing and cause of the remarkable public health success when it said thatgains occurred primarily over the last 18 months due to policies enacted under President Trump's leadership.
"The historic decline in drug overdose deaths demonstrates that America is unequivocally winning the fight against illicit drugs," White House Office of National Drug Control Policy director Sara Carter saidin a statement.
Carter credited heightened border security under Trump and claims of success dismantling "narco-terrorist" organizations for the recovery. "Critically, this represents a an approximately 41.5% decrease in total drug overdose deaths compared to the peak under the previous administration," the statement said.
What the White House failed to disclose is that declines in overdose fatalities began much earlier, under the Biden administration, with most of the gains occurring before Trump returned to office.
"Since the spring of 2023, we have seen a steady decline in overdose deaths," said Vanda Felbab-Brown, a drug policy expert at the Brookings Institution. "The fact that it has been sustained is very important."
Fentanyl crisis on Biden's watch, then a pivot toward fewer deaths
According to CDC data, reductions in drug deaths began in 2023 and have continued steadily for at least 39 consecutive months — not 18 months as the ONDCP statement said. By the time Biden left office, fatal overdoses had already dropped by roughly one-third, an improvementdescribed by addiction experts at the timeas unprecedented.

Nabarun Dasgupta, a street drug researcher at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, wasone of the first scientists to detectthe stunning drop in overdose deaths. He said the trend toward fewer deaths began in some regions and among some demographic groups as early as 2021 and rapidly gained momentum nationwide.
"It was really the period early 2024 through spring 2025 where we were seeing the greatest rate of decline that we've ever seen," Dasgupta said.
Deaths from fentanyl smuggled into the U.S. from Mexico firstbegan to rise in 2013during President Obama's time in office and accelerated during Trump's first term. Fentanyl overdoses spiked sharply the first two years of Biden's presidency, during the COVID-19 pandemic. Despite progress, fentanyl remainsthe leading cause of drug deathsnationwide.
Dasgupta, Felbab-Brown and other and addiction experts credit the Biden administration for rolling out policy responses that included wider access to healthcare, making the opioid overdose medication naloxone more readily available, and negotiating a deal with China that disrupted the flow of industrial chemicals used to make fentanyl.
President Joe Biden met China's President President Xi Jinping in Woodside, Calif., in November 2023, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperative conference. China agreed to curtail shipments of the chemicals used to make fentanyl, the drug at the heart of the U.S. overdose epidemic.Doug Mills/Pool/The New York Timeshide caption
toggle captioniDoug Mills/Pool/The New York Times
The Biden team also scored significant drug interdiction wins against the Mexican cartels that smuggle fentanyl. "We have certainly been seeing over many years, going back to the Biden administration, important efforts to crack down against them," said Felbab-Brown.
Dasgupta and Felbab-Brown both said improvements in reducing drug mortality have continued under Trump. They said it's important to have an accurate timeline of the overdose crisis because researchers are still trying to understand why deaths involving fentanyl surged and why so many fewer people are now dying.
White House on Biden role in declines
NPR asked the White House about progress in the fentanyl fight under Biden. In an emailed statement, ONDCP director Carter,a former podcaster, journalist and Fox News contributor, blamed Biden for failing to secure the U.S.-Mexico border and for allowing drug deaths to surge in the first place.
"While drug overdose deaths eventually began to decline following the peak, the Biden Administration doesn't get to take credit for overseeing the highest drug overdose numbers in history, then bringing them down from their own failure," Carter said.

According to Carter, the Trump administration is now well-positioned to build on overdose death reductions made over the last three years, in part by maintaining border security and by continuing to "relentlessly attack" drug gangs.

White House national cyber director Sean Cairncross is leaving his post, with Pentagon CIO Kirsten Davies set to serve as acting director after a week of high-profile U.S. technology outages.
The role, which advises the president on cybersecurity and coordinates U.S. cyber policy across federal agencies, has been handed to Pentagon chief information officer Davies on an interim basis. A permanent national cyber director must first be nominated by the president and then confirmed by the Senate.
Axios first reported Cairncross's exit, citing two White House officials who said PresidentDonald Trump'schief of staff Stephen Miller pushed for his departure. One official told Axios that Miller thought Cairncross "lacked the strong cyber credentials to perform the job."
The White House and the Office of the National Cyber Director did not immediately respond to a CNBC request for comment. A White House official confirmed Cairncross's departure toNBC NewsandCBS Newson Thursday.
United States National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross attends an event with U.S. President Donald Trump in the Oval Office of the White House on June 22, 2026 in Washington, DC.Andrew Harnik | Getty Images
It comes after a series of technology outages, including a nationwide aviation ground stop, a worldwideMicrosoftOutlook outage and a reported blackout of theNational Security Agency's classified communications network.
The White Househas insistedthat there areno indications of a coordinated cyberattack, state-sponsored activity or malign actor behind recent tech outages.
Davies addressed her responsibilities in the new position and thanked Miller and PresidentDonald Trumpfor their confidence late Thursday.
"Our nation stands in the crossroad of analog, digital, and quantum technologies, our American way of living increasingly interconnected. Our opportunity is to dominate the cyber landscape for generations to come… but only if we modernize and drive resilience into the foundations our great nation runs on,"she wrote on X.

The All Blacks struggle to hide their emotions after their shock loss to Wales in Cardiff.Photograph: Joe Giddens/PAView image in fullscreenThe All Blacks struggle to hide their emotions after their shock loss to Wales in Cardiff.Photograph: Joe Giddens/PA
Rattled All Blacks face rare twin threat as England eye back-to-back scalps
After their seismic defeat by Wales, New Zealand face the prospect of history repeating itself in unwanted ways
They still talk about the last – and only – time the All Blacks contrived to lose twice in succession to England. Back in 2002-03, as now, there was a Rugby World Cup looming in Australia and New Zealand had no shortage of quality players. “There is so much talent in New Zealand that, if they don’t win the World Cup, there should be an inquiry,” opined Steve Hansen, Wales’s head coach at the time, before England’s fateful visit to Wellington in the summer of 2003.
There’s a fresh inquiry under way now, even before the All Blacks trot out of the Twickenham tunnel this Saturday for the 48th meeting between the two nations. WhileSaturday’s 35-28 defeatended a 73-year wait for a Wales win, from a home perspective it has inevitably precipitated plenty of dark muttering back in the land of the long flat white.
All Blacks admit they ‘let country down’ against Wales and gear up for EnglandRead more
Caught in the firing line, rightly or wrongly, are some big names including Beauden Barrett and Richie Mo’unga. Clearly the Cardiff calamity was not their fault alone but, equally, the shortage of clear-sighted tactical nous in the latter stages was glaring. Barrett, captaining his country for the first time, was winning his 149th cap. Whether he reaches 150 this Saturday remains to be seen.
Of course, there are reinforcements riding over the hill with Codie Taylor, Damian McKenzie, Cam Roigard, Jordie Barrett and others all ready to serve against England. Never underestimate, either, the stiffening of the sinews when New Zealand’s rugby reputation is on the line. “Pressure is a lifestyle when you’re in the All Blacks,” their forwards coach, Jason Ryan, said last year. “That’s the way it’s got to be.”
But still. While those two narrow losses in 2002 and 2003 clearly stung – and coincided with a prolonged Kiwi failure to win a World Cup until 2011 – it is necessary to rewind to 1999 to find the last occasion New Zealand lost in London and Cardiff on consecutive autumn weekends, the opposition being France and South Africa respectively.
Before that, the last time they went down to Wales and England on the same tour of Europe was in 1935-36 when they lost 13-12 in Cardiff and – unlucky for some – 13-0 at Twickenham. In other words Dave Rennie’s squad will find themselves in uncomfortable territory if they cannot bounce back immediately this Saturday.
Which All Black sides have mostly tended to do as a matter of routine. Remember when they lost 38-30 to Argentina in Wellington in 2024? Seven days later in Auckland they hammered the same opponents 42-10. The following year they lost again to the Pumas in Buenos Aires only to rebound and defeat South Africa in their very next fixture.
But is that familiar old black magic now at risk of fading to grey? South Africa deservedly won this year’s best-of-four Greatest Rivalry series 3-1 and New Zealand’s subsequent two Bledisloe Cup wins over the Wallabies no longer look quite so impressive given Australia’s increasing end-of-year travails.
It doesn’t help, either, that the centre Quinn Tupaea has broken a thumb and joined a lengthening injury list at the precise moment England are starting to stockpile more strength in depth. The Springboks had a good deal of scrummaging joy at New Zealand’s expense in August and September and the English maul, bolstered by the return of Maro Itoje and others, is also now re-emerging as a useful weapon.
So, this could just be England’s chance to channel the old-school spirit of Martin Johnson’s erstwhile World Cup winners. And maybe it is a timely omen that this weekend Twickenham will also be staging the launch of a major new fundraising campaign,Front Up to MND, spearheaded by Lewis Moody who scored a try in that breathless 31-28 win over the All Blacks.
“My memories of that 2002 game are of getting knee-dropped and elbowed as I scored a try in the corner,” chuckled Moody, the former England captain who was diagnosed with motor neurone disease last year. “I had a really lovely try-scoring celebration lined up which I never got to perform because I was trying to locate my lungs after Chris Jack and Dougie Howlett both attempted to finish me off. But we ended up winning so in some respects it’s a very positive note on which to lead into this weekend.”
New Zealand, then as now, had several injury absentees but that was definitely not the case for the rematch in Wellington the following June. Richie McCaw, Carlos Spencer, Justin Marshall, Joe Rokocoko and Tana Umaga all started with Dan Carter, Mils Muliaina, Jerry Collins and Brad Thorn on the bench. Famously England were reduced to 13 men with Neil Back and Lawrence Dallaglio in the sin-bin but somehow clung on, in blustery wet conditions, to win 15-13 with Jonny Wilkinson contributing all the points.
It was nothing like as close 12 months ago when Steve Borthwick’s side roared back from 12-0 down to sweep aside Scott Robertson’s visitors 33-19. So deeply average were New Zealand that Robertson ended up being relieved of his coaching duties but the arrival of Rennie, after a promising start, has yet to bear much kiwi fruit in big games.
And the worst scenario of all? New Zealand lose this Saturday and find themselves in a second-place North v South playoff. When the opposition could easily be … England again. A thunderbolt loss of a defeat to Wales is one thing but then to follow it with two defeats in eight days to the bloody English? Let’s just say the All Blacks have heaps to play for.

Rattled All Blacks face rare twin threat as England eye back-to-back scalps
After their seismic defeat by Wales, New Zealand face the prospect of history repeating itself in unwanted ways
They still talk about the last – and only – time the All Blacks contrived to lose twice in succession to England.
Back in 2002-03, as now, there was a Rugby World Cup looming in Australia and New Zealand had no shortage of quality players.

“There is so much talent in New Zealand that, if they don’t win the World Cup, there should be an inquiry,” opined Steve Hansen, Wales’s head coach at the time, before England’s fateful visit to Wellington in the summer of 2003.
There’s a fresh inquiry under way now, even before the All Blacks trot out of the Twickenham tunnel this Saturday for the 48th meeting between the two nations.
WhileSaturday’s 35-28 defeatended a 73-year wait for a Wales win, from a home perspective it has inevitably precipitated plenty of dark muttering back in the land of the long flat white.

NWSL Championship: Washington Spirit and Kansas City Current face off Saturday for the title
Audi Field hosts as Washington aims to snap consecutive final heartbreaks, while Croix Bethune and Kansas City chase the franchise's first league crown
BySandra HerreraNov 20, 2026at 6:49 am ET•4 min readGetty Images
The hottest ticket in the nation's capital is the biggest game of the year in the NWSL. The Washington Spirit and the Kansas City Current will compete in the 2026 NWSL Championship, and both clubs have unfinished business. Kickoff is set for Nov. 21 at 8 p.m. ET onCBSandParamount+.
The Spirit return to the final after settling for runner-up finishes in the previous two NWSL Championship events. They lost 1-0 to the Orlando Pride in 2024 and fell short against Gotham FC in 2025. Now the Spirit have another chance at lifting the trophy, with a little extra incentive to do so, as the NWSL Championship returns to Washington, D.C.
Traditionally, a neutral site is determined well before the NWSL Championship, and Audi Field was announced back in June.
The Kansas City Current are equally motivated to win the NWSL Championship after falling short in last year's playoffs. The club went on a record-setting regular-season run in 2025 and won the 2025 NWSL Shield but was eliminated in the quarterfinals. This year, they stormed through the postseason to reach the final game, looking for even more hardware.
Just a few days ago, some of the biggest stars were named to the NWSL's Best XI first team. Trinity Rodman and Croix Bethune were both honored on Wednesday night, and Bethune also took home her second Midfielder of the Year award. Rodman and the Spirit are looking for another NWSL Championship to add to their 2021 title, and Bethune -- who was traded from the Spirit in February -- is chasing history with the Current, who are still on the hunt for their first.
Here's everything you need to know about the big game:
Date:Saturday, Nov. 21| Time:8 p.m. ET
Location:Audi Field -- Washington, D.C.
Odds:Spirit +145 | Draw +215 | Current +160
The Washington Spirit's return to a third consecutive final came after a third-place finish in the regular season, in which the squad scored 43 goals and midseason arrivals quickly acclimated, proving a key difference. Now the club is back in the final for the fifth time in its history.
Head coach Adrian Gonzalez and his roster got off to a quick start in the playoffs and demolished the Portland Thorns 4-1 at home. Rodman scored twice, and new signings Melissa Bethi and Clara Luvanga also got on the scoresheet. The Spirit quickly followed that up with a 2-1 come-from-behind victory over the Utah Royals, with goals by Sofia Cantore and Luvanga after the group conceded the opening goal just two minutes into the semifinal.
The Spirit's attacking trio of Rodman, Cantore and Luvanga is gelling at the right moment and looking dangerous in the postseason, with all three forwards on the scoresheet in the playoffs.
"[The dynamic has] been great. Me and Soph have been able to build this connection a little bit longer, but it didn't take Clara very long. It's been amazing to see her grow and not only get comfortable but, like, get confident as well," Rodman said of the relationship with her teammates.
"I think playing at Audi [Field] obviously helps with that. But seeing her thrive, celebrate herself, has been really cool to see. But on top of that, the connection, I think, as a winger, you always want a center forward that you can work with and build off of and learn from. So it's been an amazing experience so far, and I'm hoping that we show that again on Saturday."
Kansas City's pursuit of another trophy
Under first-year head coach Chris Armas, the group got off to a rocky start to the season but quickly clawed its way to a fourth-place finish on the league table and co-led the league in goals scored (54) this season. The group has rallied around last year's short playoff appearance as a motivator, with several players saying this year is "personal" and citing the resilience they've shown.
During some stretches of the year, the roster had to navigate varying injuries or player absences due to international duty: Temwa Chawinga came back from an injury and then participated in Women's AFCON in August; Bethune recently returned from a hip injury; and Michelle Cooper managed a lingering leg knock.
"I'm feeling great. The vibes are good, which also helps. I think in some way, in some capacity, we're all tired. We played 30-plus games this year, but I think the vibes are so high that it doesn't even matter at this point. Like, we only have 90 minutes left in our season, so if we're crawling off that field, that's what we're gonna do," Cooper said.
"I'm glad everyone didn't come back healthy just in time for playoffs. Like we've had a couple months, two to three months, where all of us are healthy, which is nice. The level is constantly there. Even if something were to happen, we trust our bench. We trust the players that we have below us as well, and to be able to build the last two months and come into playoffs where everyone's kind of firing at the right time is exactly what we needed," she said.
The Spirit and the Current will compete in the NWSL Championship on Saturday at Audi Field. The winner will then compete for more silverware next summer in the 2027 NWSL Challenge Cup against the 2026 NWSL Shield holders, Gotham FC.

All the best angles of Haley Hopkins' stunning goal that saw KC Current reach NWSL final
There was a stunner in the NWSL semifinals, as the Kansas City Current upset regular season champions and defending title-winners Gotham FC on Sunday.
Gotham had won the 2025 championship as the eight seed, and then went on to top the regular season standings in the 2026 campaign, but injuries sapped their attacking unit and allowed Kansas City to take advantage.
The Current, who finished fourth in the regular season, won the match 2-1 on a thrilling 89th-minute winner from striker Haley Hopkins, whose set-piece goal sent the club through to the 2026 title match.
Hopkins' late goal was her 12th of the year, and put her club on the doorstep of a title for the first time since falling just short of the goal in 2022.
Watch Haley Hopkins' goal for KC Current vs. Gotham FC
With the game level at 1-1 in the 89th minute, Izzy Rodriguez lined up for a free-kick from a central location atop the penalty area.
The Kansas City full-back delivered a ball to the back post where Haley Hopkins latched onto it and delivered a stunning volley from a tight angle that seemed to catch everyone, including decorated Gotham goalkeeper Ann-Katrin Berger, off guard. She roofed it, in off the underside of the crossbar, sending the Current into dreamland.

With the victory, the Kansas City Current reached the 2026 NWSL Championship game on November 21 in Washington, D.C.
As luck would have it, they will face the hometown team, the Washington Spirit, and their superstar Trinity Rodman.
The event marks the first time the Current have reached the NWSL playoff final since they lost to the Portland Thorns in 2022.
The club has never won an NWSL title, and the city of Kansas City has not won an NWSL title since FC Kansas City's back-to-back championships in 2014 and 2015. Those two clubs are not the same, as FC Kansas City ceased operations in 2017 and its assets were transferred to expansion team Utah Royals. While Utah's player-related assets transferred back to the Kansas City Current when they joined the league three years later, the club's histories are not linked.

Kansas City Current’s Haley Hopkins scores the winning goal in the 89th minute against Gotham FC during Sunday’s NWSL semi-final at Icahn Stadium in New York.Photograph: Ira L Black/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenKansas City Current’s Haley Hopkins scores the winning goal in the 89th minute against Gotham FC during Sunday’s NWSL semi-final at Icahn Stadium in New York.Photograph: Ira L Black/Getty Images
Hopkins’ late stunner sends Kansas City past Gotham and into NWSL final
Hopkins’ 89th-minute volley seals dramatic 2-1 upset
Bethune scores stunning free kick against top seeds
Current to face Washington Spirit for first NWSL title
After a week dominated by aheadline-grabbing stadium imbroglio, Gotham FC and the Kansas City Current finally got down to the vital business of their NWSL semi-final on Sunday afternoon, a frigid encounter at an unlikely venue on New York City’s Randall’s Island with a place in next Saturday’s championship match at stake.
Clara Luvanga strikes as Washington Spirit beat Utah to reach third straight NWSL finalRead more
Haley Hopkins delivered the knockout blow at the death, hitting an 89th-minute volleyoff the crossbar and into seal a 2-1 upset that shattered Gotham FC’s bid for the league’s first-ever treble. Paired with Croix Bethune’s first-half free-kick stunner, the late winner sent fourth-seeded Kansas City past the NWSL Shield and in-season Challenge Cup winners into a championship showdown in six days against the Washington Spirit.
On a windswept afternoon where unyielding gusts undercut the warmth of a near-cloudless 50F sky, a physical opening stretch produced six fouls in the first eight minutes before either side threatened. Gotham recorded the first shot after 12 minutes when Jaedyn Shaw ran onto a Guro Reiten pass and missed wide right. Kansas City answered three minutes later, with Malawian star Temwa Chawinga firing wide left from the center of the area.
Twenty minutes in, Bethune won a free kick 25 yards out after a foul by Denise O’Sullivan. Stepping up with her left foot, she coolly curled her strike around the Gotham wall andinches inside the post. The goal from Bethune, the NWSL’s midfielder of the year two seasons ago with Washington, left the crowd in stunned silence before a smattering of boos echoed around the ground.
View image in fullscreenKansas City Current’s Haley Hopkins scores the winning goal in the 89th minute of Sunday’s NWSL semi-final against Gotham FC at Icahn Stadium.Photograph: Elsa/NWSL/Getty Images
The popular Rose Lavelle came on after half-time for O’Sullivan to deafening swells and made an immediate impact, winning a couple of free kicks and nearly finding the equalizer with a left-footed shot from the center of the area that missed wide left. But opportunities came fewer and further between over the next quarter-hour as the Current tightened their defensive shell.
Kansas City coach Chris Armas said his team had deliberately traded their customary high press for a more conservative mid-block designed to deny Gotham space. “We knew this game would be much more suited for the mid-block,” he said. The approach paid off: Gotham would finish the match without a shot on target.
With their repeat bid hanging in the balance, Gotham found an equalizer against the run of play in the 69th minute when Midge Purce whipped in a cross that ricocheted between goalkeeper Lorena and defender Gabrielle Robinson before caroming off Laney Rouse into her own net – leveling the match at one apiece despite the hosts still not having registered a single shot on target. It was hardly a match for the artistry of Bethune’s silky opener, but the delirious home crowd was in no mood to quibble.
The contest appeared bound for extra time past sundown with temperatures plunging. But Gotham, havingscraped through last week’s quarter-finalon another own goal, were suddenly within reach of a second straight NWSL final without having scored a goal of their own in either playoff match. Hopkins had other ideas, delivering the dramatic decider in the 89th minute before adding insult to injury by blowing kisses to the crowd from the touchline, provoking a cacophony of boos.
Armas later revealed that the winner came from a set-piece routine months in the making, with assistant coach Lucas Rodriguez spotting space at the back post and captain Lo’eau LaBonta calling the play. “Haley Hopkins gets the finish, and not an easy one on the left foot, but well executed,” he said.
View image in fullscreenGotham FC supporters hold a sign before Sunday’s NWSL semi-final against Kansas City Current at Icahn Stadium.Photograph: Ira L Black/Getty Images
With its solitary grandstand, roofline lettering and towering floodlights, 5,000-seat Icahn Stadium gave the appearance of an 1890s English football ground dropped beneath the Triborough Bridge – an improbable stage for one of the biggest matches of theNWSLseason.
Gotham had been forced to abandon their usual home at Sports Illustrated Stadium in Harrison, New Jersey, amid concerns over the deteriorating playing surface. The relocation capped a chaotic week for the league, which found itself juggling stadium availability, network television commitments and player safety at the most consequential stage of its season. Gotham’s regular ground, owned by MLS’s New York Red Bulls, had been booked for afriendly against Mexico’s Club Américaon Saturday, further complicating an already untenable situation.
Ultimately, the club prioritized a playable pitch over capacity. At one-fifth the size of their usual home, the municipal track venue where Usain Boltmade a creaky run-up to the Rio Olympicscreated an awkward compromise: world-class stars competing on a stage resembling a relic of football’s distant past. Sunday’s meeting also carried the unmistakable flavor of revenge. A year ago, Gotham entered the playoffs as the eighth seed andstunned the top-seeded Currentin the quarter-finals, ending Kansas City’s 18-match home win streak on a dramatic extra-time goal from Katie Lampson before going on to claimtheir second NWSL crown in three seasons.

Mỗi ngày công nhân vớt từ 5-7 xác heo ở kênh Bắc, Thanh Hóa
Trong những ngày qua, trên tuyến kênh Bắc đoạn qua đập Quy Xá, thôn Lạc Quy, xã Thiệu Trung, tỉnh Thanh Hóa xuất hiện nhiều xác heo chết và bao tải chứa rác thải sinh hoạt gây ô nhiễm môi trường.
Công nhân Công ty TNHH một thành viên Sông Chu chôn lấp, tiêu hủy xác heo và rác thải sau khi vớt trên kênh Bắc - Ảnh: HÀ ĐỒNG
Theo ghi nhận của phóng viên, số heo chết, rác thải sinh hoạt được người dân bỏ vào bao tải rồi ném xuống kênh Bắc. Nhiều xác heo đang trong quá trình phân hủy, bốc mùi hôi thối.
Gần 160 xác heo ném xuống kênh thủy lợi, Sở Nông nghiệp và Môi trường Thanh Hóa chỉ đạo xử lýĐỌC NGAY
Tình trạng người dân ném xác heo chết xuống kênh Bắc diễn ra từ đầu tháng 11 đến nay, trong khi bệnh dịch tả heo châu Phi đang diễn biến phức tạp, tiềm ẩn nguy cơ phát tán mầm bệnh.
Theo công nhân Công ty TNHH một thành viên Sông Chu - đơn vị quản lý hệ thống kênh Bắc, tình trạng người dân ném xác động vật, rác thải sinh hoạt có chiều hướng gia tăng, diễn biến phức tạp.
Trong hai tuần qua, trung bình mỗi ngày công nhân phải vớt từ 5 - 7 xác heo và nhiều bao tải chứa rác thải trên kênh Bắc.
Đặc biệt, từ ngày 18 đến 19-11, công nhân đã vớt 18 xác heo cùng nhiều rác thải sinh hoạt trên tuyến kênh này.
Công nhân Công ty TNHH một thành viên Sông Chu đưa xác heo vớt trên kênh Bắc đi chôn lấp, tiêu hủy - Ảnh: HÀ ĐỒNG
Việc người dân ném xác động vật, rác thải sinh hoạt ra môi trường, xuống kênh mương thủy lợi không chỉ gây ô nhiễm nguồn nước, ảnh hưởng đến đời sống, sản xuất của người dân mà còn tiềm ẩn nguy cơ phát sinh, lây lan dịch bệnh.
Đại diện Công ty TNHH một thành viên Sông Chu cho biết từ đầu năm đến tháng 10-2026, tình trạng người dân ném xác động vật, rác thải sinh hoạt xuống kênh Bắc có giảm so với năm 2025.
Tuy nhiên, từ đầu tháng 11 đến nay, tình trạng người dân ném xác động vật, rác thải xuống kênh mương thủy lợi do Công ty TNHH một thành viên Sông Chu quản lý lại tái diễn phức tạp, gây ô nhiễm môi trường.
Bên cạnh đó, số xác heo, rác thải sinh hoạt mà người dân ném xuống kênh mương thủy lợi đã và đang gây áp lực cho đơn vị quản lý, bởi phải huy động nhiều công nhân đi trục vớt, thu gom, tiêu hủy hằng ngày.
Công nhân Công ty TNHH một thành viên Sông Chu vớt rác trên kênh Bắc đoạn qua đập Quy Xá, thôn Lạc Quy, xã Thiệu Trung - Ảnh: HÀ ĐỒNG
Ông Ngô Văn Ngọc - Phó giám đốc phụ trách Chi nhánh thủy lợi Thiệu Hóa, thuộc Công ty TNHH một thành viên Sông Chu - cho biết: "Việc thu gom, tiêu hủy xác động vật, rác thải mà người dân ném xuống kênh thủy lợi chỉ là giải pháp khắc phục hậu quả trước mắt.
Để ngăn chặn tình trạng này, chính quyền địa phương cần nâng cao trách nhiệm quản lý địa bàn, tăng cường kiểm tra, giám sát tại khu vực thường xảy ra vi phạm. Chủ động phối hợp với đơn vị quản lý thủy lợi phát hiện, xác minh, xử lý nghiêm người vi phạm.
Hành vi cố tình ném xác động vật, rác thải sinh hoạt ra môi trường phải được xử lý theo quy định của pháp luật, bảo đảm tính nghiêm minh, răn đe, không để tái diễn vi phạm.

Nhân vật thầm lặng đứng sau các chuyến công du của Tổng thống Mỹ
(Dân trí) - Đứng đằng sau các chuyến công du của Tổng thống Mỹ Donald Trump là một trợ lý mà ông rất tin cậy với chức vụ Trưởng ban nghi lễ.
Bà Monica Crowley quan sát Tổng thống Donald Trump và Chủ tịch Tập Cận Bình bắt tay nhau hôm 18/11 (Ảnh: SCMP).
Khi Tổng Bí thư, Chủ tịch Trung Quốc Tập Cận Bình ra sân bay đón Tổng thống Mỹ Donald Trump tại Thâm Quyến hôm 18/11, máy quay đã ghi lại hình ảnh một phụ nữ mặc chiếc váy vàng đứng cách 2 nhà lãnh đạo vài bước chân.
Đó là bà Monica Crowley, Trưởng ban Nghi lễ thứ 35 của Mỹ.
Trong những hội nghị cấp cao có ý nghĩa đặc biệt quan trọng, bà đóng vai trò như một đạo diễn hậu trường thầm lặng, chịu trách nhiệm về công tác hậu cần ngoại giao và sắp xếp các nghi thức trong những chuyến công du nước ngoài của Tổng thống Mỹ.
Tối cùng ngày, bà xuất hiện tại Trung tâm Giao lưu Quốc tế Thâm Quyến, chỉ ít phút trước khi ông Trump bước xuống chiếc siêu xe để tham dự tiệc chiêu đãi chào mừng APEC do ông Tập và phu nhân chủ trì.
Nghi thức ngoại giao có vai trò quan trọng khi các nhân vật quyền lực hàng đầuthế giớigặp gỡ. Chúng chi phối mọi yếu tố, từ cấp độ đón tiếp, chiều dài thảm đỏ cho đến thực đơn tiệc tối.
Lễ đón tại sân bay hôm 19/11 của phía Trung Quốc đã được tính toán kỹ lưỡng nhằm đáp lại cử chỉ của ông Trump hồi tháng 9, khi Tổng thống Mỹ ra đón ông Tập tại Căn cứ liên hợp Andrews bên ngoài Washington.
Trong sự kiện này, bà Crowley cũng giữ vai trò tương đối quan trọng. Bà xuất hiện tại sân bay cùng ông Tập và phu nhân, trò chuyện ngắn với 2 người trước khi tiễn họ lên máy bay trở về Trung Quốc.
Trên cương vị này, bà tư vấn cho Tổng thống, Phó Tổng thống và Ngoại trưởng Mỹ về các vấn đề liên quan đến nghi thức ngoại giao trong nước và quốc tế.
Trong một cuộc phỏng vấn trước đây, bà Crowley từng giải thích rằng, công việc của bà “thực sự xoay quanh sự chính xác” và sự tỉ mỉ đến từng chi tiết. Bà nhắc lại một câu đùa lâu năm trong giới ngoại giao rằng khi các nghi thức được thực hiện một cách suôn sẻ, không ai nhận ra vai trò của người đứng sau, nhưng “khi có điều gì trục trặc, thì cả thế giới đều biết”.
Bà Crowley chụp cùng chuyên cơ Không lực Một (Ảnh: Instagram).
Trước khi bắt đầu chuyến công du châu Á với vai trò hỗ trợ cho ông Trump, bà Crowley đã chia sẻ những bức ảnh chụp cùng chuyên cơ Không Lực Một trên mạng xã hội. Bà đã đứng sau chuyến thăm của phái đoàn Mỹ tại Philippines để dự hội nghị cấp cao ASEAN.
Là một nhà bình luận lâu năm của đảng Cộng hòa, bà Crowley từng giữ chức Trợ lý Bộ trưởngTài chínhphụ trách các vấn đề công chúng trong giai đoạn 2019-2021, dưới thời chính quyền đầu tiên của ông Trump.
Trước đó, bà hoạt động trong lĩnh vực truyền thông, từng là cộng tác viên của Fox News và biên tập viên phụ trách bình luận của báo Washington Times.
Ông Trump công bố đề cử bà Crowley vào vị trí Trưởng ban Nghi lễ vào tháng 12/2024, đồng thời ca ngợi những đóng góp của bà trong chính quyền đầu tiên của ông. Bà chính thức tuyên thệ nhậm chức vào tháng 5/2025.

Tổng thống Mỹ Donald Trump ca ngợi mối quan hệ tuyệt vời với Chủ tịch Trung Quốc Tập Cận Bình khi hai nhà lãnh đạo gặp song phương bên lề hội nghị cấp cao APEC.

Nắm rõ được niềm yêu thích của Tổng thống Mỹ Donald Trump, Tổng thống Philippines Ferdinand Marcos Jr đã thết đãi "ông chủ" Nhà Trắng món gà rán nổi tiếng.

Công đoàn TP.HCM hỗ trợ công nhân Công ty ECCO mới giải thể 2 triệu đồng/người
Phan Diệp- phandiep32@gmail.com18/11/2026 21:01 GMT+7Chia sẻChọn BáoThanh Niênlàmnguồn ưu tiêntrên Google tìm kiếm.Xem hướng dẫn.BƯỚC1Nhấp vào nút"ThêmThanh Niêntrên Google"hoặc mở trực tiếp đường dẫn này:https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=thanhnien.vnBƯỚC2Tại trang vừa mở, tìm dòng"BáoThanh Niên"và bấm vào ô vuông bên phải.Khi ô vuông chuyển thành dấu tích xanh là bạn đã thành công rồi!LƯU Ý NHỎ:Nếu muốn kiểm tra xem cài đặt còn hiệu lực không, bạn chỉ cầnmở lại link trênlà thấy ngaydấu tích xanhvẫn đang hiển thị.Chúc bạn đọc báo vui vẻ!1.518 công nhân, người lao động làm việc tại Công ty ECCO vừa giải thể sẽ được Liên đoàn Lao động TP.HCM hỗ trợ từ 1-2 triệu đồng/người.
Liên đoàn Lao động TP.HCM vừa công bố quyết định hỗ trợ, chăm lo cho 1.518 đoàn viên, người lao động bị mất việc do Công ty TNHH ECCO Việt Nam (xã Bàu Bàng, TP.HCM) giải thể với tổng kinh phí là 2,88 tỉ đồng.
Kinh phí hỗ trợ, chăm lo trích từ nguồn tài chính Công đoàn thành phố. Cụ thể, với 1.362 đoàn viên, người lao động làm việc trực tiếp tạiCông ty TNHH ECCO Việt Nam, mức hỗ trợ là 2 triệu đồng/người. Tổng kinh phí là 2,724 tỉ đồng.
Còn với 156 người lao động của Công ty TNHH MTV cung ứng lao động Tâm Đức và Công ty TNHH cung ứng nhân lực Nhân Kiệt làm việc tại dự án ECCO, mức hỗ trợ là 1 triệu đồng/người. Tổng kinh phí 156 triệu đồng.
Công nhân Công ty ECCO nghe tư vấn việc làm từ các doanh nghiệp tại Khu công nghiệp Bàu Bàng, ngày 18.11
Liên đoàn Lao động TP.HCM giao bộ phận Chính sách pháp luật - Quan hệ lao động phối hợp bộ phận Tài chính, Công đoàn Khu công nghiệp số 5 và Công đoàn cơ sở Công ty TNHH ECCO Việt Nam khẩn trương tổ chức trao hỗ trợ kịp thời, đúng đối tượng, công khai, minh bạch, thực hiện thanh quyết toán theo quy định.
Đồng thời, phối hợp Trung tâm Dịch vụ việc làm TP.HCM và các đơn vị liên quan tư vấn, giới thiệu việc làm, hướng dẫn người lao động thực hiện các thủ tục hưởng chế độ bảo hiểm thất nghiệp, bảo hiểm xã hội theo quy định.
NhưThanh Niênđã đưa tin,Công ty ECCOthông báo giải thể ngày 2.11, chính thức dừng hoạt động ngày 30.11.
Ngay sau đó, Liên đoàn Lao động TP.HCM, Ban Quản lý các Khu chế xuất và công nghiệp TP.HCM cùng chính quyền địa phương đã làm việc với công ty, yêu cầu thực hiện đầy đủ cam kết quyền lợi của người lao động. Các đơn vị cũng phối hợp, kết nối nhiều doanh nghiệp có nhu cầutuyển dụng công nhâncủa ECCO.
Ít nhất 12 doanh nghiệp tuyển dụng công nhân do Công ty TNHH ECCO VN giải thể
Sáng 3.11, lãnh đạo Ban Quản lý các Khu chế xuất và công nghiệp TP.HCM cho biết có ít nhất 12 doanh nghiệp tham gia tuyển dụng toàn bộ số công nhân do Công ty TNHH ECCO VN ở Khu công nghiệp Bàu Bàng (xã Bàu Bàng, TP.HCM).

Mỗi ngày công nhân vớt từ 5-7 xác heo ở kênh Bắc, Thanh Hóa
Trong những ngày qua, trên tuyến kênh Bắc đoạn qua đập Quy Xá, thôn Lạc Quy, xã Thiệu Trung, tỉnh Thanh Hóa xuất hiện nhiều xác heo chết và bao tải chứa rác thải sinh hoạt gây ô nhiễm môi trường.
Công nhân Công ty TNHH một thành viên Sông Chu chôn lấp, tiêu hủy xác heo và rác thải sau khi vớt trên kênh Bắc - Ảnh: HÀ ĐỒNG
Theo ghi nhận của phóng viên, số heo chết, rác thải sinh hoạt được người dân bỏ vào bao tải rồi ném xuống kênh Bắc.
Nhiều xác heo đang trong quá trình phân hủy, bốc mùi hôi thối.
Gần 160 xác heo ném xuống kênh thủy lợi, Sở Nông nghiệp và Môi trường Thanh Hóa chỉ đạo xử lýĐỌC NGAY
Tình trạng người dân ném xác heo chết xuống kênh Bắc diễn ra từ đầu tháng 11 đến nay, trong khi bệnh dịch tả heo châu Phi đang diễn biến phức tạp, tiềm ẩn nguy cơ phát tán mầm bệnh.
Theo công nhân Công ty TNHH một thành viên Sông Chu - đơn vị quản lý hệ thống kênh Bắc, tình trạng người dân ném xác động vật, rác thải sinh hoạt có chiều hướng gia tăng, diễn biến phức tạp.
Trong hai tuần qua, trung bình mỗi ngày công nhân phải vớt từ 5 - 7 xác heo và nhiều bao tải chứa rác thải trên kênh Bắc.
Đặc biệt, từ ngày 18 đến 19-11, công nhân đã vớt 18 xác heo cùng nhiều rác thải sinh hoạt trên tuyến kênh này.
Công nhân Công ty TNHH một thành viên Sông Chu đưa xác heo vớt trên kênh Bắc đi chôn lấp, tiêu hủy - Ảnh: HÀ ĐỒNG

Việc người dân ném xác động vật, rác thải sinh hoạt ra môi trường, xuống kênh mương thủy lợi không chỉ gây ô nhiễm nguồn nước, ảnh hưởng đến đời sống, sản xuất của người dân mà còn tiềm ẩn nguy cơ phát sinh, lây lan dịch bệnh.
Đại diện Công ty TNHH một thành viên Sông Chu cho biết từ đầu năm đến tháng 10-2026, tình trạng người dân ném xác động vật, rác thải sinh hoạt xuống kênh Bắc có giảm so với năm 2025.

Tuy nhiên, từ đầu tháng 11 đến nay, tình trạng người dân ném xác động vật, rác thải xuống kênh mương thủy lợi do Công ty TNHH một thành viên Sông Chu quản lý lại tái diễn phức tạp, gây ô nhiễm môi trường.

Bên cạnh đó, số xác heo, rác thải sinh hoạt mà người dân ném xuống kênh mương thủy lợi đã và đang gây áp lực cho đơn vị quản lý, bởi phải huy động nhiều công nhân đi trục vớt, thu gom, tiêu hủy hằng ngày.
Công nhân Công ty TNHH một thành viên Sông Chu vớt rác trên kênh Bắc đoạn qua đập Quy Xá, thôn Lạc Quy, xã Thiệu Trung - Ảnh: HÀ ĐỒNG

Ông Ngô Văn Ngọc - Phó giám đốc phụ trách Chi nhánh thủy lợi Thiệu Hóa, thuộc Công ty TNHH một thành viên Sông Chu - cho biết: "Việc thu gom, tiêu hủy xác động vật, rác thải mà người dân ném xuống kênh thủy lợi chỉ là giải pháp khắc phục hậu quả trước mắt.
Để ngăn chặn tình trạng này, chính quyền địa phương cần nâng cao trách nhiệm quản lý địa bàn, tăng cường kiểm tra, giám sát tại khu vực thường xảy ra vi phạm.
Chủ động phối hợp với đơn vị quản lý thủy lợi phát hiện, xác minh, xử lý nghiêm người vi phạm.
Hành vi cố tình ném xác động vật, rác thải sinh hoạt ra môi trường phải được xử lý theo quy định của pháp luật, bảo đảm tính nghiêm minh, răn đe, không để tái diễn vi phạm.
Mỗi người dân cần nâng cao ý thức, thực hiện đúng quy định về thu gom, vận chuyển, tiêu hủy động vật chết và rác thải sinh hoạt".
Xác heo, rác thải đọng lại trên kênh Bắc đoạn qua đập Quy Xá, thôn Lạc Quy, xã Thiệu Trung, tỉnh Thanh Hóa - Ảnh: HÀ ĐỒNG
Hàng chục xác heo trên kênh cấp nước, cơ quan chức năng vào cuộc

Hơn một tuần qua, cơ quan chức năng tỉnh Thanh Hóa đã vớt, tiêu hủy hàng chục xác heo chết được thả trôi trên nhiều tuyến kênh cung cấp nước sinh hoạt và sản xuất cho 11 phường, xã trên địa bàn tỉnh này.

lead_title: GTA 6 breaks records as sales top $2bn - industry estimate

evidence_pages.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c9zr:
GTA 6 breaks records as sales top $2bn - industry estimate - BBC News
Image source,Rockstar GamesImage caption,
GTA 6 central characters Lucia and Jason
Grand Theft Auto 6 is estimated to have become the biggest entertainment release in history following the blockbuster video game's launch on Thursday, after a 13-year wait.
The highly anticipated open-world action-adventure has sold more than 24.5 million units as of Thursday, raking in about $2.36bn (£1.8bn), according to analytics platform Sensor Tower.
In comparison, this year's highest grossing movie so far, Spider-Man: Brand New Day, made$2.5bn over its entire run in cinemas.
GTA 6's maker Rockstar and parent company Take-Two have not released details of the game's sales but said demand has been "unprecedented". The BBC has contacted both the firms for comment.
GTA 6 is the latest instalment in Rockstar's nearly three decade old crime simulator franchise, which has become one of the most popular games in history.
At its core, the series is a satirical take on the American dream, putting players in the shoes of career criminals in Leonida, the game's Florida-inspired state.
The latest game follows new characters Lucia and her partner Jason, a pair of small-time criminals.
Grand Theft Auto 6 is a masterpiece, say critics
Sensor Tower said GTA 6 will be so popular that it will reduce the time gamers spend on other single-player titles by 10%.
The research firm said its estimates are based on email receipts data and other statistical sources that track millions of people daily. They also track public profiles across major gaming platforms like PlayStation and Xbox, where GTA 6 is available.
Anticipation for the blockbuster title has grown through repeated delays, following a 13-year wait.
GTA 6 has been hailed by some reviewers as one of the most impressive gaming experiences ever. Entertainment media site IGN described it as an "uncompromisingly engineered" masterpiece.
The release of GTA 6 at midnight on Thursday across various time zones saw many gamers stay up through the night, while some took the following day off to play the game.

François Picard is pleased to welcome Olivier Mauco, President of the European Video Game Observatory and Lecturer at Paris Dauphine University. For Spotlight, he discusses the extraordinary anticipation surrounding "GTA VI", the game's enduring popularity and the economics of blockbuster video game production. "It's kind of the masterpiece of the game industry," says Mauco of Grand Theft Auto, whose next instalment has generated considerable anticipation following a 13-year hiatus.
"GTA is the king of what we call the open world," explains Mauco. And that explains the game's appeal and unique endurance. The gaming community has continued playing "GTA V", keeping it alive and kicking for more than a decade.
Mauco also offers the backstory on introducing of a female protagonist and the possibility of playing a couple. But despite Grand Theft Auto's wild popularity, he does question the economics of increasingly expensive video games. "The recipe to make a blockbuster is not so efficient today," he observes, although he expects "GTA VI" to generate exceptionally high sales.
