fact_units.text: VinFast ra mắt hai mẫu xe máy điện cao cấp Sadie và Rasad | Báo Dân trí
VinFast ra mắt hai mẫu xe máy điện cao cấp Sadie và Rasad
(Dân trí) - Ngày 19/11, VinFast công bố bổ sung thêm vào danh mục sản phẩm hai mẫu xe máy điện cao cấp Sadie và Rasad, với giá niêm yết lần lượt là 59,9 và 78,9 triệu đồng (đã bao gồm VAT).
Sadie và Rasad minh chứng cho năng lực nghiên cứu, phát triển sản phẩm cao cấp của VinFast, góp phần định vị xe máy điện ở những phân khúc cao cấp nhất của thị trường xe hai bánh.

Sadie và Rasad là hai mẫu xe mở đầu cho phân khúc xe máy điện cao cấp được VinFast định hướng phát triển từ đầu năm, tập trung vào các yếu tố công nghệ, thiết kế và trải nghiệm sử dụng, hướng đến nhóm khách hàng có yêu cầu cao về thẩm mỹ và tính năng sản phẩm.

Mỗi mẫu xe được thiết kế theo một phong cách riêng như một tuyên ngôn nghệ thuật của chủ sở hữu, đồng thời được trang bị những công nghệ tối tân giúp định hình chủ xe như những người tiên phong, đón đầu xu hướng.
Sadie sở hữu nét đẹp tân cổ điển (Ảnh: VinFast).

Trong đó, Sadie sở hữu nét đẹp tân cổ điển với nhiều đường cong mềm mại, liền mạch từ phần mặt nạ trước kéo dài tới đuôi xe, phù hợp với nhóm người dùng đề cao phong cách sống thanh lịch và sành điệu.
Xe được trang bị màn hình TFT 5 inch (Ảnh: VinFast).

Điểm nhấn mang tính nhận diện trong thiết kế của Sadie là cụm đèn pha LED Projector hình kim cương, ôm trọn trong viền mạ chrome sáng bóng ở phía trước, bên dưới là dải ốp chạy dọc mặt nạ làm nổi bật logo hình chữ V đặc trưng của VinFast.
Ở phía sau, dải đèn hậu LED vắt ngang tạo dấu ấn hiện đại cho phần đuôi xe.
Với kích thước dài x rộng x cao lần lượt là 2.030 x 729 x 1.152 mm và trọng lượng 140 kg, Sadie có dáng vẻ thanh thoát, gọn gàng, dễ dàng xoay trở trên phố.
Cốp dung tích 30 lít, đủ chỗ cho mũ bảo hiểm, túi xách, ba lô (Ảnh: VinFast).

Thiết kế của Sadie được chăm chút tỉ mỉ với các chi tiết thể hiện sự tinh tế, chỉn chu như: đường nẹp chrome mảnh chạy dọc yếm và sàn xe, tay dắt sau được mạ sơn sáng, dòng chữ tên xe được viết tay cách điệu...
Xe được trang bị bộ vành đúc đa chấu màu bạc, màn hình TFT 5 inch và cốp dung tích 30 lít, đủ chỗ cho mũ bảo hiểm, túi xách, ba lô cùng các vật dụng cá nhân thiết yếu.
Sadie có 6 lựa chọn màu sắc là đen bóng, xám xi măng, xanh cẩm thạch, trắng sữa, đỏ tươi và nâu titanium.
Trong khi đó, Rasad là mẫu maxi-scooter chạy điện được thiết kế theo một phong cách hoàn toàn khác, phù hợp với những khách hàng đề cao sự mạnh mẽ, lịch lãm và hiện đại.
Rasad là mẫu maxi-scooter đề cao sự mạnh mẽ (Ảnh: VInFast).
Thân xe vạm vỡ với các khối cơ bắp và các mảng cắt xẻ dứt khoát.
Phần đầu xe gây ấn tượng với cụm đèn pha LED đôi sắc sảo, hai dải LED định vị ôm logo chữ V, kết hợp cùng kính chắn gió mang đến dáng vẻ mạnh mẽ và nam tính.
Phần đuôi xe được thiết kế vuốt cao, kết thúc bằng cụm đèn hậu LED góc cạnh giúp tạo nên tổng thể cân đối, hài hòa và khỏe khoắn.
Với kích thước 2.036 x 750 x 1.220 mm, trọng lượng 155 kg và chiều cao yên 765 mm, Rasad vừa sở hữu dáng vẻ bề thế, vừa có không gian ngồi thoải mái, chống chân dễ dàng khi vận hành.
Bộ lốp bản rộng 110/80-14 phía trước và 130/70-13 phía sau giúp tăng độ đầm chắc, trong khi cặp phuộc sau được trang bị bình dầu phụ giúp duy trì hiệu suất giảm chấn ổn định cho xe.
Xe sở hữu màn hình TFT cỡ lớn 7 inch (Ảnh: VinFast).
Rasad được trang bị tay lái trần thể thao, yên xe hai tầng phối hai tông màu và tay dắt sau kim loại nhôm giúp hoàn thiện diện mạo thể thao và đẳng cấp.
Xe sở hữu màn hình TFT cỡ lớn 7 inch, cốp rộng tới 45 lít và 4 lựa chọn màu sắc là đen bóng, xanh cẩm thạch, trắng sữa và nâu titanium.

Về tính năng vận hành, cả hai mẫu xe cao cấp mới của VinFast đều được trang bị động cơ đặt giữa (center motor) có công suất danh định 3.500W, công suất tối đa 7.500W, cho tốc độ tối đa 100 km/h, đáp ứng cả nhu cầu di chuyển trong đô thị lẫn những hành trình dài.

Xe có khả năng tăng tốc từ 0 lên 50 km/h trong chưa đầy 6 giây, 3 chế độ lái Eco - Normal - Sport, kết hợp phanh tái sinh 4 mức giúp thu hồi năng lượng, nạp lại điện cho pin mỗi khi nhả ga hoặc phanh giảm tốc, qua đó giúp kéo dài quãng đường di chuyển.
Xe có tính năng khởi hành ngang dốc (Ảnh: VinFast).
Xe còn có tính năng hỗ trợ khởi hành ngang dốc, hạn chế trôi ngược khi bắt đầu di chuyển trên dốc, cùng số lùi kèm đèn cảnh báo nguy hiểm (hazard) để đảm bảo an toàn.
VinFast Sadie và Rasad sử dụng 2 pin LFP dung lượng 2,3 kWh hoạt động song song, cho quãng đường di chuyển lên tới 160 km sau mỗi lần sạc đầy (theo điều kiện kiểm thử của VinFast).
Cổng sạc được bố trí ngoài thân xe, có nắp đậy kín, cho phép cắm sạc trực tiếp mà không cần mở cốp.
Động cơ đạt chuẩn chống nước IP67, pin đạt chuẩn IP68, đảm bảo cho xe vận hành bền bỉ trong các điều kiện thời tiết khắc nghiệt.
Cả hai mẫu xe đều được trang bị hệ thống chống bó cứng phanh ABS 2 kênh, giúp giữ ổn định khi phanh gấp hoặc phanh trên đường trơn.

Nhằm mang đến cho người dùng trải nghiệm công nghệ hiện đại, Sadie và Rasad được trang bị nhiều tính năng thông minh và tiện nghi như: hỗ trợ kết nối Bluetooth với điện thoại, cho phép hiển thị bản đồ dẫn đường Google Maps, báo cuộc gọi đến, cuộc gọi nhỡ ngay trên màn hình TFT của xe; chìa khóa thông minh; cổng sạc USB Type-C và USB Type-A tích hợp trên yếm trước…
Cốp xe rộng tới 45 lít (Ảnh: VinFast).

Người dùng cũng có thể quản lý xe toàn diện từ xa thông qua ứng dụng VinFast e-Scooter trên điện thoại, với các chức năng như: định vị và tìm xe từ xa; theo dõi tình trạng pin; xem lịch sử hành trình; thống kê quãng đường đã đi; thiết lập vùng an toàn để nhận cảnh báo khi xe di chuyển ra ngoài khu vực đã cài đặt; chẩn đoán lỗi…

VinFast Sadie có mức giá niêm yết 59,9 triệu đồng, trong khi VinFast Rasad có giá niêm yết 78,9 triệu đồng (đã bao gồm VAT), được ưu đãi 8 triệu đồng theo chương trình “Vì tương lai xanh” đến hết ngày 19/12.
Cả hai đều được bảo hành 6 năm cho xe, 8 năm cho pin không giới hạn số km, dự kiến sẽ có mặt tại hệ thống đại lý phân phối VinFast trên toàn quốc ngay trong tháng 11.

Với việc bổ sung thêm hai mẫu xe thuộc phân khúc cao cấp, VinFast đang cung cấp dải sản phẩm xe máy điện phong phú bậc nhất thị trường, trải rộng ở tất cả phân khúc giá từ 12 đến 78,9 triệu đồng, khẳng định vị thế thương hiệu trên thị trường.

Đậu Tiến Đạt19/11/2026 22:27 GMT+7Chia sẻChọn BáoThanh Niênlàmnguồn ưu tiêntrên Google tìm kiếm.Xem hướng dẫn.BƯỚC1Nhấp vào nút"ThêmThanh Niêntrên Google"hoặc mở trực tiếp đường dẫn này:https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=thanhnien.vnBƯỚC2Tại trang vừa mở, tìm dòng"BáoThanh Niên"và bấm vào ô vuông bên phải.Khi ô vuông chuyển thành dấu tích xanh là bạn đã thành công rồi!LƯU Ý NHỎ:Nếu muốn kiểm tra xem cài đặt còn hiệu lực không, bạn chỉ cầnmở lại link trênlà thấy ngaydấu tích xanhvẫn đang hiển thị.Chúc bạn đọc báo vui vẻ!
Tối 19.11, Tổng thống Azerbaijan Ilham Aliyev và phu nhân đến Hà Nội, bắt đầu thăm chính thức Việt Nam từ ngày 19 - 21.11 theo lời mời của Tổng Bí thư, Chủ tịch nước Tô Lâm và phu nhân.
Đây là chuyến thăm chính thức Việt Nam lần thứ hai của Tổng thốngAzerbaijanIlham Aliyev kể từ sau chuyến thăm lần đầu tiên vào năm 2014. Chuyến thăm góp phần đưa quan hệ Việt Nam - Azerbaijan bước sang giai đoạn phát triển mới, tương xứng với tầm vóc của khuôn khổ Đối tác chiến lược.
Bộ trưởng Bộ Tư pháp Hoàng Thanh Tùng đón Tổng thống Azerbaijan Ilham Aliyev và phu nhân tại sân bay quốc tế Nội Bài, Hà Nội
Ra sân bay quốc tế Nội Bài đón đoàn có: Bộ trưởng Bộ Tư pháp Hoàng Thanh Tùng; Thứ trưởng Bộ Ngoại giao Lê Thị Thu Hằng; Đại sứ Việt Nam tại Liên bang Nga kiêm nhiệm Azerbaijan Đặng Minh Khôi.
Tháp tùng Tổng thống Azerbaijan Ilham Aliyev thăm chính thức Việt Nam có: bà Mehriban Aliyeva, phu nhân Tổng thống; Chánh văn phòng Tổng thống Samir Nuriyev; Bộ trưởng Bộ Ngoại giao Jeyhun Bayramov; Bộ trưởng Bộ Quốc phòng Zakir Hasanov; Trợ lý Tổng thống Hikmat Hajiyev; Bộ trưởng Bộ Năng lượng Parviz Shahbazov; Bộ trưởng Bộ Tình trạng khẩn cấp Kamaladdin Heydarov; Bộ trưởng Bộ Kinh tế Mikayil Jabbarov; Đại sứ đặc mệnh toàn quyền Azerbaijan tại Việt Nam Shovgi Mehdizade.
Việt Nam và Azerbaijan có mối quan hệ hữu nghị truyền thống lâu đời, được xây dựng và vun đắp qua nhiều thế hệ lãnh đạo và nhân dân hai nước. Trong suốt chặng đường phát triển, Azerbaijan luôn dành cho Việt Nam sự ủng hộ và tình cảm chân thành; Việt Nam cũng luôn coi trọng quan hệ hữu nghị và hợp tác với Azerbaijan.
Đặc biệt, chuyến thăm cấp nhà nước của Tổng Bí thư Tô Lâm tới Azerbaijan tháng 5.2025 và việc hai nước chính thức nâng cấp quan hệ lên Đối tác chiến lược đã mở ra một chương mới trong quan hệ song phương. Từ đó đến nay, tình hình hợp tác trên các lĩnh vực đã có những bước phát triển rõ rệt.
Trong bối cảnh đó, chuyến thăm của Tổng thống Ilham Aliyev tới Việt Nam có ý nghĩa đặc biệt quan trọng. Đây là dịp để lãnh đạo cấp cao hai nước tiếp tục củng cố tin cậy chính trị, trao đổi toàn diện về các định hướng phát triển quan hệ, đồng thời xác định những biện pháp cụ thể nhằm triển khai hiệu quả khuôn khổ Đối tác chiến lược; tạo xung lực mới, góp phần tăng cường hợp tác trên tất cả các lĩnh vực, từ chính trị, ngoại giao, kinh tế, thương mại, đầu tư đến năng lượng, giáo dục, khoa học, công nghệ và giao lưu nhân dân.
Đưa quan hệ song phương VN - Azerbaijan lên tầm cao mới
Ngày 8.5, trong khuôn khổ chuyến thăm cấp Nhà nước đến Cộng hòa Azerbaijan, Tổng Bí thư Tô Lâm đã có cuộc hội kiến Thủ tướng Azerbaijan Ali Asadov.Chia sẻChọn BáoThanh Niênlàmnguồn ưu tiêntrên Google tìm kiếm.Xem hướng dẫn.

Tổng thống Azerbaijan Ilham Aliyev bắt đầu thăm chính thức Việt Nam

Đậu Tiến Đạt19/11/2026 22:27 GMT+7Chia sẻChọn BáoThanh Niênlàmnguồn ưu tiêntrên Google tìm kiếm.Xem hướng dẫn.BƯỚC1Nhấp vào nút"ThêmThanh Niêntrên Google"hoặc mở trực tiếp đường dẫn này:https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=thanhnien.vnBƯỚC2Tại trang vừa mở, tìm dòng"BáoThanh Niên"và bấm vào ô vuông bên phải.Khi ô vuông chuyển thành dấu tích xanh là bạn đã thành công rồi!LƯU Ý NHỎ:Nếu muốn kiểm tra xem cài đặt còn hiệu lực không, bạn chỉ cầnmở lại link trênlà thấy ngaydấu tích xanhvẫn đang hiển thị.Chúc bạn đọc báo vui vẻ!
Tối 19.11, Tổng thống Azerbaijan Ilham Aliyev và phu nhân đến Hà Nội, bắt đầu thăm chính thức Việt Nam từ ngày 19 - 21.11 theo lời mời của Tổng Bí thư, Chủ tịch nước Tô Lâm và phu nhân.
Đây là chuyến thăm chính thức Việt Nam lần thứ hai của Tổng thốngAzerbaijanIlham Aliyev kể từ sau chuyến thăm lần đầu tiên vào năm 2014.
Chuyến thăm góp phần đưa quan hệ Việt Nam - Azerbaijan bước sang giai đoạn phát triển mới, tương xứng với tầm vóc của khuôn khổ Đối tác chiến lược.
Bộ trưởng Bộ Tư pháp Hoàng Thanh Tùng đón Tổng thống Azerbaijan Ilham Aliyev và phu nhân tại sân bay quốc tế Nội Bài, Hà Nội
Ra sân bay quốc tế Nội Bài đón đoàn có: Bộ trưởng Bộ Tư pháp Hoàng Thanh Tùng; Thứ trưởng Bộ Ngoại giao Lê Thị Thu Hằng; Đại sứ Việt Nam tại Liên bang Nga kiêm nhiệm Azerbaijan Đặng Minh Khôi.

Tháp tùng Tổng thống Azerbaijan Ilham Aliyev thăm chính thức Việt Nam có: bà Mehriban Aliyeva, phu nhân Tổng thống; Chánh văn phòng Tổng thống Samir Nuriyev; Bộ trưởng Bộ Ngoại giao Jeyhun Bayramov; Bộ trưởng Bộ Quốc phòng Zakir Hasanov; Trợ lý Tổng thống Hikmat Hajiyev; Bộ trưởng Bộ Năng lượng Parviz Shahbazov; Bộ trưởng Bộ Tình trạng khẩn cấp Kamaladdin Heydarov; Bộ trưởng Bộ Kinh tế Mikayil Jabbarov; Đại sứ đặc mệnh toàn quyền Azerbaijan tại Việt Nam Shovgi Mehdizade.
Việt Nam và Azerbaijan có mối quan hệ hữu nghị truyền thống lâu đời, được xây dựng và vun đắp qua nhiều thế hệ lãnh đạo và nhân dân hai nước.
Trong suốt chặng đường phát triển, Azerbaijan luôn dành cho Việt Nam sự ủng hộ và tình cảm chân thành; Việt Nam cũng luôn coi trọng quan hệ hữu nghị và hợp tác với Azerbaijan.

Đặc biệt, chuyến thăm cấp nhà nước của Tổng Bí thư Tô Lâm tới Azerbaijan tháng 5.2025 và việc hai nước chính thức nâng cấp quan hệ lên Đối tác chiến lược đã mở ra một chương mới trong quan hệ song phương.
Từ đó đến nay, tình hình hợp tác trên các lĩnh vực đã có những bước phát triển rõ rệt.
Trong bối cảnh đó, chuyến thăm của Tổng thống Ilham Aliyev tới Việt Nam có ý nghĩa đặc biệt quan trọng.

Đây là dịp để lãnh đạo cấp cao hai nước tiếp tục củng cố tin cậy chính trị, trao đổi toàn diện về các định hướng phát triển quan hệ, đồng thời xác định những biện pháp cụ thể nhằm triển khai hiệu quả khuôn khổ Đối tác chiến lược; tạo xung lực mới, góp phần tăng cường hợp tác trên tất cả các lĩnh vực, từ chính trị, ngoại giao, kinh tế, thương mại, đầu tư đến năng lượng, giáo dục, khoa học, công nghệ và giao lưu nhân dân.

lead_title: Anthropic’s Record-Breaking IPO Highlights the AI Giant’s Worst Enemy—Itself

evidence_pages.https://www.wired.com/story/anthropics-r:
Anthropic’s Record-Breaking IPO Highlights the AI Giant’s Worst Enemy—Itself | WIREDSkip to main content
After closing thelargest initial public offering in history on Wednesday,Anthropichas about $200 billion in the bank, more than every tech giant besides Alphabet. But the AI lab has also committed to paying vendors more than $900 billion over the next 19 years, mostly to developdata centerspoweringClaudeand its other AI models.
Some financial analysts say that gap doesn’t look concerning when you factor in that the company’s most recent quarterly sales were $17 billion, up more than 1,100 percent from the year before. Whether investors agree will become apparent on midday Thursday when Anthropic shares begin trading on the Nasdaq stock exchange under the ticker symbol ANT.
The case for pessimism over the long term rests on issues that may slow Anthropic’s progress in developing new tools. This month,US voters largely rejected data centerswhen given the chance, andprotests against new projectsshow no signs of slowing. Delays in the launch or expansion of new facilities could leave Anthropic struggling to train more powerful AI models.
“The jury’s still out on whetherartificial intelligenceis going to benefit everyone, or just a few people,” says Elaine Matheny, one of 70 members of Mason County United, a grassroots organization fighting an under-construction data center intended for Anthropic in West Virginia. “Do we really need to cover up all our farmland so Claude can do all our thinking for us?”
Then there are the concerns about the safety and security of Anthropic’s models. At a livestreamed investor meeting last week, Anthropic CEODario Amodeisaid developing safeguards was the limiting factor in deploying its AI models. “We don’t want these agents to run wild,” he said. It’s possible the company could prioritize safety to a point that stunts growth.
The San Francisco-based developer is organized as a public benefit corporation, a legal designation that allows it to prioritize societal impacts alongside shareholder interests. Amodeihas saidthe company held back a new model earlier this year, jeopardizing sales to protect the public from potentially harmful technology. He also has said the company tries to screen for hires “oriented toward the public benefit” to ingrain the safety culture among its 5,300 employees, which is “painful in the short run” as the company passes over otherwise qualified candidates.
Anthropic’s market debut is the largest for a so-called PBC, and the first for a company solely focused on generative AI development. It also represents a triumph for the handful ofrenegade engineers and business leaderswho started it. They siphoned themselves off fromOpenAIin the midst of the pandemic nearly six years ago over strategic differences, and the two companies have beenrivals ever since.
For some time, OpenAI was expected to go public first, butexecutive departures,shifting priorities, andlegal troubleshave introduced roadblocks.
Anthropic also has some compelling numbers to show investors. Revenue issoaring, while operating losses aredeclining.Its big spatwith the US Department of Defense this year over limits on Claude use doesn’t appear to have significantly slowed growth. Overall, the number of customers spending six figures annually is up 12 times compared to a year ago. “I don’t think you could have dreamt of an [IPO prospectus] that’s as good,” says Tomasz Tunguz, general partner at the investment firm Theory Ventures.
Because of how Anthropic must account for compensating employees with stock, it’s still wildly unprofitable—over $104 billion in losses this year through September. That’s no matter when investors are eager to buy shares and lend money.
The IPO raised about $81 billion (more than $107 billion when adding in private sales of shares), which is more thanthe $75 billion SpaceX receivedin June in a previous world record. Anthropic’s initial valuation of roughly $1.5 trillion fell short of SpaceX’s nearly $1.8 trillion, though the Elon Musk-led rocket maker does have a more sprawling business beyond AI. (OpenAI has been valued at $1.25 trillion in an ongoing fundraising campaign.)
Anthropic reportedly sought, but failed, to achieve a higher valuation, suggesting some anxiety on Wall Street. US midterm electionresultshave increased the possibility of new regulations on emerging technologies. Fears about the debt enabling AI data center development are rising, and a potential pullback in investment from Nvidia after CEO Jensen Huang’s sudden exitare deepening those worries.

It was during November 2020 that somewhere in San Francisco, a woman called Daniela Amodei phoned a friend, asking for advice.
Daniela oversaw safety and policy at OpenAI, one of the most talked-about AI companies in the world.
But Daniela and her brother Dario - who worked there too - had misgivings over safety levels at OpenAI and thought it could be time to walk away.
So she did what many do when we can't make a decision about something, she phoned a friend. The friend's reply was direct and to the point: "You don't need to be on the phone with me. You already know the answer."
The Amodei siblings and a handful of other colleagues quit. Together, they set up a rival – Anthropic.
Six years on and Anthropic, the maker of leading AI model Claude, has predicted revenues of $52bn in 2026 and $135bn in 2027, according to analyst estimates.
It is about to sell shares to the public for the first time in what's known as an Initial Public Offering or IPO, aiming for a valuation of an estimated $1.4tn (£1tn), which would propel it straight into the top 10 of the most valuable US companies.
The sale comes at a crucial time when many are wondering whether, amid increasing concern about the potential of AI, the industry's bubble is showing signs of bursting.
Where once investors were "all in" on a technological revolution to rival the railroads, the car, electricity and the internet, some are now hedging their bets, amid arguments that AI prices will be driven down as the technology becomes more common and concerns that a hefty wedge of the AI investment is tech giants investing in each other.
Shares in companies that supply the raw computing power behind AI, like Coreweave and Nebius, have seen their value cut in half while even the mighty Nvidia has lost its crown as the world's most valuable company with its shares down 30% - a staggering $2tn fall in value.
So could the Anthropic IPO reinflate the bubble or will it be remembered as the last gasp of a boom that is heading for a bust?
At an event last week, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei told JPMorgan Chase's CEO Jamie Dimon that his guiding principle was to "never let your company be worth a single dollar more than it's worth".
The company is selling roughly $81bn worth of shares to the general public and a further $26bn on to other big tech companies. It is comfortably the single biggest money raising event in US corporate history.
It's an old adage that during a gold rush you should buy companies that sell the picks and shovels as opposed to those staking everything on striking gold. In AI's case that's the chip makers, the data centre builders, the energy providers. But Anthropic is arguably the gold itself and this IPO will see what value people put on it, according to Fiona Cincotta.
"I think the reason that this IPO is so important is basically it's the first ability for the public investors to access a pure play AI trade," she says, adding that previous offerings have been about "other parts of the ecosystem, which are, the semiconductors, the chips, the, data centres. But this is the first time that we were actually able to access the AI provider."

Daniela Amodei helped set up a rival company to OpenAI
What a company is worth depends almost entirely on predicted future earnings.
It's that calculation that many think presents the sharpest needle to the AI bubble.
Will current and future users of AI be prepared to pay enough to justify the trillions being spent on the chips, data centres, energy and employees, some of whom can command annual salaries of over $100m?
"AI is certainly in a financial bubble. While LLMs [large language models] offer genuine utility and are undoubtedly here to stay, the economics don't add up," said Gary Marcus, Professor Emeritus at New York University and author of Taming Silicon Valley, speaking earlier this year.
"[The] more companies build AI models, the [more the] technology becomes commoditised, eliminating meaningful competitive advantages and driving down prices."
So far, the growth rates in Anthropic revenue are extraordinary.
But these explosive growth rates hide a potential problem. Around a quarter of that revenue came from just a handful of companies, among them Google and Amazon.
It's also concentrated in the US which accounts for two-thirds of its revenue.
There is also the staggering network of circular financing found in the AI world. For example, Anthropic has agreements to buy or lease hundreds of billions of dollars worth of chips and computing power from a handful of companies including Broadcom, Google, Amazon. Many of those firms are also investors in Anthropic and major customers of its products.
It's not just some Wall Street investors questioning whether the AI boom is all it's cracked up to be. Out on Main Street, ordinary Americans have concerns too.
With the US driving so much of global AI growth, a growing public backlash against a technology that threatens to replace millions of jobs and hoover up vast amounts of energy and water became a factor in the recent midterm elections in the US.
Many areas in the US have passed moratoriums on data centre development and many candidates deemed too close to big tech found that association a political liability rather than an asset. Many Democrat candidates publicly opposed data centre development and won.
Added to that, the Pied Piper of AI, chip maker Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang, resigned last week after admitting to having been "unfaithful" to his wife after reports he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, Alice Huang and another with a company executive who reported to him.
Dario Amodei is one of Silicon Valley's big beasts
Huang's spectacular fall from grace and Nvidia's 30% fall in value from its peak have left AI investors looking for a new champion for the AI boom that has underpinned the US stock market and arguably much of its entire economy for the last two years.
If Anthropic – and its CEO are to be AI's new Pied Piper, he will be playing a different tune to the relentlessly upbeat, leather jacket-clad talisman Huang.
While Huang wanted AI development to continue full throttle, Anthropic was built on misgivings over the levels of safety and responsibility the OpenAI leavers felt were being exercised over the development of society-changing technology.

Anthropic shares are about to make their market debut after the company raised more than $100 billion in a record-breaking initial public offering that valued it at around $1.5 trillion.
It's a remarkably rapid ascent for the five-year-old artificial intelligence powerhouse, and a sign of strong investor appetite despite growing concern about a possible AI bubble.
Can Anthropic make enough money to justify its value?
Anthropic sold 956 million shares — far more than originally planned — at an IPO price of $83 per share, it announced on Wednesday. That price exceeded its targeted range of $70 to $78 per share.
The company's seven founders also sold more than 23 million shares as part of the IPO. On top of that, Anthropic's prospectus included plans to put an additional $26 billion worth of shares into the market through private placements with companies including Google, Microsoft and Nvidia.
The total haul is more than $107 billion.

Anthropic valuation could rise or fall later on Thursday, when its shares start trading publicly on the Nasdaq exchange under the ticker symbol ANT.
The amount of money raised makes Anthropic's IPO the biggest in history, after Elon Musk's mega-conglomerate SpaceXlanded$75 billion when it listed in June.
"We've never seen a company that's able to grow this fast [and] be this dominant," said Andrew Rocco, a stock analyst at the financial research firm Zacks.
Anthropic got its start in 2021 as a breakaway group of researchers who once worked for ChatGPT-maker OpenAI. Led by now-CEO Dario Amodei, the Anthropic founders were concerned that OpenAI, run by Sam Altman, was not on a path to develop AI safely.

Amodei and the others quickly raised hundreds of millions of dollars and set out to develop AI models in a way that the company said focused on safety and "alignment," or the idea that AI should be harmless and act in ways that jibe with human values and intent.
Anthropic launched Claude in early 2023, just months after OpenAI released ChatGPT. Ever since, the two companies have been neck-and-neck competitors in cutting-edge artificial intelligence, known as "frontier AI." The Claude family of AI models, including the Claude chatbot and Claude Code, are among the most popular and powerful in the world, and have helped transform everything from online search to software engineering.
They are also the San Francisco-based company's main source of income, according to its IPO prospectus, which said revenue in the first half of the year skyrocketed 1,300% at $16.3 billion, while its adjusted operating income — a measure of potential profitability — hit $1.6 billion during the period, versus a loss of $1.8 billion the year before.
The IPO comes at a time when shares in tech companies linked to the AI boom have been volatile. Investors have vacillated between enthusiasm for what many believe will be a revolutionary technology and concern that the vast sums of money being poured into it may be hard to justify.
"It's going to be a test of investor sentiment towards the AI trade," said Janice Quek, an equity analyst at the investment research firm CFRA. "We've seen in recent weeks that there has been a lot of pressure and really market sell-offs on the AI ecosystem just because a lot of people are worried about the AI bubble, for example, or the concerns around AI financing and whether there's a return on investment on AI."

The bigger-than-expected IPO comes after investor demand for the stock far outstripped forecasts.
Anthropic had said in corporate filings last week that it intended to offer 825 million shares at between $70 and $78 apiece.
The Claude creator is also set to raise $26bn through a private placement, a type of deal involving the sale of stock to private investors, taking the total capital raised to $107.3bn.
SpaceX’s total IPO haul later came to $85.7bn, after the deal’s underwriters exercised an overallotment option to purchase additional shares.
The blockbuster offering gives Anthropic a market value of roughly $1.5 trillion, making it the world’s 12th-biggest firm at current valuations, just behind Tesla.
Anthropic shares will begin trading on the Nasdaq stock exchange in New York on Thursday under the ticker “ANT”.
The public listing of Anthropic, founded in 2021 by former researchers from rival AI firm OpenAI, has been closely watched as a test of the eye-watering valuations of tech companies leading the AI rollout.
Tech firms have poured trillions of dollars into AI, anticipating it will usher in revolutionary changes in business and society.
AI-related spending is forecast to reach $2.7 trillion in 2026 and $3.6 trillion in 2027, according to technology insights company Gartner.
Companies betting on the frontier technology currently make up roughly half of the value of the S&P 500 index.
The spending frenzy has stoked debate over whether Big Tech is funding a future gold mine or a speculative bubble like the one that preceded the 2000 dot-com crash.
Anthropic’s headquarters are pictured in San Francisco, California, on October 27, 2026 [File: Benjamin Fanjoy/Getty Images via AFP]
Anthropic’s listing also comes as the market for the advanced graphics processing units that power AI is under a cloud amid the spying claims roiling chip giant Nvidia.
Nvidia co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang stepped down last week amid unproven claims that a woman he was romantically involved with worked with the Chinese intelligence services.
The scandal has fuelled calls in the United States for stronger restrictions on China’s access to high-end chips, casting a pall over an AI boom partly sustained by Chinese developers’ remote access to data centres in Southeast Asia.
The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite stock index has shed 7.6 percent of its value over the past month, led by a more than 30 percent plunge in Nvidia’s stock price.
Asian stock markets with heavy exposure to AI had a mixed session on Thursday amid the flurry of excitement around Anthropic.
Japan’s benchmark Nikkei 225 rose 0.7 percent, while South Korea’s Kospi closed up 0.9 percent after sliding in morning trading.
Hong Kong’s Hang Seng Index and Taiwan’s Taiex both finished in the red, shedding 2 percent and 4.4 percent, respectively.
Nasdaq futures gained 1.9 percent ahead of Wall Street’s reopening.
Jay R Ritter, an IPO expert at the University of Florida, said that Anthropic’s ability to make profits to justify its valuation will depend on various factors, some of which are outside its control.
“Thirty years ago, the internet was the next big thing. It has changed our lives,” Ritter told Al Jazeera. “Today, artificial intelligence is the next big thing. It will change our lives, too.”
Ritter said investors are particularly excited about the potential of Anthropic’s AI models to find cures for conditions such as cancer and dementia in the near future.
“When Google went public in 2004, no one knew whether it would be able to dominate on-line searches, and no one knew how lucrative the targeted search advertising business would become,” he said.
Dan Ives, partner and senior managing director at Yorkville Ives, said Anthropic’s strong debut should help reassure investors that the AI boom is sustainable.
“At a time in which investors are very nervous on the overall tech trade and the Nvidia black cloud moment casts a shadow over the tech sector, Anthropic’s IPO is a big near-term win for the tech sector and should help restore some investor confidence that the AI revolution growth thesis is not waning,” Ives said in a note to clients.
“It is going through a very turbulent, white-knuckle period that does not change our longer-term view that $3 trillion to $4 trillion of capex will be spent over the next few years on the AI revolution,” Ives said, adding that Anthropic would be “a central player” in the buildout.

After closing thelargest initial public offering in history on Wednesday,Anthropichas about $200 billion in the bank, more than every tech giant besides Alphabet.
But the AI lab has also committed to paying vendors more than $900 billion over the next 19 years, mostly to developdata centerspoweringClaudeand its other AI models.
Some financial analysts say that gap doesn’t look concerning when you factor in that the company’s most recent quarterly sales were $17 billion, up more than 1,100 percent from the year before.
Whether investors agree will become apparent on midday Thursday when Anthropic shares begin trading on the Nasdaq stock exchange under the ticker symbol ANT.
The case for pessimism over the long term rests on issues that may slow Anthropic’s progress in developing new tools.
This month,US voters largely rejected data centerswhen given the chance, andprotests against new projectsshow no signs of slowing.
Delays in the launch or expansion of new facilities could leave Anthropic struggling to train more powerful AI models.

“The jury’s still out on whetherartificial intelligenceis going to benefit everyone, or just a few people,” says Elaine Matheny, one of 70 members of Mason County United, a grassroots organization fighting an under-construction data center intended for Anthropic in West Virginia.
“Do we really need to cover up all our farmland so Claude can do all our thinking for us?”
Then there are the concerns about the safety and security of Anthropic’s models.
At a livestreamed investor meeting last week, Anthropic CEODario Amodeisaid developing safeguards was the limiting factor in deploying its AI models.
“We don’t want these agents to run wild,” he said.
It’s possible the company could prioritize safety to a point that stunts growth.
The San Francisco-based developer is organized as a public benefit corporation, a legal designation that allows it to prioritize societal impacts alongside shareholder interests.
Amodeihas saidthe company held back a new model earlier this year, jeopardizing sales to protect the public from potentially harmful technology.

He also has said the company tries to screen for hires “oriented toward the public benefit” to ingrain the safety culture among its 5,300 employees, which is “painful in the short run” as the company passes over otherwise qualified candidates.
Anthropic’s market debut is the largest for a so-called PBC, and the first for a company solely focused on generative AI development.
It also represents a triumph for the handful ofrenegade engineers and business leaderswho started it.
They siphoned themselves off fromOpenAIin the midst of the pandemic nearly six years ago over strategic differences, and the two companies have beenrivals ever since.
For some time, OpenAI was expected to go public first, butexecutive departures,shifting priorities, andlegal troubleshave introduced roadblocks.
Anthropic also has some compelling numbers to show investors.
Revenue issoaring, while operating losses aredeclining.Its big spatwith the US Department of Defense this year over limits on Claude use doesn’t appear to have significantly slowed growth.
Overall, the number of customers spending six figures annually is up 12 times compared to a year ago.
“I don’t think you could have dreamt of an [IPO prospectus] that’s as good,” says Tomasz Tunguz, general partner at the investment firm Theory Ventures.
Because of how Anthropic must account for compensating employees with stock, it’s still wildly unprofitable—over $104 billion in losses this year through September.
That’s no matter when investors are eager to buy shares and lend money.
The IPO raised about $81 billion (more than $107 billion when adding in private sales of shares), which is more thanthe $75 billion SpaceX receivedin June in a previous world record.
Anthropic’s initial valuation of roughly $1.5 trillion fell short of SpaceX’s nearly $1.8 trillion, though the Elon Musk-led rocket maker does have a more sprawling business beyond AI.
(OpenAI has been valued at $1.25 trillion in an ongoing fundraising campaign.)
Anthropic reportedly sought, but failed, to achieve a higher valuation, suggesting some anxiety on Wall Street.
US midterm electionresultshave increased the possibility of new regulations on emerging technologies.
Fears about the debt enabling AI data center development are rising, and a potential pullback in investment from Nvidia after CEO Jensen Huang’s sudden exitare deepening those worries.
Amodei and OpenAI’sSam Altmanhave insisted investors are bullish in the long term because demand for AI models is surging.
But it’s questionable whether the companies can sustain their business without coming up with ever more powerful models that drive their profits by enabling customers to automate new types of work.
Without eye-catching capabilities, customers could shift to cheaper alternatives.
Some Anthropic employees have taken the safety concerns to extremes.
ResearcherJacob Coxon resigned from Anthropicin September, citing a belief that humanity could be destroyed within a couple of years without even more focus on keeping models under human control.
But, more recently, Coxon wasquoted by the Stanford Dailyas saying that he might return to Anthropic because he suspects he could have “more of an impact” working on safety there.
Notably, Amodei mentioned safety as a challenge even above access to electricity for data centers, which many other AI companies list as their top issue.

The NFL is pushing back on a joke by Pro Football Talk's Mike Florio about Mike Vrabel that alluded to Adolf Hitler during a discussion about the Patriots' time in Munich.
Florio, who founded Pro Football Talk, now runs the site under the umbrella of NBC Sports and contributes to NBC's "Football Night in America" each Sunday.

Florio came under fire for a joke he made during Tuesday's episode of "ProFootballTalk Live" with co-host Chris Simms.
Discussing a video of Patriots coach Mike Vrabel drinking with fans the day before New England's game in Munich, Simms mentioned that Vrabel had "the German mustache," which set Florio up for an allusion to Hitler.
"You gotta be careful trimming that thin," Florio said. "Yeah, if you’re in Germany, you gotta be careful trimming the sides of that thing."

When a producer groaned, Florio shot back, "It's funny, Gary. It was 80 years ago. Let us have some fun, for crying out loud."
Florio never mentioned Hitler's name, but it still caught the attention of the NFL, which responded on Wednesday.

An NFL spokesman condemned Florio's joke in a statement on Wednesday.
"We found the remarks inappropriate and offensive," NFL executive vice president of communications Jeff Millertold Front Office Sports. The outlet also reported that the league has reached out to NBC Sports, though it's unclear if the NFL recommended any course of action.
Florio's Pro Football Talk is licensed by NBC, and he's a "Football Night in America" contributor for the network on Sunday nights, offering insight on the rest of the league before "Sunday Night Football."

"There's more of the story to be written." Kirk Cousins could barely fight back the tears as he processed a day he thought might never come, a second chance he thought might never arrive. But football can't keep Kirko Chainz down, and suddenly the Minnesota Vikings have hope.
It is the easiest story in the NFL to get behind. A 38-year-old Kirk Cousins, written off more times than he can count, deemed deep into the back nine of his career, coming back to a hero's welcome to spearhead a playoff charge while lighting a fire under an offense in desperate need of inspiration. His inspiration.
He is football's lovable goof, with the unpretentious, unflashy dad clothes and a 'down with the kids' willingness to sling on Justin Jefferson's chains should it lift his teammates. He is also now Minnesota's great hope of rewarding defensive mastery with an attack capable of competing in January football.
The Vikings were limping behind Kyler Murray, limping behind Carson Wentz but sitting a coveted 6-2, and on Tuesday rolled the dice by trading to bring back Cousins from the Las Vegas Raiders.
It was three years ago that Cousins played the final game of his first chapter with the Vikings when he tore his Achilles tendon in Week Eight against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field. On Sunday he was back where it ended - but could it yet be where it all started again?

His start featured a perfectly placed sideline strike between two defenders to a reception-starved Justin Jefferson on third-and-second in the first quarter, and so too a high-level tight-window bullet to Myles Price for a 38-yard touchdown catch-and-run on third-and-23.

It would become Jefferson's best game of the season as he made eight catches from nine targets for 92 yards and two touchdowns, Cousins' reconnecting with one of the stars of the league having seen him suffer for the first half of the season.
Much of the debate and, at times, criticism around Cousins throughout his career has been the shortage of point guard ability as a needle-moving creator. The Patrick Mahomes' and Josh Allens and Joe Burrows and Lamar Jacksons of the world have unfortunately heightened that bar for all quarterbacks across the league. But what has never been in doubt with Cousins is the efficiency at which he feeds his best players, and at which he moves the ball and at which he can accentuate an offense's strengths without being spectacular. Spectacular isn't exactly needed when there is a Brian Flores defense foaming at the mouth in wait of their chance to go hunting on the sideline.
In one game the Vikings looked a more polished, more accomplished operation behind Cousins, and alongside that came another rampant defensive play that saw Minnesota sack Jordan Love eight times.
In the first half alone they produced five sacks, 12 pressures, one interception and one fumble recovery, including sacks on back-to-back plays at the end of the second quarter. Their sixth sack then arrived on the very first play from scrimmage after the break, followed by the third of their four turnovers when Dallas Turner recover a wayward snap.
They were frightening, and the perfect complement once Cousins had helped the Vikings get on top early. The impact was evidenced through the time of possession, Cousins' offense holding the ball for 17.55 minutes in the first half and 35.16 a week on since the Vikings mustered just 17 minutes and 28 seconds of possession against the Bills. What a difference some respite for one of the league's most potent defenses makes.
There was a nice moment in the second half when former New Orleans Saints quarterback Drew Brees paid tribute to Cousins' communication at the line of scrimmage, where he shifted personnel and changed the play like an orchestra conductor. It was long-lost control and assurance under center.
Cousins later executed a trick play that saw him pump fake left and the swivel to pump fake to his right before tossing to Gavin Bartholomew over the middle of the field for a touchdown. For Kevin O'Connell to dial up a play like that just days after Cousins' arrival is testament to the footballing brain now leading Minnesota's offense.

It has been an absolutely brutal year for quarterback injuries in the NFL. When Iwrote about this in September, the2026 seasonwas already looking as if it could be on the high end for missing signal-callers. And as we hit Week 11, it's almost more difficult to find teams that haven't had to go to their backups than ones who have been able to stick with their starter all season.
Fourteen teams have been unable to play their primary quarterback for more than a quarter of work because of an injury this season. The Bears, Cardinals and Ravens have been forced to turn to theirthird-stringoption. As many as seven of the 10 afternoon games Sunday will feature at least one backup quarterback.
Though both the league and its teams are desperate to keep the best quarterbacks healthy, injuries are going to happen. And in just about every case, going from a starter to a backup is going to create problems. Over the past decade -- without factoring in any other information -- teams that got a full game from their starting quarterback and went up against opposition that didn't get a single snap from their preferred starter won nearly 66% of the time.
It would be great if teams could turn to a deep pool of backups, but that just isn't the case at quarterback. And there's a phrase that comes up all the time: "There aren't 32 starting-caliber quarterbacks to go around in the NFL." And yes, the reality is that the league rarely, if ever, has 32 quality starters featuring at the same time.
But does that mean that therecouldn'tbe 32 quality starters if they were dispersed around the league's 32 teams? I'm not so sure. There are some gaps in that logic, and it's a topic I've always wanted to explore. The middle of an injury-riddled 2026 season feels like the right time to get there. How many viable starting QBs are typically on NFL rosters at any one time? Is it 20? 30? 40?
I wasn't sure of the answer, but I'm sure we're not considering the question correctly. I'm going to show why that's the case and give my best estimate for how many viable quarterbacks have typically been present on NFL rosters at any one time over the past few decades.
The fundamental flaw in the "There aren't 32 starting-caliber quarterbacks" argument is that it evaluates only the 32 quarterbacks who are currently playing in NFL lineups. Even if we ignore injuries and just consider each team's ideal and preferred option heading into 2026, that's still going to leave us with a handful of teams that don't have a quarterback who projects to be even a viable starter, let alone a solid one. United States President Donald Trump has accused Iran of exploring chemical and biological weapons, reignitingallegationsthat Tehran may be planning a “dirty bomb” attack.

Trump claimed Tehran has pivoted away from developing nuclear capabilities given that “we’ve shut them out”. “We’ll see what happens after January 1,” he said, before referring to Iranians as “nasty people”.
His comments follow a report by CNN on Tuesday citing US intelligence indicating that Iran may be developing plans to target senior officials in Trump’s administration with a chemical weapon in Washington, DC.
On Wednesday, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio dismissed concerns about a possible Iranian attack, saying the US does not face an “imminent threat”. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin echoed Rubio’s conclusion, confirming there was no indication of an upcoming attack.
But Trump did not dismiss the possibility. Asked whether people in Washington, DC, should be concerned about a potential attack, Trump said he did not believe so, but threatened retaliation if it happened.
“If it does happen, we wipe them out,” he said.
Is there evidence that Iran possesses a ‘dirty bomb’?
Iran is a signatory to the Biological Weapons Convention, but it ratified it six years before the 1979 revolution that overthrew the Pahlavi monarchy and established the Islamic Republic of Iran. It is also a party to the Chemical Weapons Convention (CWC), ratified in 1997.
Nonetheless, Western intelligence agencies have long maintained that Iran is pursuing unconventional capabilities.
According to a report by a British think tank, the Royal United Services Institute (RUSI), Iran’s biological weapons programme is believed to have accelerated since the Iran-Iraq War, which ended in 1988.
After Iraq extensively used chemical weapons during that conflict, Tehran resolved never again to accept such an asymmetry in unconventional capabilities, RUSI concluded. What followed was a sustained effort to develop biological agents under the cover of civilian research.
Hamish de Bretton-Gordon, an analyst and former British Army officer, said it would not be surprising if Iran was resorting to developing chemical weapons after US military strikes on its nuclear facilities set back its nuclear programme.
“It is also possible they are looking at biological weapons,” de Bretton-Gordon told Al Jazeera. “With the advent of AI-enabled bio weapons, they have the potential to be as devastating as nuclear weapons at a fraction of the cost and time.”
Such weapons could “replace their nuclear programme [and] be far more difficult to detect”, he added.
According to Dan Kaszeta, an associate fellow at RUSI focussing on defence against chemical, biological and radiological weapons, “this is an area where things are incredibly vague”.
“Any country with the industry, science and laboratory infrastructure that Iran has could, in theory, make chemical and biological hazards in sufficient quantity for a singular incident like a localised terrorist attack,” Kaszeta told Al Jazeera. “The underlying technology is not highly sophisticated.”
“As far as whether Iran has had a chemical or biological weapons programme has been debated for decades, ever since the Iran-Iraq war,” he added. “There have been arguments put forward on both sides of that hypothesis, without any firm conclusion.”
Jacek Siewiera, nonresident senior fellow with the Atlantic Council’s Europe Center, separated scientific expertise operational weapons capability from the political willingness to conduct an attack.
“A research programme does not, by itself, establish the ability to carry out a particular operation abroad,” Siewiera told Al Jazeera. “A credible assessment would require corroborated information about capability, operational reach and intent. I would therefore be cautious about assigning a probability to the specific scenario described.”
This is not the first time the US has accused an enemy of possessing unconventional weapons.
Glen Rangwala, associate professor in the Department of Politics and International Studies at the University of Cambridge, in the UK, said: “There is a fairly extensive history of successive US administrations making unfounded allegations about countries of the Middle East possessing weapons of mass destruction (WMD).”
“It serves to raise the stakes internationally and put potential domestic critics on the back foot,” Rangwala told Al Jazeera.
Washington launched an invasion of Iraq in 2003 after claiming that Saddam Hussein’s government posed an imminent threat due to its alleged chemical, biological and nuclear programmes.
A Senate committee found the CIA and others in George W Bush’s administrationmanipulated evidenceto justify the occupation of Iraq, calling the operation a “whitewash for the White House.”
No stockpiles of banned weapons, nor evidence of a programme to develop any, were ever found in Iraq following the US-led military action.

It has been an absolutely brutal year for quarterback injuries in the NFL.
When Iwrote about this in September, the2026 seasonwas already looking as if it could be on the high end for missing signal-callers.
And as we hit Week 11, it's almost more difficult to find teams that haven't had to go to their backups than ones who have been able to stick with their starter all season.
Fourteen teams have been unable to play their primary quarterback for more than a quarter of work because of an injury this season.
The Bears, Cardinals and Ravens have been forced to turn to theirthird-stringoption.
As many as seven of the 10 afternoon games Sunday will feature at least one backup quarterback.
Though both the league and its teams are desperate to keep the best quarterbacks healthy, injuries are going to happen.
And in just about every case, going from a starter to a backup is going to create problems.

Over the past decade -- without factoring in any other information -- teams that got a full game from their starting quarterback and went up against opposition that didn't get a single snap from their preferred starter won nearly 66% of the time.
It would be great if teams could turn to a deep pool of backups, but that just isn't the case at quarterback.

And there's a phrase that comes up all the time: "There aren't 32 starting-caliber quarterbacks to go around in the NFL." And yes, the reality is that the league rarely, if ever, has 32 quality starters featuring at the same time.
But does that mean that therecouldn'tbe 32 quality starters if they were dispersed around the league's 32 teams?
There are some gaps in that logic, and it's a topic I've always wanted to explore.
The middle of an injury-riddled 2026 season feels like the right time to get there.
How many viable starting QBs are typically on NFL rosters at any one time?
I wasn't sure of the answer, but I'm sure we're not considering the question correctly.
I'm going to show why that's the case and give my best estimate for how many viable quarterbacks have typically been present on NFL rosters at any one time over the past few decades.
The fundamental flaw in the "There aren't 32 starting-caliber quarterbacks" argument is that it evaluates only the 32 quarterbacks who are currently playing in NFL lineups.

Even if we ignore injuries and just consider each team's ideal and preferred option heading into 2026, that's still going to leave us with a handful of teams that don't have a quarterback who projects to be even a viable starter, let alone a solid one.

Opening the meeting, Xi said that it “has groundbreaking significance”.
“The world is at peace when great powers live in harmony,” Xi said, adding that the three countries “should work together to address global challenges”.
In a major statement, the Chinese leader also said “nuclear weapons should be comprehensively banned and thoroughly destroyed, building a nuclear-free world,” reported China’s Xinhua news agency.

“Too often past leaders avoided talking to leaders they had disagreements with,” he said. “No peace ever forged by declining opportunities.”
Meanwhile, in his opening remarks, Putin made it clear that the war in Ukraine would be the focus of his conversation, before the three retreated into closed-door talks which lasted for about 55 minutes.
Thetalks between the leadersof the world’s largest nuclear powers were not likely to produce major agreements, analysts say, given deep differences over Ukraine, Iran, nuclear weapons and trade. But the meeting had unnerved smaller countries that feared their interests might be disregarded.
‘Special friendship’ between US, China
Ahead of the trilateral gathering, Trump held separate bilateral meetings with both Xi and Putin on Thursday.
The US president described Xi as a “friend” and said Washington and Beijing enjoyed a “special relationship”.
“As long as the two of us are in charge, I don’t think we’ll have a problem,” Trump said in opening remarks at his meeting with the Chinese leader. He also boasted that “no other countries can do what we can”.
Trump said the US has done “amazing” things in the past two years, since he returned to power, while praising China for many of its gains over several years.
Xi, meanwhile, said that he remained committed to working with Trump to steer ties between their countries on the “correct course”.
Relations between Beijing and Washington have been stable and improving, Xi said to Trump at the start of their third one-on-one meeting this year, which lasted for about an hour.
“We have established a new definition of a constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability, giving it new substance based on respect, fairness and reciprocity,” Xi said.
Ahead of the bilateral meeting, Trump said the Board of Trade that he and the Chinese president agreed to form at their Beijing summit in May has brought balance to the two countries’ relationship. He said the US and China had split their tariffs in a “fair way”.
Earlier in the day, during talks with Putin, Trump also called the Russian leader a “friend”.
“We’ve had a great relationship for many years. We know each other for a long time, and I think a lot of wonderful things can come out of this, or at least start. But I think they’ll come out of this,” Trump told Putin.
A video published by the White House showed the two leaders shaking hands and Trump briefly whispering to Putin at the start of their meeting.
In another video posted by the White House Rapid Response X account, Trump was shown pointing at Putin and saying, “He’s my friend.”
Kremlin foreign policy aide Yury Ushakov said the two leaders “discussed the conflict in Ukraine and bilateral relations issues”.
“The meeting between the Russian and US leaders went well,” Ushakov said, according to Russia’s state news agency TASS, adding that Putin left the talks “in an excellent” mood.
Thursday also features the main event of the APEC summit, as representatives of the 21 Pacific Rim economies gather for discussions that will include high-stakes diplomacy, Al Jazeera’s Katrina Yu said, reporting from Shenzhen.
“Xi Jinping, who spoke at the banquet last night during the opening ceremony, said the discussion will centre on promoting mutual openness, innovation-driven growth and results-oriented cooperation,” said Yu.

Speaking to Fox News earlier on Thursday, Trump highlighted the pomp surrounding his arrival. Xi greeted Air Force One on the airport tarmac on Wednesday, which contrasted with the more muted greetings offered to other leaders.
“This is a great president, one of the great presidents of China, and he’s never gone to the airport to meet somebody,” Trump said when asked what he wanted to get out of the trilateral summit.
Trump has insisted that nuclear arms control be a central topic of the meeting, despiteBeijing’s repeated objectionsto talks on the issue with Washington and Moscow, which have far larger nuclear arsenals.

The unprecedented trilateral meeting in Shenzhen between US President Donald Trump, China’s Xi Jinping and Russia’s Vladimir Putin ended on Thursday without statements from the three leaders, after Trump declared at the beginning that the three global powers "are making history".
Opening their first such summit, which could be a pivotal moment in world history, Trump said the three leaders “will talk about all problems that are being discussed in the world.”
“We have great responsibilities to solve problems that affect the entire planet," he added.
Trump said he had a "long discussion" with Putin on Russia's ongoing all-out war in Ukraine and that all sides "would like to see an end to that war".
Xi joined Trump in saying their summit “has groundbreaking significance”, adding that “the world is at peace when great powers live in harmony," calling on the three countries to “abandon Cold War mentality, not pursue decoupling and breaking chains”.
"The three countries should work together to address global challenges,” and that they "can strengthen coordination to safeguard global energy supply chain stability," Xi said. “Adversity reveals true responsibility.”
Putin said that Russia’s war in Ukraine would be part of the talks, stating that “we have shared interests in Ukraine.”
“Russia, the US and China are united not only by their status as victorious nations in World War II, but also by their responsibility for maintaining international peace,” Putin said.
However, after the summit ended, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told the Russian media that Ukraine was not "the central topic" at the summit.
Just as the summit was starting, China's state news agency published a statement from Xi saying that “nuclear weapons should be comprehensively banned and thoroughly destroyed, building a nuclear-free world.”
In his opening statements, Trump said that the “three countries are uniquely positioned to discuss nuclear weapons."
“Too often past leaders avoided talking to leaders they had disagreements with,” Trump added.
The leaders posed for a family photo without shaking hands as they started their summit and made no statements when it concluded.
The meeting ended after around an hour and 20 minutes. Trump left the venue immediately for Shenzhen's airport and took off shortly after, while Xi accompanied Putin who also departed for Russia.
China's state news agency Xinhua published the full text of what it called the "trilateral peace declaration," listing four key points: commitment to UN reform, plans to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products, respect for the immunity of state officials and opposition to the ICC and similar institutions abusing their jurisdiction, as well as an agreement to hold dialogue on nuclear risk reduction and non-proliferation.
The declaration makes no explicit reference to Ukraine, Iran, Taiwan or North Korea.
High-stakes bilateral talks before the trilateral
The US and Chinese presidents met bilaterally earlier on Thursday in their third substantial meeting this year.
During the meeting, Trump said that the US and China want to help end the war in Ukraine, stating that "we're looking to both help with respect to the war with Russia and Ukraine."
The US president praised their friendship and their shared interest in having oil shipped through the Strait of Hormuz, which has become a key site of attacks in the Iran war.

Chinese state media, particularly Xinhua and People's Daily, framed the APEC summit and the trilateral around Xi's diplomatic leadership, multilateral cooperation and China's commitment to free trade. ByOlivia IrelandandLaura Bicker,China correspondent
Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin met for the first time in more than a year on Wednesday, as they prepared for landmark talks in China with Xi Jinping.
The US president was greeted off his plane by the Chinese leader as he arrived in Shenzhen for a summit of Asia-Pacific leaders, which will culminate in a closely-watched meeting between the pair and the Russian president.
After a carefully choreographed handshake and hug between Trump and Xi on the tarmac, the US president later greeted and exchanged pleasantries with Putin ahead of a reception.
Trump and Putin are expected to hold one-on-one talks on the sidelines of the summit on Thursday, in which the war in Ukraine could be discussed.
However the main focus during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum (Apec) will be on the US-China-Russia talks on Thursday - the first time the trio of leaders have met together in person.
A full agenda has not been made public but there have been various hints about what could be discussed, including the wars in Ukraine and Iran, nuclear proliferation, trade tensions and developments in artificial intelligence.

Peskov also said that "no more than an hour" had been allocated for Thursday's trilateral talks between Putin, Trump and Xi.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has raised fears of a plan to end the war being discussed in the absence of representatives from Kyiv or Europe.
It is unclear whether China would want this issue to be on the agenda in Shenzhen, with Beijing talking more generally about the need to discuss "safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability".
China has officially remained neutral since Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, rejecting accusations from Kyiv and its allies that it has been tacitly supporting Moscow, including by exporting dual-use technology used by the Russian military.
Wednesday's handshake was the first in-person meeting between Trump and Putin since August 2025, when the Russian leader travelled to Alaska for talks on the Ukraine war which failed to deliver a breakthrough.
Xi's personal reception for Trump at the airport mimicked a similar move by the US president when the Chinese leader visited Washington in September, a gesture Xi described as "special".

Chinese state-run news agency Xinhua quoted Xi as saying he wanted to pursue a "constructive strategic and stable relationship based on respect, fairness, and equality".
Xi's greeting will be seen as a diplomatic gesture designed to begin the week's talks with his American counterpart on a cordial note.

“The world is at peace when great powers live in harmony,” Xi said, adding that the three countries “should work together to address global challenges”.
In a major statement, the Chinese leader also said “nuclear weapons should be comprehensively banned and thoroughly destroyed, building a nuclear-free world,” reported China’s Xinhua news agency.
In Trump’s opening remarks, the US president said the three countries are “uniquely positioned” to discuss nuclear weapons.
“Too often past leaders avoided talking to leaders they had disagreements with,” he said.

Meanwhile, in his opening remarks, Putin made it clear that the war in Ukraine would be the focus of his conversation, before the three retreated into closed-door talks which lasted for about 55 minutes.
Thetalks between the leadersof the world’s largest nuclear powers were not likely to produce major agreements, analysts say, given deep differences over Ukraine, Iran, nuclear weapons and trade.
But the meeting had unnerved smaller countries that feared their interests might be disregarded.
Ahead of the trilateral gathering, Trump held separate bilateral meetings with both Xi and Putin on Thursday.
The US president described Xi as a “friend” and said Washington and Beijing enjoyed a “special relationship”.
“As long as the two of us are in charge, I don’t think we’ll have a problem,” Trump said in opening remarks at his meeting with the Chinese leader.
He also boasted that “no other countries can do what we can”.
Trump said the US has done “amazing” things in the past two years, since he returned to power, while praising China for many of its gains over several years.
Xi, meanwhile, said that he remained committed to working with Trump to steer ties between their countries on the “correct course”.
Relations between Beijing and Washington have been stable and improving, Xi said to Trump at the start of their third one-on-one meeting this year, which lasted for about an hour.
“We have established a new definition of a constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability, giving it new substance based on respect, fairness and reciprocity,” Xi said.
Ahead of the bilateral meeting, Trump said the Board of Trade that he and the Chinese president agreed to form at their Beijing summit in May has brought balance to the two countries’ relationship.
He said the US and China had split their tariffs in a “fair way”.
Earlier in the day, during talks with Putin, Trump also called the Russian leader a “friend”.
We know each other for a long time, and I think a lot of wonderful things can come out of this, or at least start.
But I think they’ll come out of this,” Trump told Putin.
A video published by the White House showed the two leaders shaking hands and Trump briefly whispering to Putin at the start of their meeting.
In another video posted by the White House Rapid Response X account, Trump was shown pointing at Putin and saying, “He’s my friend.”
Kremlin foreign policy aide Yury Ushakov said the two leaders “discussed the conflict in Ukraine and bilateral relations issues”.
“The meeting between the Russian and US leaders went well,” Ushakov said, according to Russia’s state news agency TASS, adding that Putin left the talks “in an excellent” mood.

Thursday also features the main event of the APEC summit, as representatives of the 21 Pacific Rim economies gather for discussions that will include high-stakes diplomacy, Al Jazeera’s Katrina Yu said, reporting from Shenzhen.

“Xi Jinping, who spoke at the banquet last night during the opening ceremony, said the discussion will centre on promoting mutual openness, innovation-driven growth and results-oriented cooperation,” said Yu.
On the US-China-Russia talks, James Bays, Al Jazeera’s diplomatic editor, said that when it comes to Trump, “his personal role always matters to him”.
But, he added, “something worth bearing in mind: you have three leaders here, Trump, Xi, and Putin.
Putin has been in power; he’s been in the main driving seat in Moscow for 26 years; Xi’s been there for 14 years; and they know President Trump only has 26 more months.”
Speaking to Fox News earlier on Thursday, Trump highlighted the pomp surrounding his arrival.

lead_title: Crimean Bridge attacked again, Russian official says

evidence_pages.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cm87:
Putin's Crimean Bridge comes under attack again, Russian official says - BBC News
Final moments before stretch of Crimean Bridge collapsed after Ukrainian attack earlier this week
Published19 November 2026, 01:05 GMT
The Crimean Bridge has been attacked by Ukraine for the third time this week, Russia has said.
The Moscow-installed head of Crimea, Sergei Aksyonov, said that rail traffic was temporarily suspended following another strike on the bridge connecting Russia to occupied Crimea.
On Tuesday, Ukrainian missiles and drones destroyed the central road section of the critical bridge, collapsing part of it into the water.
The important infrastructure has long been targeted by Ukraine because of its significance as a logistical and symbolic asset to Moscow's war effort.
A screengrab of the damaged Crimean bridge in the Kerch Strait on 17 November
It comes as Russian President Vladimir Putin meets US President Donald Trump and China's President Xi Jinping on Thursday forlandmark talks in China.
Aksyonov confirmed the strike on the bridge in the early hours of Thursday via Telegram.
Russia's transport ministry said nobody had been hurt in the attack, and that specialists were assessing damage to the bridge.
"As a result of a nighttime drone attack, train services on the railway section of the Crimean Bridge have been temporarily suspended," the ministry said in a statement on Telegram.
Meanwhile, Ukrainian sources have continued to issue air raid alert warnings overnight for districts just outside of the capital Kyiv.
At least four people were killed in a Russian drone attack on the southern city of Odesa on Wednesday, according to Odesa Governor Oleh Kiper. Officials described the attack as "brutal and deliberate... directly targeting people and their lives".
President Volodymyr Zelensky called the initial strikes on the Crimean Bridge an "unprecedented operation" weeks in the making.
Putin's Crimean Bridge partly collapses as Zelensky hails 'unprecedented' attack by Ukraine
Ukraine used drones and missiles against it on 17 November which brought down a key section of the road.
That section of the double-arched, 12-mile bridge now lies on the seabed, brought down by an arsenal of Ukrainian long-range weaponry in a seven-stage operation culminating in a dramatic collapse.
In response, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov has said the bridge "will be rebuilt, and it will be even better than before".
While Ukrainian forces have struggled to close the bridge for good, recent attempts have brought them closer to destroying the bridge's crucial road and rail route for Russian soldiers heading towards the front line.
Russian forces have also targeted key bridge crossings over the Dnipro River in Kyiv in recent days.
Russian strikes hit the Pivnichnyi (Northern) and Pivdennyi (Southern) bridges causing traffic closures, partial damage to the metro system and some power and water outages.

Crimea bridge has been attacked again, says Russian-installed governor
Assessment of damage under way, days after two attacks that destroyed road section of key bridge across Kerch strait linking annexed peninsula to Russia
The remaining Kerch rail bridge connecting Crimea to Russia was attacked overnight, leading to a halt in train services, two days after adramatic Ukrainian air raidhad knocked out the road bridge alongside.
Sergei Aksyonov, the Kremlin-appointed governor ofCrimea, said on Wednesday night that there had been another attack on the bridge, then added on Thursday that trains would start crossing from “approximately 4pm”.
Emergency repair workers had made “heroic efforts” to restore the track, the governor said. Nobody was reported wounded as a result of the incident, Russia’s transport ministry added.
The latest air raid took place hours before theunprecedented three-way summitin Shenzhen, China, between Donald Trump, the US president, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping, his Russian and Chinese counterparts.
It was the third time that the $3.6bn bridge, built by Russia after its occupation of Crimea, has been struck in a week. On Tuesday, a 227-metre section of the road spanning the Kerch strait was destroyed after a complex missile and drone attack that had been prepared and planned over several weeks.
0:34Ukraine releases footage of strike on Crimean Bridge – video
Ukrainian military sources had indicated the timing of the attack on the road bridge was deliberate, ahead of the summit, suggesting that the follow-up raid on the rail bridge overnight may have been intended to bring it down as well.
One source in Ukraine’s armed forces said this week’s attacks weredesigned to embarrass Putinon the world stage. “The bridge is a symbol of Putin’s rule. Destroying it sends a message to the other two great leaders that Putin is not as strong as he pretends,” the person said.
‘They were keeping it for a rainy day’: Ukraine’s Kerch bridge attack is proof Kyiv still has cards to playRead more
For Ukraine, the bridge across the Kerch strait is ahated symbolof Russian arrogance and colonial thinking. Ukraine has previously declared that the bridge, built eight years ago, is illegal. Kyiv had tried twice to blow it up – with a truck bomb in 2022, and a sea drone the following year.
Earlier, Ukraine critically damaged the road section of the bridge in what President Volodymyr Zelenskyy hailed as an“unprecedented” military operation. A span of the bridge’s road section collapsed, but the railway line was still standing.
Zelesnkyy described the earlier attack as the culmination of a long and complex campaign to demolish the bridge, largely involving domestically produced drones and ballistic missiles.
Flamingo FP-5 cruise missiles and Palianytsia drones struck the central road section of the bridge, bringing down its supporting arch. A range of weapons, including Ukraine’s Neputune cruise missile and the Ruta, made by Dutch company Destinus, targeted the adjacent rail section, Zelenskyy said.

lead_title: Bốn hạng mục có thể ảnh hưởng khai thác Long Thành vào tháng 12

evidence_pages.https://vnexpress.net/bon-hang-muc-co-th:
Bốn hạng mục có thể ảnh hưởng khai thác Long Thành vào tháng 12 - Báo VnExpress
Bốn hạng mục có thể ảnh hưởng khai thác Long Thành vào tháng 12
Hơn một tháng trước ngày vận hành thương mại, sân bay Long Thành còn khối lượng lớn phải hoàn thành, từ thi công nhà ga, đường nội cảng đến nghiệm thu, cấp phép.
Sân bay Long Thành tại Đồng Nai dự kiến khai thác thương mại từngày 24/12. Cùng với việc đẩy nhanh thi công các hạng mục chính, dự án triển khai chương trình chuẩn bị khai thác (ORAT) với 55 kịch bản, chia thành ba đợt từ tháng 9 đến tháng 12 năm nay.
Trong báo cáo gửi lãnh đạo Chính phủ về điều kiện và công tác chuẩn bị khai thác sân bay mới đây, Bộ Xây dựng đánh giá phương án vận hành từ ngày 24/12 do ACV đề xuất giúp sớm đưa công trình vào sử dụng, từng bước phát huy hiệu quả và tạo điều kiện triển khai lộ trình chuyển đổi. Tuy nhiên, một số hạng mục còn khối lượng công việc lớn nên mốc khai thác cần xem xét dựa trên kết quả thực tế.
Bên ngoài nhà ga hành khách sân bay Long Thành, ngày 17/11. Ảnh:Quỳnh Trần
Theo tiến độ đến cuối tháng 10, ba dự án thành phần có thể hướng tới mục tiêu sẵn sàng khai thác trong tháng 12, gồm dự án thành phần 1 (trụ sở cơ quan quản lý nhà nước), thành phần 2 (công trình phục vụ quản lý bay) và thành phần 4 (công trình dịch vụ mặt đất).
Thách thức lớn nhất nằm ở dự án thành phần 3 - các công trình thiết yếu. Trong số 16 gói thầu của dự án này, 4 gói đã hoàn thành, 12 gói đang triển khai. Theo tiến độ ACV đưa ra, khối lượng còn lại tại một số gói vẫn rất lớn, có nguy cơ ảnh hưởng tới mốc hoàn thành, tập trung ở đường giao thông nội cảng và hạ tầng kỹ thuật (gói 4.8), nhà ga hành khách (gói 5.10), nhà ga hàng hóa số 1 và các công trình phụ trợ (gói 7.8), nhà để xe (gói 11.5).
Các gói thầu này có nhiều hạng mục phức tạp, đồng thời còn vướng mắc về nguồn vật liệu xây dựng và thanh toán cho nhà thầu. Một số gói thuộc dự án thành phần 3 phải hoàn thành trong tháng 11 để các hạng mục liên quan ở dự án thành phần 1, 2 và 4 có thể đấu nối, nghiệm thu.
Tiến độ các gói thầu được đánh giá ảnh hưởng trực tiếp đến khả năng khai thác đồng bộ sân bay. Đây cũng là điều kiện để chủ đầu tư và cơ quan quản lý hoàn tất thủ tục cấp phép môi trường, an ninh hàng không và các nội dung liên quan.
Bộ Xây dựng cho biết theo thông lệ quốc tế và khuyến nghị của Hiệp hội Vận tải hàng không quốc tế (IATA), với sân bay mới quy mô lớn, có tính tích hợp cao, ORAT không chỉ kiểm tra thiết bị mà còn đánh giá khả năng vận hành của toàn hệ thống.
Do có nhiều hệ thống tự động phức tạp và cần sự phối hợp giữa nhiều đơn vị, quá trình chuẩn bị, thử nghiệm thực tế thường kéo dài 6-12 tháng. Các đợt thử nghiệm được tổ chức liên tiếp nhằm phát hiện, khắc phục lỗi và kiểm tra lại.
Hãng hàng không lắp đặt thiết bị để vận hành thương mại. Ảnh:Quỳnh Trần
Tại Long Thành, quá trình thử nghiệm tích hợp toàn diện dự kiến kéo dài khoảng ba tháng, từ cuối tháng 9 đến khi khai thác thương mại vào tháng 12. Trong thời gian này, sân bay chưa có chuyến bay thực tế, trong khi ACV phải đẩy nhanh thi công, nghiệm thu, hiệu chuẩn thiết bị, hoàn tất thủ tục, bố trí nhân sự và xây dựng quy trình vận hành.
Bộ Xây dựng đánh giá thời gian ORAT ngắn sẽ thu hẹp quỹ dự phòng để xử lý sự cố, nhất là những lỗi chỉ xuất hiện khi nhiều hệ thống cùng hoạt động hoặc khi có hành khách, hành lý, hàng hóa và tàu bay thực tế.
Từ đó Bộ Xây dựng đề nghị ACV, với vai trò đơn vị khai thác cảng, rà soát và đánh giá toàn diện phương án đưa sân bay vào khai thác trong tháng 12. ACV chịu trách nhiệm xác định thời điểm, phạm vi và phương án khai thác dựa trên mức độ hoàn thành đồng bộ của công trình, kết quả nghiệm thu, vận hành thử, đánh giá an toàn và việc hoàn tất các thủ tục.
Để bảo đảm mốc khai thác trong tháng 12, Phó thủ tướng thường trực Phạm Gia Túc đã giao Bộ Xây dựng chỉ đạo ACV xây dựng phương án bảo đảm tuyệt đối an ninh, an toàn và khả thi. Phương án cần được rà soát cùng với việc đánh giá các điều kiện cần thiết để đưa sân bay vào vận hành. Bộ Tài chính và các cơ quan liên quan được giao tiếp tục hướng dẫn, hỗ trợ ACV tháo gỡ vướng mắc trong thanh toán của dự án.
Về tiến độ thi công, ACV cần rà soát kỹ khối lượng còn lại của các gói thầu, xác định thời hạn hoàn thành từng hạng mục và đề ra giải pháp tháo gỡ vướng mắc về nguồn cung nhiên liệu, vật liệu và thanh toán khối lượng thi công. Chủ đầu tư cần chỉ đạo nhà thầu bảo đảm tiến độ, nếu không đáp ứng phải xác định rõ trách nhiệm và xử lý.
Song song đó, ACV phải phối hợp với các đơn vị của Bộ Xây dựng triển khai các thủ tục, như nghiệm thu các hạng mục công trình; kiểm tra, đánh giá điều kiện khai thác và thực hiện thủ tục cấp phép... Các thủ tục chuyên ngành hàng không cần đảm bảo hoàn thành đúng tiến độ, không ảnh hưởng đến thời điểm đưa công trình vào khai thác.
Hệ thống vận chuyển hành lý ở sân bay. Ảnh:Quỳnh Trần
Về phía địa phương, lãnh đạo Chính phủ giao Đồng Nai và TP HCM tiếp tục rà soát khả năng cung ứng nhiên liệu, vật liệu để ưu tiên cho dự án sân bay. Các tuyến giao thông kết nối Long Thành cần được đẩy nhanh tiến độ hoàn thiện.
Trước đó, theo kế hoạch của ACV, sân bay dự kiến khai thác tối đa 366 chuyến mỗi tuần trong giai đoạn đầu, gồm 322 chuyến nội địa và 44 chuyến quốc tế. Để chuẩn bị đưa sân bay vào khai thác, Cục Hàng không Việt Nam đã khảo sát các hãng bay và nhiều bên liên quan, cho thấy các hãng quốc tế đều ủng hộ chuyển sang Long Thành.
Tuy nhiên, nhiều hãng muốnlùi chuyển đổiđến lịch bay mùa đông 2027 hoặc muộn hơn để có đủ thời gian chuẩn bị. Đối với trong nước, một số hãng đã sẵn sàng khai thác ở sân bay từ giai đoạn đầu theo kế hoạch của ACV.
Sân bay Long Thành xây dựng trên diện tích khoảng 5.000 ha, chia làm ba giai đoạn đầu tư. Dự án hiện ở giai đoạn một, với công suất thiết kế 25 triệu lượt khách và 1,2 triệu tấn hàng hóa mỗi năm.
