Why Eagles are cutting Fred Johnson, Hollywood Brown during bye week | Sporting NewsSkip to main content
Why Eagles are cutting Fred Johnson, Hollywood Brown during bye week
ThePhiladelphia Eagles' season is pretty much over. At 2-7 heading into their Week 10 bye, the Eagles are all but eliminated from playoff contention. Instead, the only thing this team will be contending for is a top-five pick.
As the Eagles start preparing for the 2027 NFL season, seeing how their youngsters play will be one of the main things to watch for the rest of the year. During their bye, they made the first moves as they head in that direction.
TheEagles announced Fridaythat Fred Johnson and Hollywood Brown were waived. Why are the Eagles moving on from both of those veterans? There are a few reasons why those two veterans are now set to hit waivers.
Why the Eagles are cutting Hollywood Brown and Fred Johnson
"We have waived WR Marquise Brown and T Fred Johnson," the Eagles announced on Friday, November 13, during their Week 10 bye.
These two players being released makes a lot of sense, as they'll save money by waiving both, which is a smart decision amid a lost season.
That's especially the case considering that neither player was contributing to this team. Johnson hasn't been a factor along the offensive line, with other youngsters getting involved.
Browns' lack of involvement in the offense is especially notable. Despite DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks dealing with injuries, Brown hasn't gotten much run at wide receiver.
MORE:Eagles’ Braden Mann boots punt not seen in over 20 years
It's instead been all about Makai Lemon and Darius Cooper. Brown, the veteran, wasn't a part of the WR rotation in Philadelphia. Coming out of the bye, Smith and Cooper might be back, which would leave Brown without a role in the offense.
Besides, the Eagles might be activating Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley off injured reserve soon, and the release of these two players is necessary to open roster spots for those moves.
Also, it's worth noting that the NFL trade deadline has passed, so the Eagles aren't missing out on the chance to get draft capital by cutting these two players.
Brown and Johnson haven't been factors in the game plan this season, and likely wouldn't have been for the remainder of the season. These roster moves make a lot of sense, even though it's technically making the Eagles worse.

We're gonna ride it till we just can't ride it no more
'Cause the sun is shining all the time
Here at Bottom 10 Headquarters, located under one of the giant end zone tarps the Rose Bowl pulls out for UCLA Friday night home games, we are in mourning. However, we are also in celebration. Why? Because the Bottom 10's founding father has left this extremely mortal coil at the age of 80.
Steve Harvey was sweet, funny and a singular Los Angeles newspaper institution. He died last Tuesday, fittingly just as last week's Bottom 10 had been filed to ESPN.com. You see, we did not invent this ranking of college football's most rankled rosters. Harvey did, and it happened more than six decades ago, dreamed up when he was a USC undergrad, right around the time he achieved one of his proudest accomplishments: being burned in effigy by the Trojans marching band because of some unflattering words he'd penned in the school paper.
The man was pure SoCal, born in Santa Monica, raised in West Los Angeles and a journalism student during the Trojan eras of John McKay and Mike Garrett. But while his alma mater was battling UCLA forVictory Bellsand Athletic Association of Western Universities (precursor to the Pac-8) titles, he was instead drawn to the loser-y likes of 0-10 Kansas State, 1-8 Pacific and 1-9 Iowa.
Looks like it's back to the fundamentals for USC's football team. https://t.co/t1cErRD3HP
— Steve Harvey (@sharvey9)September 4, 2016
"I never saw it as something mean," Harvey told me during our lone phone conversation several years ago, when I unsuccessfully tried to convince him to co-author an ESPN.com Bottom 10 with me. "I always I saw more of me in them than I did in the teams who never lost. They felt more relatable."
Harvey related to a lot. From the L.A. Herald Examiner and L.A. Times to L.A. Observed and Long Beach's Grunion Gazette, he spent the adult years of his 80 trips around the sun scouring Los Angeles for the weird and misspelled.
And yes, he was well aware that he was not the most famous Steve Harvey.

More banks says customers using AI agents are on their own — even if they get hacked | TechCrunch
Image Credits:Julian Prizont-Cado / Getty ImagesAI
More banks says customers using AI agents are on their own — even if they get hacked
Tim Fernholz9:32 AM PST · November 18, 2026
Citibank, the third largest commercial bank in the United States, changed its terms of service this week, telling customers who use third-party AI tools for personal finance that anything that goes wrong is their problem — even if they get hacked.
AI agents, ranging from frontier lab models to purpose-built personal finance tools, can be given the credentials to your bank account and other online financial portals, with the idea that they can analyze spending and investment decisions, offer advice, and even handle transactions and bill payments.
But financial institutions aren’t thrilled with the unreliable AI actors in their systems, and are telling customers that they won’t be held responsible for reversing an intentional or unintentional transaction made by automated assistants.
“As third-party AI tools become more widely available, we want customers to understand the risks associated with sharing banking credentials or authorizing those tools to access their accounts,” a Citi spokesperson told TechCrunch. “We recently updated our Online User Agreement to provide greater clarity about those risks and to reinforce that customers who choose to grant account access to third-party AI agents are responsible for activities conducted through those agents.”
JPMorgan andBank of America, the two largest banks in the country, announced similar policies last month. And PNC, the eight largest bank, changed its terms today.
Citi’s update goes beyond telling customers that they are responsible for anything their agents may do; it also informs them that if the AI tools leaks their credentials or is hacked, the customer will be responsible for anything hackers do with their account. Banking giant Citizens similarly emailed its customers this week, warning that they are also on the hook for anything their AI assistant does, according to an email seen by TechCrunch.
As AI startups look for more revenue, breaking into personal finance presents an attractive opportunity for companies to add value for customers and wet their beaks in the stream of fees generated by the sector. But if consumers are already leery of sharing their email or chat records with an AI agent, bank and brokerage accounts offer a new trust challenge.
Anthropic’s approach is telling: Thepersonal finance toolit launched earlier this month is explicitly billed as “read-only” and “can’t move, manage, or invest your money.”
Beyond cybersecurity concerns, banks also view efforts to enter their franchise as a competitive threat. Markets shuddered briefly in reaction to the prospect of AI tools making it easier for consumers to avoid unnecessary fees or low-interest deposit accounts that pad bank margins. But if AI agents become an important way to interact with financial decisions, banks will fight to control that pathway. Citi’s terms note that AI agents it provides can be used by customers without worrying about additional liability.
The reaction by banks is part of a broader trend among businesses of all stripes: AI labs promise that their agents will revolutionize the way people engage with a variety of service providers, then the service providers say “hold on a minute.” We’ve seen it in everything fromcar-hailingtofood service, and how these relationships play out will help determine which AI investments pay off.

Instagram’s ‘school safety’ push was also a way to get more teens on the app
Meta’s own internal documents show how ‘Project Gryffindor’ aimed to ‘fuel’ the acquisition of teen users.
Illustration: Kristen Radtke / The VergeEmma Roth
is a news writer who covers the streaming wars, consumer tech, crypto, social media, and much more. Previously, she was a writer and editor at MUO.
Meta’s initiative to make Instagram safer for schools stemmed from efforts to increase user “acquisition,” “friending,” and “invites,” accordingto a report from NPR. Internal documents revealed as part of a group ofchild safety lawsuitsagainst Metareference a“Project Gryffindor” — a school program that would “fuel organic and unattributed acquisition” of users.One internal presentation from November 2023says a school program would “give teens a new reason to join / find more value in IG [Instagram].”
The internal documents suggest Meta considered more goals than just teen safety when rolling out Instagram’s School Partnership Program, whichlaunchedtouting features to fast-track moderation reports from participating school districts. Metaexpanded this program in Septemberby creating dedicated channels where schools can share announcements with students and parents. It also adds school banners to profiles, as well as directories for clubs and teams.
Meta spokesperson Liza Crenshaw said in an emailed statement toThe Vergethat NPR’s story “completely mischaracterizes a positive program that helps thousands of U.S. schools protect their students online, communicate with them safely about extracurricular activities, and easily report safety issues.” Crenshaw adds that Meta doesn’t “want Instagram to be a distraction during class.”
The November 2023 document says that Meta’s “current strategy of relying on power user teens to get less active friends onto IG may not be effective if there are full communities of teens that have not yet joined IG.” Another2023 presentationquestions whether Meta can “use school networks as a lever for acquisition,” and says that structured school data could “help improve the ability to find friends and acquaintances,” for attracting teens who “don’t think their friends are on IG.”
In 2024, Meta started automatically putting users under 18 intomore restrictive teen accountswhile facing global scrutiny about the safety of its platforms. It later agreed to impose age verification, time limits, and an option to turn off personalized feeds to settle claims that itsplatforms are addictive.

How Meta used schools to boost teen Instagram use : NPRAccessibility links
How Meta used schools to boost teen Instagram useMeta said it launched its "school partnership program" to keep teens safe, but internal documents tell a different story.
Project Gryffindor: Meta's plan to get more school kids using Instagram
An aerial view of Meta headquarters on Jan. 29, 2025 in Menlo Park, Calif.Justin Sullivan/Getty Imageshide caption
toggle captioniJustin Sullivan/Getty Images
Internal Meta documents show the company planned to boost Instagram use among teens by targeting schools in an initiative it named "Project Gryffindor."
Theproject focusedon growing what it called "school communities" in the U.S. by encouraging teens to include their school banner on their profiles and establishing a student directory that allows users to see and connect with others from their school who use the platform.
Metalaunchedthe initiative in 2025, calling it a "school partnership program," and significantlyexpanded itin September 2026. The company said almost 17,000 schools had signed up for the program at the time.
Meta said the program sought to provide a safer experience on Instagram for children, including protecting them from bullying and online risks by allowing educators to report safety concerns to the company.
Meta, states agree to $17 billion settlement in child safety trial
Another feature gives school-related accounts the ability to post stories and notes visible to all verified students and parents in a school community. Meta said these features would help students and parents stay informed about happenings at school. The announcement gave an example of a school using the Instagram Stories feature to share a notice of basketball tryouts.
However, in internal documents prior to the program's public launch, the company discussed more explicitly commercial motivations for establishing school networks. In a 2024 presentation on Project Gryffindor, Meta said that embedding in schools was a way to increase user "acquisition," "friending" and "invites" to join Instagram. Gryffindor is one of the four Hogwarts school houses from theHarry Potterbooks.
"We believe network connections will fuel organic and unattributed acquisition," the project's presentation states, referring to adding new users.
Jury finds Meta and Google negligent in social media harms trial
In another internalpresentationfrom 2023, titled "Unlocking New Networks Through School Communities," Meta stated that its school program would "give teens a new reason to join / find more value in IG [Instagram]."
"Our current strategy of relying on power user teens to get less active friends onto IG may not be effective if there are full communities of teens that have not yet joined IG," the presentation stated.
The previously unreported Meta documents are part of evidence obtained by lawyers through discovery in a multidistrict lawsuit alleging that social media platforms are designed to be harmful to users under 18, and that the companies knew their products carried risks they failed to disclose. Meta, alongside TikTok, Google and Snap, are defendants in the cases, which were brought by children and their families, school districts and state attorneys general.
A cell phone locker is seen at Ronald McNair Sr. High School, Thursday, Aug. 7, 2025, in Atlanta.Mike Stewart/Associated Presshide caption
toggle captioniMike Stewart/Associated Press
Online safety experts interviewed by NPR said that rather than boosting online safety, Instagram's school partnership program could make teen users more vulnerable to mental health issues and increase their likelihood of being targeted by predators.
"Meta's own documents refer to this very program as a mere way to get more teens addicted to Instagram and Facebook," said Sacha Haworth, the executive director of the Tech Oversight Project, a nonprofit advocacy group focused on tech policy. "Meta's latest attempt to trojan-horse their tech into the school day shows the business strategy remains the same: maximize their profits at our kids' expense."
According to Paul Raffile, a cybersecurity investigator, Instagram's school partnership program could create privacy and security vulnerabilities to teens' accounts that could be "a loophole that scammers, sextortion scammers, as well as groomers, would obviously exploit."
Using schools to recruit teen Instagram users
Meta has long focused on boosting Instagram's popularity among teenagers. The social media giant viewed the slowdown in teen Instagram user growth since TikTok's US launch in 2018 as "an existential threat for not just IG [Instagram] but the company overall," according to other internal documents submitted as evidence in the multidistrict lawsuit.
Internal documents show that as early as 2015, the company was making plans to form relationships with schools to acquire new teen users.
One companypresentationfrom 2023 stated: "Our competitors in social connection are leveraging school integrations as a way to keep in touch with their community. Can we take things a step further and use school networks as a lever for acquisitions?"Snapchatalso has a school and college community program, where users can apply to have their school badge displayed on their profile, which hasfaced criticismfor facilitating inappropriate posts and bullying.
Another Meta document discussed how acquiring teen users would have the knock-on effect of introducing younger children to the platform. "Teens strongly influenced preteens' understanding of what and how frequently to share on Instagram," the document said. Meta's own policy states that Instagram users must be atleast 13 years oldto have an account.
In another internal Metapresentationfocused on the long-term retention of users on Facebook, a bullet point stated: "Tweens (approximate age 10-12) are special. People who join Facebook as tweens have the highest long term retention out of all age groups." Facebook also has a minimum age requirement of 13 to use the platform.
Targeting schools may also have served as a strategy to increase the amount of time teens spent on Instagram. In a2025 legal brieffiled on behalf of school districts and boards of education across the country, lawyers cited a 2015 internal comment from a Meta employee describing the company's engagement goals: "One of the things we need to optimize for is sneaking a look at your phone under your desk in the middle of Chemistry :)."

Rogue Agents Hacked His Company. Why Is Clément Delangue So Optimistic About AI? | WIREDSkip to main content
Clément Delangue, CEOof the open-source AI companyHugging Face, may go down in history as one of the first people ever attacked by a rogue AI agent. His company, which hosts millions of AI models and datasets, was breached in July when hundreds of agents being tested byOpenAIbroke free from their sandbox and went on a hacking spree.
As the agents worked at superhuman speed to probe and exploit systems, Hugging Face confronted a bewildering deluge of data. The company’s engineers were only able to analyze the attack by using an open-weight model called GLM 5.2 from aChinese company called Z.ai.
Delangue moved to the US more than a decade ago, “barely speaking English,” and built Hugging Face into a platform that supports tens of millions of AI developers. The fresh-faced Frenchman, who dresses even more like a skater than most AI execs, says the summer attack highlighted the value of open-weight models, which unlike ChatGPT or Claude can be downloaded and run by anyone.
Despite championing the democratization of AI, however, Hugging Face was acquired by one of the industry’s biggest players, Nvidia, for $12.93 billion in September. When I caught up with Delangue recently, that was the subject of my first question.
This interview has been edited for length and clarity.
CLÉMENT DELANGUE:We need more resources to give open-source AI a chance. It has grown really well in the past few years and has become a really credible alternative to closed-source APIs. But the field is still dominated by closed-source.
We’re gonna have the Anthropic IPO in a few weeks. They basically went from zero to a top five or top 10 most valuable company in the world in a few years. I don't think that's ever happened before.
Does Anthropic's IPO suggest the closed approach is winning?
It’s hard to say. I've always said that there is a very strong natural tendency for AI to concentrate capabilities and wealth. People haven't internalized how much of the future compute capacity has already been reserved by a few companies. Talent, compute, resources—these all fuel the natural tendency for AI to be dominated by a few closed-source labs.
Let’s talk about the attack. When did you first realize Hugging Face was being hacked by a group of AI agents?
At the beginning, it didn't go to the top of our priority list. It just wasn't bad enough to really trigger that. The goal was pretty narrow and wasn’t deemed to be very dangerous or damaging. But it was raising questions. Especially the number of actions taken compared to the narrowness of the goal. It was surprising to us, and we couldn't really fit it into a familiar pattern. That's why we started investigating.
And you used the Chinese model called GLM to investigate.
I actually think that 95 percent of the risks are being created by a few companies that are pushing the frontier behind closed doors. And 95 percent of the protection or defense is going to be done by the open-source ecosystem.
Does the US need its own open-weight models—ones as powerful as GLM, DeepSeek, Kimi, orQwen?
Yeah, I think it's very, very important for sovereignty, for understanding AI, and for academia. It’s kind of weird that most academic labs have to use Chinese models because they’re the ones that are open. If you go to Stanford or MIT, you have no choice but to use the Chinese open-weight models.
There is some momentum, but I don't think it's enough. I think there's a lot more to do. A lot more investment is needed.
The best open-source non-Chinese models are actually coming from outside of the US. Right from France, Mistral; Cohere from Canada; South Korea is starting to do more and more. But it’s still pretty far from what the US could do.
Perhaps we don’t need to panic about AI agents, but what about the idea of AI escaping human control due to recursive self-improvement?
You use a computer to write code. There's already some form of self-improvement in using the tools to build more tools. Now the question is how fast it accelerates. One thing that a lot of people realized this summer is that keeping AI behind closed doors in a few labs isn't actually safer. For recursive self-improvement, I think openness is a way to understand, follow, and regulate if we need to regulate.
Can we talk about theMicroduck? I’m a bit obsessed.
Oh yeah, it's so fun, no? We're probably gonna sell over 50,000 of them this year. It's probably the most popular robot of the year.
We haven't talked about this much, but AI was really the unlock for the robot. We had the design for two years, but the problem was that when it fell, it couldn’t get up. And then at some point with reinforcement learning, one of our software engineers managed to get the Microduck to get itself back up.
At the end of the day, how do you convince people to take an interest in open-source AI?
Think of a world where two or three companies could write software and nobody else. That would be incredibly scary. It would mean that the whole world would be controlled by two or three companies. And unfortunately, that's kind of the direction that AI is taking right now.
Can open-source AI compete with something as capable as Claude or ChatGPT?
Yes, especially with agents. Many companies have shown that when you post-train your own model for your own use case, you get frontier—or even better than frontier—performance at a fraction of the cost.
Do you think we are getting close to AGI?
I struggle a little bit with the meaning of that. Obviously the technology is progressing incredibly fast, and it’s more and more capable. I just don’t necessarily find it super useful to always compare AI to human capabilities. But if we’re getting to AGI or to superintelligence, it’s incredibly important that it’s as distributed as possible. The last thing you want is to have it concentrated in a few corporations.

Thousands of customers at major US banks, including JP Morgan Chase, Wells Fargo and Bank of America, reported trouble accessing services, though Chase said its issue has now been resolved.

The issue comes after a string of unrelated technical problems, includinga massive Microsoft outageand a network failure thatgrounded all US flights.
In addition, United Airlines also reported a "widespread system outage".
The problems with the banks started on Monday afternoon. There were almost 5,000 reports of problems with Chase Bank's services, according to the Downdetector website.
Clients reported issues accessing their online accounts, viewing balances and performing transactions, like bank transfers and wire transfers, according to the BBC's US media partner CBS News, though Chase Bank told the BBC that customers still had access to their accounts and funds.
A Chase Bank customer in Texas told CBS that he could not deposit a check at a Dallas branch on Monday, reporting that he was told his transaction could not be completed. He said a bank teller told the customer in front of him that the "system was down" but did not provide additional details.

The bank, a subsidiary of JP Morgan Chase, serves more than 86m customers at 5,000 branches across the US, as well as 7.4m small businesses, according to the company's webpage. It is also the top credit card issuer in the US.

fact_units.text: More banks says customers using AI agents are on their own — even if they get hacked | TechCrunch
More banks says customers using AI agents are on their own — even if they get hacked
Tim Fernholz9:32 AM PST · November 18, 2026

Citibank, the third largest commercial bank in the United States, changed its terms of service this week, telling customers who use third-party AI tools for personal finance that anything that goes wrong is their problem — even if they get hacked.

AI agents, ranging from frontier lab models to purpose-built personal finance tools, can be given the credentials to your bank account and other online financial portals, with the idea that they can analyze spending and investment decisions, offer advice, and even handle transactions and bill payments.

But financial institutions aren’t thrilled with the unreliable AI actors in their systems, and are telling customers that they won’t be held responsible for reversing an intentional or unintentional transaction made by automated assistants.

“As third-party AI tools become more widely available, we want customers to understand the risks associated with sharing banking credentials or authorizing those tools to access their accounts,” a Citi spokesperson told TechCrunch.

“We recently updated our Online User Agreement to provide greater clarity about those risks and to reinforce that customers who choose to grant account access to third-party AI agents are responsible for activities conducted through those agents.”
JPMorgan andBank of America, the two largest banks in the country, announced similar policies last month.
And PNC, the eight largest bank, changed its terms today.

Citi’s update goes beyond telling customers that they are responsible for anything their agents may do; it also informs them that if the AI tools leaks their credentials or is hacked, the customer will be responsible for anything hackers do with their account.
Banking giant Citizens similarly emailed its customers this week, warning that they are also on the hook for anything their AI assistant does, according to an email seen by TechCrunch.

As AI startups look for more revenue, breaking into personal finance presents an attractive opportunity for companies to add value for customers and wet their beaks in the stream of fees generated by the sector.
But if consumers are already leery of sharing their email or chat records with an AI agent, bank and brokerage accounts offer a new trust challenge.
Anthropic’s approach is telling: Thepersonal finance toolit launched earlier this month is explicitly billed as “read-only” and “can’t move, manage, or invest your money.”
Beyond cybersecurity concerns, banks also view efforts to enter their franchise as a competitive threat.
Markets shuddered briefly in reaction to the prospect of AI tools making it easier for consumers to avoid unnecessary fees or low-interest deposit accounts that pad bank margins.
But if AI agents become an important way to interact with financial decisions, banks will fight to control that pathway.
Citi’s terms note that AI agents it provides can be used by customers without worrying about additional liability.

The reaction by banks is part of a broader trend among businesses of all stripes: AI labs promise that their agents will revolutionize the way people engage with a variety of service providers, then the service providers say “hold on a minute.” We’ve seen it in everything fromcar-hailingtofood service, and how these relationships play out will help determine which AI investments pay off.

GTA 6 reviews say highly-anticipated game is a masterpiece - BBC News
Review scores for GTA 6 are a fairytale ending after years of development
ByTom RichardsonandRiyah Collins,BBC Newsbeat
Published18 November 2026, 12:22 GMT
After 13 years of waiting, record-breaking trailers and lengthy delays, critics have given their answer to one of the year's biggest questions.
Does Grand Theft Auto 6, surely the most anticipated game of all time, live up to the hype?
According to the first reviews, it's a resounding yes.
Metacritic, which aggregates reviews from critics, averages it at99 out of 100,external- tying with Nintendo's The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, which has held the record since 1998.
Reviewers overwhelmingly agreed the open-world action game was an ambitious, ground-breaking title that was well worth the wait.
Not everyone is enjoying the glowing praise - with some posters to online forums objecting to what one called "the ultra fan-boy hype."
But there is no question the reviewers have been effusive with their praise, with gaming websiteIGN,externalbranding GTA 6 "unprecedented", "unbelievable" and "unmissable".
Meanwhile in its five star review, Eurogamer said makers Rockstar had "pushed back the horizon of video games once again" with its graphics, storytelling and world building.
"The awe is all part of the point, of course, and GTA 6 is nothing if not truly awesome,"reviewer Chris Tapsell wrote,external, but he added "there are also nits to pick".
For TheNew York Times,externalone of those nits was whether the realism of the game might dull the fun chaos of its predecessors.
Reviewer Yussef Cole said GTA 6 had "matured beyond its memorable car crashes and stickups" with consequences to every action.
But "some of my favourite moments have been careening through streets with squad cars in hot pursuit," he wrote.
Critics say the relationship between Jason and Lucia is central to the game
The graphics of the game were hotly anticipated and so far have not disappointed critics, withThe Guardian,externaldescribing Leonida, the setting inspired by Miami, as "so lifelike that at times it beggars belief".
And the relationship between the lead characters, Jason and Lucia, has also stunned critics.
"They feel like real people rather than puppets dancing to your whim," The Guardian's Keza MacDonald wrote, adding: "I found it impossible not to care for them".
Writing for Forbes,external, Paul Tassi said: "I can't say I've ever seen a better video game relationship than the one they share".
TheWashington Post,externalsaid GTA 6 "raises the bar at every level", whileBloomberg,external's Jason Schreier called it a "masterpiece" in his five star review.
"It's hard not to be astonished by what Rockstar has done here," he wrote. "There's nothing else like it.
"While playing this game, I often found myself wondering how it even exists."
Rockstar hasn't revealed the cost of the game, but some estimates put the figure north of $1bn (£760m).
GTA 6 is the most hotly anticipated videogame ever
Gaming journalist Jordan Middler is one of the lucky few in the UK who got early access from Rockstar and tells BBC Newsbeat it is the "game of a generation".
He'd played for about 100 hours by the time he hit the credits and says he still has so much to do.
Middler did spot one negative though - he found the game can "slow down" because of how much is going on.
He also says it is "long overdue" that there is a female lead in Lucia.
"The way previous GTA games have dealt with women has been a boys' club approach," he says.
"Introducing Lucia and not making her some kind of token character, she just fits in completely... and she will quickly become a fan favourite without question."
The Game Awards - the most watched ceremony of its kind in the industry - gave players a teaser of the critical reception when its 2026 nominations were revealed on Tuesday.
And despite having not released at the time, GTA 6 was the most-nominated title.
It will be up for eight prizes, including game of the year and best music.
The nomination of Manni L Perez in the best performance category confirmed wide speculation that she is the actress behind main character Lucia in GTA 6 - a fact Rockstar hadn't previously officially confirmed.
The jury for the event is largely made up of gaming journalists around the world, who would have received advanced copies for review.
Some, though, have questioned how a game that has just been released has garnered such positive reviews and award nominations.
There is a view in some online forums that the hype around the game has got out of control as, with one poster commenting: "I think everyone's tired of hearing about this game - I don't even want to play it anymore."
It appears so far, however, that is likely to be very much a minority view.
Additional reporting by Jasmine Sandhar

Grand Theft Auto VI does something impossible — it lives up to the hype
Thirteen years later, Rockstar has crafted a worthy successor to GTA V and the new standard-bearer for open-world games.
Image: Rockstar GamesPart OfGrand Theft Auto VI has arrivedsee all updatesAndrew Webster
is an entertainment editor covering streaming, virtual worlds, and every single Pokémon video game. Andrew joined The Verge in 2012, writing over 4,000 stories.
How do you follow a game likeGrand Theft Auto V? Thirteen years ago, Rockstar’s crime-fueled epic went on to redefine what an open-world game could be and became an enormous success, selling more than 230 million copies across three generations of game consoles. It sits just behindTetrisandMinecrafton the list of the best-selling games of all time, andits lucrative online modehas helped it remain popular for well over a decade.
That level of success has allowed Rockstar to take its time with a sequel, which has further increased the hype around the nextGTA. A series ofmajor leaksanddelaysonly exacerbated this. At a time whenmuch of the video game industry is struggling,the next edition ofGTAstands alone, a cultural moment so big (almost)everybody has been forced to get out of the way. The buildup toGrand Theft Auto VI’s launch is unlike anything the game industry has ever seen.
Even more remarkable? The game was actually worth the wait.
At this point I’ve spent nearly 80 hours in Leonida,GTA VI’s fictional take on Florida. And what I’ve experienced is a game that combines the wide-open freedom offered inGTA Vwith the remarkable level of immersion from the studio’s 2018 releaseRed Dead Redemption 2, while also improving on both qualities. At the same time, it’s also the most matureGTAgame Rockstar has ever made, merging the criminal antics and absurdist humor the series is known for with a love story that gives you new ways to interact with the world and new reasons for wanting to push forward. This is theGTAgame the studio has been building toward for its entire existence.
Let’s start with that new premise.GTA Vintroduced the idea of multiple protagonists to the series, andVItakes that concept in a different direction. It’s a Bonnie and Clyde-inspired story about Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, two small-time criminals who meet while, of course, stealing a car. It’s the mostGTA-possible meet-cute. The idea is that you can play as both characters individually and also build their relationship over the course of the game. Things start out relatively slow. At the outset, Lucia is in prison, and you play solely as Jason, getting things ready for when she gets out. You can fix up your ramshackle house — that involves actually nailing down new stairs and rolling out paint on the walls — and also start building up a nest egg through means that are not exactly legal.
Jason and Lucia’s relationship grows naturally over the course of the game, but it’s also a slow buildup to becoming the inseparable pair they were by the end of my playthrough.GTA VIapproaches most of the experience with confident and deliberate pacing. Even when you control them individually, the characters are often together, either just hanging out or partnering for a crime. And being able to play as both is one of the game’s standout features. But I didn’t get to that point in the game until almost 17 hours in. Before that, you play as both leads mostly solo, learning who they are as people, before you’re given free rein to switch between the two.
‘It’s a risk’: How Rockstar built the most detailed (and romantic) GTA yet
What’s great about the premise is how seamlessly it fits with what you’re actually doing in the game. There’s some bigger-picture stuff that I won’t spoil, but generally speaking, the main goal inGTA VIis to make a lot of money so that Jason and Lucia can get out of the criminal life for good and retire somewhere comfortably. And outside of the big story missions, you’re largely free to choose how you go about that. You can rob jewelry stores, steal cars, raid drug dens, or even search for hidden treasure at the bottom of the sea. Over the course of the game you’ll also meet different criminals who serve as fences, so you can sell them whatever you’ve got to build up your savings account. Sometimes they’ll even text you targets that are particularly lucrative.
The structure feels natural and gives you a lot of freedom in how you play. I’m not a big fan of armed robbery, for instance. There are just so many things that can go wrong, and I almost always end up killing some innocent bystander when I try to escape. But I love getaway chases, and so stealing cars became my main form of income. Most importantly, though, this structure gives you a lot of reasons to go out in the world and explore. The missions take you all over the map — which is actually entirely accessible from the very beginning, if you choose to play that way — including not only the bright lights of the Miami-like Vice City, but also tourist beaches, swamps, trailer parks, and a wild variety of other locations, each with its own landscape to explore and characters to meet.
To be clear: Despite being larger, more mature, and more lifelike, this is still very muchGTA. This is a game about chaos and crime. This comes across in a few ways. First, there are those smaller missions where you never really know how things will play out. The cashier at the pawn shop you’re robbing might have a shotgun, or you might accidentally smash into a big rig during a high-speed getaway. The world itself is full of unpredictable moments that force you to think on your feet. Several times I stopped my car to talk to an NPC whose vehicle broke down on the side of the road. In one instance the driver just swore at me to leave her alone. In another, I got pulled into an entire storyline involving a delivery driver who needed help to keep her AI chatbot manager off her back. I delivered her packages and ended up dealing with everything from porch pirates to tigers.
The structure feels natural and gives you a lot of freedom in how you play.
There are also the multistep heists, which return fromGTA Vmore intricate and complex. These are the big scores and involve several different missions: You spend time getting the right gear and gathering all

I Will Never Stop Playing ‘Grand Theft Auto’ | WIREDSkip to main content
I knewGTAwas something special even before my mom punched me in the face.
This was an accident. She’s not much of a gamer, so the controls on the PS5 version ofGrand Theft Auto Onlineare a bit of a mystery to her. She pressed the circle button, and her in-game character swung a giant punch that caught my character right in the head. Blood splattered. My mom cried out. My brother and I howled with laughter. She’d only been playing for a couple of hours, and she was already punching her kids. What a violent nightmare these games were.
GTAhas been a part of my life since I was way too young to be playing it. My brother and I, aged 9 and 11-ish, discoveredGrand Theft Auto 3at a cool cousin’s house. We’d sit there, enraptured, cackling like gremlins and passing the controller back and forth every time one of us got WASTED. I remember wondering if video games could ever get more realistic.
Flash forward a couple of decades, andGrand Theft Auto VIreleases on Thursday, a game poised to be the most lifelike, expansive title in the series—maybe in all of gaming. (The game apparently has a system for tracking your empathy.) It also has a real chance of becoming perhaps the highest-grossing entertainment property of all time.
Still fromGrand Theft Auto VI.Photograph: Courtesy of Rockstar Games
People are very excited about this thing, so much so that there’s been hand-wringing about workplace productivity dropping because some12.5 million peopleare taking time off to play the game. (It’s me; I am part of the problem. Please don’t tell my boss.)
Does that feel like too much hype for a video game? Not to me. Not whenGrand Theft Autohas always been such a presence at very pivotal points in my life. It’s been much more than a flashy violence simulator.
My brother and I were the target demographic for these games. Vaguely inspired by gangster shoot-em-ups likeScarface, the GTA games have long been vehicles for male power fantasies. We got into them because you could run around and blow stuff up. Be chaotic. It was a good place to do that in, rather than, you know, the real world.
We also weren’t always that friendly when we entered adulthood. Lots of siblings aren’t all that close, especially as adults. When you live far away for long enough, phone calls and occasional visits can only do so much. The distance can be hard to close.
That really changed for us during theCovid-19 pandemic. My brother and I lived hundreds of miles apart. As it did for many people, playing games becamea way to stay connected. The best conversations usually happen while doing something like chatting on a long drive, going on a walk, or hanging out at the beach. You couldn’t really do that in theendless Zoom partiesCovid unleashed upon the world, where you’d all sit there, talking one at a time, not quite making eye contact on the screen.
Grand Theft Auto Onlineproved to be a rich environment for finding those kinds of activities. I think it’s the closest anythinghas ever gotten to feelinglike an actualmetaverse, where you can do just about whatever you want.
If you’ve playedGTAO, you’ve probably rage-quit after getting bombed by an adolescent fighter jet pilot dressed like the prison Joker for the eighth time. That’s fair. But my brother and I usually made the mostly unconscious decision not to fight back. We’d just … hang out. Drive around. Watch the sunset. Spend hours in the in-game nightclubs, listening to real-life musicians play hour-long sets made specifically for the game. We’d go to the stores and curate outfits that felt snazzy.
Really, we are just playing dolls. GTA is a sandbox, after all, and it became the perfect space to mess around without worrying about any real stakes.
“We were brothers before, sure, but we weren’t like adult friends,” my brother told me when I asked him aboutGTA. “This gave us a way to spend time together and really learn more about what each other’s personality really is.”
We’ve made friends with a group in Australia who shared our approach, just hanging out in this vast virtual world and having casual conversations with the people around us. We’ve managed to convince our parents, who have never played games before, to join us. My mom—who once took our Nintendo 64 cartridge ofGoldenEye 007and smashed it with a hammer because she thought video games would make us violent—now runs around with us inGTA Online, pummeling tailgaters’ cars with a baseball bat. Despite the distance, we can spend time together in something that feels close to a real-life hang, one where we accidentally get smacked with the bat sometimes too.
It’s been a blast, and all that time spent in this virtual world starts to bleed over into the real world. I’ve sought out real-life shows of artists on the soundtrack. Sometimes an outfit would feel snazzy enough that we’d later try to replicate it in real life. Just a minute ago, I was shooting my way out of a cocaine deal gone wrong, darting behind furniture for cover. Now I’m sitting on the floor of my home, working through the instructions to construct an Ikea-style coffee table with my partner. A tiny heart with a plus sign pops up, showing that our relationship is stronger for this quotidian domestic effort.
This is the contrast at the heart ofGrand Theft Auto VI, a game that seems to revel in both action movie bombast and the mundanities of everyday life for an up-and-coming young criminal couple.
The reimagined and expanded Vice City is still the grand, crude, satirical criminal playground you’d expect after 25 years of 3D Grand Theft Auto games. And that world is as full, detailed, technically impressive, and polished as you would expect after this latest installmentreceived a reported billion-dollar budgetand roughly a decade of development work involving thousands of Rockstar staffers.

Taken together, the juxtaposition lends a sense of surreal hyperreality to the goings-on in Vice City and its environs. Each of the game’s two sides gives the other a chance to breathe, forming a series of emotional peaks and valleys that stretch across a truly gargantuan amount of detailed simulation and pure gaming content.

A large part of why this works so well is Jason and Lucia, the dual protagonists whose relationship drives the story. While that relationship starts off a bit awkwardly—thanks chiefly to Lucia’s brief prison stint—it quickly develops into a true criminal and life partnership. Both sides of the relationship are driven by a mutual desire to move up in the criminal world and eventually settle down to a legit family life, if they can just earn enough from the next big score.

Grand Theft Auto VI Review: a vicious, romantic crime masterpieceAn inspired synthesis of violent satire and contemplative storytelling,Grand Theft Auto VIis more mature and ambitious than any prior game in the record-breaking franchise.
Grand Theft Auto VI is a grounded love story, a gonzo crime thriller and a gaming triumph
Grand Theft Auto VIprotagonists, Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval, against the backdrop of the Miami-inspired Vice City.Rockstar Gameshide caption
I want to tell you about the time I saw Bigfoot. I want to tell you about sitting in the rain on a city street in a muscle car and prepping to rob a bank while lightning split the sky between high-rise condo towers in the distance and the drum fill fromIn The Air Tonightplayed on the radio. I want to tell you about gunfights and fistfights, the perfect satire of radio commercials and how the sunrise looks over Ocean Beach. But more than any of that, I want to tell you about the time an alligator bit my mom.
It happened in the backyard of an abandoned house with a rotting inground pool. My mom, Mia Caminos (mother of Lucia Caminos, one of the two leads in Rockstar Games'Grand Theft Auto VI, probably the most highly anticipated video game sequel of all time), was thrilled by the pool. Standing there, amid the artfully rendered weeds and trash, she spread her arms and told me to use my imagination, to see her vision for this ruin of a house with its upmarket water feature, in a scabby neighborhood on the outskirts of Vice City. She speaks in tones of increasingly frantic desperation because she has already put money down on this house, sight unseen. All of her money, actually, in hopes of flipping it and selling it fast to keep her startup real estate business afloat.
Lucia begins her epic as a petty criminal.Rockstar Gameshide caption
The pool is still half full of water. There's a dirty, sodden mattress floating in it. And as if this is the main thing standing between her and success, Mia is fixated on getting it out of the pool.
And, dutifully, I do. Playing as Lucia, I grab hold, mash buttons, help my mom drag away the wet, heavy, stinking mattress. And just as we get it up and over the lip of the pool that's going to be the thing that makes this wreck of a house suddenly desirable – that's when the alligator lunges out of the murky water, grabs my mom by the arm and tries to drag her back in.
This is a story about folly, fixation, unrealistic expectations of success at the ass-end of late capitalism, and the vicious, whip-crack cruelty of predators who lie in wait for anyone trying to improve a terrible situation.
But then I shoot the alligator in the head before it can eat my mom. Because this isalsoa story about violence, and how sometimes (maybe all the times), the loud, cathartic rip of gunfire is the only solution left for people who have already lost so much and can't bear to see one more thing taken from them.
It's a story about my mom and an alligator, sure.
Grand Theft Auto VIreturns to Vice City and its Florida-inspired environs.Rockstar Gameshide caption
But let's back up a little. For anyone who has somehow missed the shrieking, neon-and-swamp-water marketing onslaught over the past several days, weeks, months and years,Grand Theft Auto VIis the newest release from Rockstar Games. It is a Bonnie and Clyde love story, a knife-edged satire of modern American culture and politics, an unapologetic murder simulator, a love letter to 50 years of crime movies, and a thoughtful, emotional meditation on the sacrifices, small and large, that we make for family. A massive open world game set in the fictional state of Leonida (based on the very real state of Florida), it represents a return to a location that Rockstar hasn't visited in-depth since its 2002 release ofGTA: Vice City, and is the first new game in the franchise sinceGTA5launched in 2013. According to estimates, italready earned over $1.5 billion in pre-salesand will likely make a total of$3 to $5 billion in its first week, which could make it the largest single entertainment product launch ever.
Fans have been waiting yearsfor it. They have createdlibraries worth of loreand theories and dissected trailers frame-by-frame. To discount the overheated environment into which this singular work of art is being released would be doing a disservice both to it and the legions of salivating prognosticators who have made guessing the number ofbird species included in-game, or speculating on the square mileage of its map, their entire personalities.
While Vice City remains the game's hub, most of itsmapis actually rural or wild.Rockstar Gameshide caption
Now, though, they know it all. We all do. We know thatGTA6is expansive, covering everything from the Keys (where the game starts) to the hilly, forested north, with Vice City in all its grimy, pastel-colored splendor at the beating heart of it. It is a playground, equal parts gorgeous and maniacal, and in all that space the developers have given us a thousand different things to do. You can rob a bank or take a bike ride, go fishing, hunt trophy animals, visit strip clubs, rob random civilians, street race, fly drones, eat a sandwich, work out, manage your family savings account, jump a sports car off the top of a building, steal a plane, punch out a convenience store clerk, fight a bear or, yes, just wander out toward the horizon and study the birds. And while some of that is fun and all of it is diverting (at least for a little while), none of it is the ostensible point. The game-y part of the game — the hundred extras and time-wasters that players have come to expect from open-world projects in general, and GTA specifically — is not what makes it matter.
Whatmattersis Mia and the alligator, Lucia and the gun. It's the multi-pronged, exquisitely balanced narrative about poverty and rigged systems that makes it hard to turn away fromGTAwhile you're playing and impossible not to think about when you're away.

fact_units.text: GTA 6 reviews say highly-anticipated game is a masterpiece - BBC News
Review scores for GTA 6 are a fairytale ending after years of development
Published18 November 2026, 12:22 GMT
After 13 years of waiting, record-breaking trailers and lengthy delays, critics have given their answer to one of the year's biggest questions.
Does Grand Theft Auto 6, surely the most anticipated game of all time, live up to the hype?
According to the first reviews, it's a resounding yes.
Metacritic, which aggregates reviews from critics, averages it at99 out of 100,external- tying with Nintendo's The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, which has held the record since 1998.
Reviewers overwhelmingly agreed the open-world action game was an ambitious, ground-breaking title that was well worth the wait.
Not everyone is enjoying the glowing praise - with some posters to online forums objecting to what one called "the ultra fan-boy hype."
But there is no question the reviewers have been effusive with their praise, with gaming websiteIGN,externalbranding GTA 6 "unprecedented", "unbelievable" and "unmissable".
Meanwhile in its five star review, Eurogamer said makers Rockstar had "pushed back the horizon of video games once again" with its graphics, storytelling and world building.
"The awe is all part of the point, of course, and GTA 6 is nothing if not truly awesome,"reviewer Chris Tapsell wrote,external, but he added "there are also nits to pick".
For TheNew York Times,externalone of those nits was whether the realism of the game might dull the fun chaos of its predecessors.
Reviewer Yussef Cole said GTA 6 had "matured beyond its memorable car crashes and stickups" with consequences to every action.
But "some of my favourite moments have been careening through streets with squad cars in hot pursuit," he wrote.
Critics say the relationship between Jason and Lucia is central to the game

The graphics of the game were hotly anticipated and so far have not disappointed critics, withThe Guardian,externaldescribing Leonida, the setting inspired by Miami, as "so lifelike that at times it beggars belief".
And the relationship between the lead characters, Jason and Lucia, has also stunned critics.
"They feel like real people rather than puppets dancing to your whim," The Guardian's Keza MacDonald wrote, adding: "I found it impossible not to care for them".
Writing for Forbes,external, Paul Tassi said: "I can't say I've ever seen a better video game relationship than the one they share".
TheWashington Post,externalsaid GTA 6 "raises the bar at every level", whileBloomberg,external's Jason Schreier called it a "masterpiece" in his five star review.
"It's hard not to be astonished by what Rockstar has done here," he wrote.
"While playing this game, I often found myself wondering how it even exists."
Rockstar hasn't revealed the cost of the game, but some estimates put the figure north of $1bn (£760m).
GTA 6 is the most hotly anticipated videogame ever
Gaming journalist Jordan Middler is one of the lucky few in the UK who got early access from Rockstar and tells BBC Newsbeat it is the "game of a generation".
He'd played for about 100 hours by the time he hit the credits and says he still has so much to do.
Middler did spot one negative though - he found the game can "slow down" because of how much is going on.
He also says it is "long overdue" that there is a female lead in Lucia.
"The way previous GTA games have dealt with women has been a boys' club approach," he says.
"Introducing Lucia and not making her some kind of token character, she just fits in completely...
and she will quickly become a fan favourite without question."
The Game Awards - the most watched ceremony of its kind in the industry - gave players a teaser of the critical reception when its 2026 nominations were revealed on Tuesday.
And despite having not released at the time, GTA 6 was the most-nominated title.
It will be up for eight prizes, including game of the year and best music.

The nomination of Manni L Perez in the best performance category confirmed wide speculation that she is the actress behind main character Lucia in GTA 6 - a fact Rockstar hadn't previously officially confirmed.
The jury for the event is largely made up of gaming journalists around the world, who would have received advanced copies for review.
Some, though, have questioned how a game that has just been released has garnered such positive reviews and award nominations.

There is a view in some online forums that the hype around the game has got out of control as, with one poster commenting: "I think everyone's tired of hearing about this game - I don't even want to play it anymore."
It appears so far, however, that is likely to be very much a minority view.

House Democrats Are Officially Coming for Trump’s Orbit | WIREDSkip to main content
Donald Trump Jr.was barefoot and beaming when a photographer snapped agroup pictureof him, his new bride, and his 30-or-so wedding party guests on a private island in the Bahamas last May. But that party—which was reportedlypaid for by a Russian oligarch—has since turned into alegal and political headache.
In a letter sent Wednesday, the incoming head of the House Oversight Committee has directed the president’s son to preserve all records related to his “lavish wedding celebrations” and his many business ventures, too.
That demand is a key step in any serious Congressional probe, and one sign among many that Democratic investigators are going after the president’s family in the new term following their massive wins in the election earlier this month.
Representative Robert Garcia, the incoming head of the House Oversight Committee, also issued similar record-preservation requests to Eric Trump along with Donald Trump Jr., as cofounders of the wildly controversial crypto firm World Liberty Financial, and their brother-in-law Jared Kushner, who runs a Saudi-backed investment firm while serving as a presidential envoy to the Middle East. Garcia even sent a notice to Donald Trump Jr.’s onetime fiancée Kimberly Guilfoyle, who’s been involved in apay-for-access scandalof her own.
Garcia also sent record-retention letters to White House chief of staff Stephen Miller, for his role in directing the immigration raids that havekilled at least six peopleanddetained more than 500 US citizens; Trust for the National Mall CEO Catherine Townsend, for the $600 million in private and public money spent on the White House ballroom; and vice president JD Vance and attorney general Todd Blanche, for their roles, the letters state, in the alleged cover-up of the Epstein files. Other figures from the last year and a half of the Trump administration were listed, including former Department of Homeland Security chief Kristi Noem, her top aide Corey Lewandowski, and recently departed White House chief of staff Susie Wiles.
“As the President has said, he's willing to work with anyone to continue delivering victories for hardworking Americans. If Democrats choose to pursue sham investigations and radical left policies, they are choosing to work against the American people,” White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis tells WIRED. A representative for the Trump family did not immediately respond to a request for comment for this story.
After they won control of the House and Senate in the midterm elections, Democrats made it plain that they were going to be beyond aggressive in ramping up their investigations. (“They are going to need to plant new forests for all of the subpoenas we'll be printing,” Senator Ed Markeyquipped.) The target set for those probes is beginning to come into focus more clearly, and the Democrats appear to be starting with the Trump family, who have made a killing in thepresident’s second term.
Now that they have the added resources and authority that come with being in the majority, Garcia and other Democrats want to dig into that growing fortune and who contributed to it.
Senator Richard Blumenthal, the ranking member of the Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, has been looking into World Liberty and other Trump family crypto projects “for 18 months,” as a recent letter to the firm noted. Senator Elizabeth Warren has repeatedly called for investigations into World Liberty’s “national security risks,” including sales of its token to alleged North Korean hackers and Russian money launderers. Representative Ro Khanna wants to know more about thesecret saleof 49 percent of World Liberty to funds controlled by SheikhTahnoun bin Zayed al Nahyan, the United Arab Emirates’ intelligence chief, and whether that sale had anything to do with the Trump administration’s decision to allow the sale of advanced AI chips to Abu Dhabi.
World Liberty has been particularly lucrative for the Trumps; according to Forbes, it added at one pointmore than $300 millionto the president’s accounts. “It’s troubling that Congress might baselessly target a compliant company that has dedicated itself to expanding access to the US dollar when there are a plethora of issues afflicting the American public that need to be addressed,” World Liberty spokesperson David Wachsman tells WIRED.
World Liberty is only one family business among many that has gone through a boom cycle in the past few years. Donald Trump Jr.’s venture capital firm, 1789, went from a few hundred million under management to somewhere around$4 billion. The Trump Organization has real estate development deals underway fromBucharest to Bali.
The sudden influx of cash, Garcia notes in his letters, “raises serious concerns” that the deals are essentially “contributions to President Trump and his family in exchange for government action on behalf of the wealthy and well connected. Access to preferential treatment, federal secrets, regulatory law enforcement leniency, and the president and senior officials appears to trace back to suspicious activity associated with these schemes.”
The Trumps and their representatives have repeatedly insisted they’ve done nothing to merit this kind of scrutiny, other than have the wrong last name. “We've been dealing with the conflict-of-interest stuff for years,” Donald Trump Jr. told CNBC at a World Liberty Finance event at Mar-a-Lago in February. “Frankly, it's gotten old.”
The Russian oligarch who paid for Donald Trump Jr.’s wedding party later claimed the president’s sonreimbursed him. “There is no evidence that any member of the Trump family ever sought to influence government policy or sought preferential treatment or government intervention to advance their personal or business interests,” Alan Garten, the Trump Organization’s chief legal officer,told this reporterprior to the election.
The pushback from Trumpworld has grown more intense since the Democrats’ midterm sweep. Aaron Reitz, the US attorney for the Southern District of Texas and a MAGA die-hard, sent a document-preservation letter of his own to Warren, accusing her of “terrorizing” Big Tech executives with her promises of investigation.
The White House even claimed that overly aggressive oversight might itself be a crime. “The Administration,” counsel to the president Will Scharf wrote to Garcia after the election, “will not be extorted.”

Hakeem Jeffries nominated to be US Speaker of the House - BBC News
Image source,Getty ImagesByKayla Epstein
Published18 November 2026, 15:38 GMT
Democrats in the US House of Representatives officially nominated Hakeem Jeffries to be Speaker, setting him on the path to become the first black lawmaker to lead the chamber.
The House will elect its new Speaker on 3 January, when the next term begins and Democrats will be in the majority.
His election to the powerful position - the Speaker is in line to succeed the president after the vice-president - is widely expected. Should he win, Jeffries will preside over his party's largest House majority in years and benefit from the partnership with a Senate also under Democrats' control.
Jeffries told reporters after the vote that the nomination was "a high honour and a distinct privilege".
As of Wednesday, Democrats will hold at least 257 seats in the House next year, with seven races still uncalled, which is well beyond the 218 needed for a majority.
Jeffries, who represents a district in New York, was re-elected as the party leader in a 251-11 closed-door vote on Wednesday. He has served as minority leader since 2023.
Despite overwhelming support in Wednesday's vote, Jeffries faced a handful of holdouts from new members in the party's left wing, who have said the party's sweeping victory in the midterm elections is a sign voters want change.
"While we have seen meaningful progress, there is still work to be done to ensure that the direction our party takes in this coming Congress reflects what our constituents are demanding of our leadership," seven incoming lawmakers, including fellow New Yorkers Darializa Avila Chevalier and Claire Valdez, said in a statement.
All congressional Democrats are gearing up for clashes with the White House once they officially take control in January.
President Donald Trump, a Republican, has signalled a willingness to work with Democrats on some issues, but has also pledged to use his veto power to reject legislation he does not like.
That could make it hard for Democrats to deliver on their campaign promises to address affordability and pass other reforms.
At a news conference following the vote on Wednesday, Jeffries pledged House Democrats would "fight to lower the high costs of groceries and gas and housing", and "make healthcare affordable for every single American".
Though the party will have a large enough majority to weather defections on must-pass legislation, Jeffries will still have to navigate internal ideological divisions that have grown particularly sharp over US support of Israel and Americans' rising healthcare costs.
Many incoming Democrats, including members of the Democratic Socialists of America, won their elections by challenging the party establishment.
The Congressional Progressive Caucus, from the party's left wing, congratulated Jeffries on the nomination, adding they would "continue conversations with Leader Jeffries to ensure Democrats deliver a bold agenda for working people".

If successful, as is widely expected, Jeffries will make history as the first Black lawmaker to serve in the job.
"Thank you House Democrats," Jeffries wrote in a post on social media after the vote. "Together, we will deliver bold change. And make a big difference in the lives of the American people!"

Jim Jordan of Ohioto be the conference's minority leader; in the Senate, Republicans tapped South Dakota's John Thune for a second term as party leader.
Jeffries, who's led House Democrats since 2023, will need just a simple majority of member votes in a Congress where Democrats are poised to control at least 257 seats, with several remaining races still to be decided.
It's a vastly different reality from what awaited House Republicans four years ago when they regained the House majority. Facing extremely narrow margins, GOP leadersstruggled to unite the conferencearound a speaker and were forced to negotiate with a handful of far-right party holdouts in order to reach consensus. Divides inside the party may prove more pronounced in the Senate, where some Democrats are more publicly questioning whether current Minority Leader Chuck Schumer of New York is best suited to deliver on voter demands for change.

Both sides still have time to shore up votes, with leadership elections set for early December.

ANTALYA, Turkey—After their big gains in the2026 midterm elections, a delegation of Democratic US House members appeared at the United NationsCOP31climate change conference Monday, pledging to rejoin the international fight against global warming.
Rep.Jared Huffman(D-Calif.), ranking member of the House Natural Resources Committee, said it is a “pivotal time” for US climate and energy policy.
“The wrecking ball of Donald Trump and this out-of-touch administration, and the temporarily empty chair of the United States at this COP31, does not represent what the Americans want or need,” Huffman said.
President Donald Trump has pulled the United States out of the Paris climate agreement twice and is trying to quit the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change. The current administration has also tried to cut all funding for climate programs.
Since Trump returned to the White House in 2025, the United States has had no formal government presence at the UN talks, but wasinformally representedbyAmerica Is All In, a coalition including local governments, businesses, faith groups, Native American tribes, and universities.
Huffman said the midterm election shows that Americans have rejected the current administration’s efforts to “turn the United States into something like a petro-dictatorship.” The results could pave the way for the country to reestablish a formal presence at the annual talks.
Given legal uncertainties about Trump’s efforts to completely withdraw the US from the UN’s climate framework, the extent of US participation in the talks is unclear. But Huffman said that, in the past, US congressional delegations have attended the annual Conference of the Parties, as the meeting is formally known, under both Democratic and Republican majorities.
“The next time we’re here, we will be an official congressional delegation led by the leadership of the House of Representatives,” Huffman said in an interview with Inside Climate News.
The US would still be excluded from the formal government-to-government negotiations, but a congressional delegation representing the majority party, potentially capable of advancing climate and energy legislation, could make a difference, Huffman said.
“We want to take the best practices that we’ve heard from all of the global partners… and craft them into good, solid climate policy once we get back to Congress,” said Rep.Lucy McBath(D-Ga.).
The new Democratic majority in the House of Representatives can also use its oversight authority to try to ensure that the money the US has promised for climate aid and sustainable development is restored, said U.S. Rep. Sean Casten (D-Ill.).
Casten said some of America’s European allies are “spending $500, $600 million per day more than before the United States attacked Iran” because of increased oil prices, and that simply stopping those hostilities could free up funding for climate efforts.
“We have lost [the] trust of the international community when it comes to climate,” said Rep.Yassamin Ansari(D-Ariz.).
“I think it is a complete betrayal of our responsibility that Donald Trump has pulled us out of the Paris Agreement not once but twice,” she said. A Democrat winning the 2028 presidential election would help ensure the US can rejoin that agreement, she added.
It will take time to regain trust in the international community, Ansari said.
“But we will come back,” she said, “working 10 times harder, 50 times harder than we did before, to make sure that we are being team players, to make sure that we are… supporting small island developing states and supporting vulnerable African nations.”
Climate activists reacted cautiously to the promises about the United States’ potential return to the international climate arena.
“We welcome the political shift in the United States that puts the brakes on the reckless dismantling of domestic green policies,” saidHarjeet Singh,director ofSatat Sampada Climate Foundation. “However, here at COP31 in Antalya, the international community cannot afford to celebrate prematurely or suffer from collective amnesia.”
Singh said the US has a long history of obstructing climate negotiations across successive administrations and regardless of which party holds power.
“As the world’s largest historical emitter, the US carries an outsized moral and legal responsibility to act,” he said. “Real change will not be measured by who walks through the halls of this summit, but by whether Washington finally ends its expansion of oil, gas, and coal at home and delivers hundreds of billions of dollars in grant-based climate finance to developing countries.”
Singh said until the US pays its fair share to help vulnerable countries recover from climate impacts and transition to sustainable energy systems, “warm words from visiting lawmakers mean very little to communities on the frontlines.”
Brandon Wu, withActionAid USA, said the new Democrat-led House majority must reassert control over the budget and hold the Trump administration accountable for “likely illegal actions like dismantling USAID and gutting foreign assistance” funding approved by Congress.
“What they can deliver to the United Nations process is extremely limited,” he said, adding that it’s unlikely there will be any sweeping new climate legislation or climate funding in the next two years. What members of Congress can do is lay the groundwork for more ambitious action in a post-Trump era, he added.
While meeting delegates from other countries, Huffman said he’s heard both gratitude and optimism, as well as skepticism, about a possible US return to the climate talks.
“The fact is the US has become kind of an unreliable partner and we’ve lost our credibility,” he said. “So we’ve tried to bring humility to this moment. We’ve got work to do to reclaim our credibility in this institution.”
Bob Berwyn is an Austria-based reporter who has covered climate science and international climate policy for more than a decade. Previously, he reported on the environment, endangered species, and public lands for several Colorado newspapers, and also worked as editor and assistant editor at community newspapers in the Colorado Rockies.

Jeffries is set to become one of Trump’s most prominent opponents for final two years of his presidency
Democrats on Wednesday resoundingly nominatedHakeem Jeffriesto serve as speaker of the House when the new Congress begins next year, teeing him up to become the first Black lawmaker to lead the chamber.
A New York congressman who has served as the Democratic minority leader since 2023, Jeffries is set to become one of Donald Trump’s most prominent opponents for the final two years of his presidency, when Democrats will control both the Senate andHouse of Representativesand are expected to undertake aggressive efforts to check his powers.
Democrats nominated Jeffries despite concerns from some progressives that he represents a politically risky status quo for a party that is looking to capitalize on a surprisingly good performance in the midterms, where voters swept them back into power in both the House and Senate with significant majorities.
The vote took place at a caucus meeting held behind closed doors, and no other lawmaker challenged Jeffries for the speakership nomination. A source familiar with the tally said Jeffries was supported by 251 of 262 ballots cast.
Following the election, Jeffries posted a photo of himself as a childon X, and wrote: “Thank you House Democrats. Together, we will deliver bold change. And make a big difference in the lives of the American people!”
The 56-year-old is set to be formally elected speaker when the House of Representatives convenes at the beginning of next year, with Democrats controlling their largest majority in nearly two decades. He would become the first Democratic House speaker since Nancy Pelosi, who will retire from Congress at the end of this year.
The caucus additionally elected the California congressman Ted Lieu to serve as their chair, the first Asian American to hold that position. Fellow Californian Pete Aguilar was named the incoming majority whip, and will be the first Latino in that role.
In office since 2013, Jeffries served as House Democratic caucus chair during Pelosi’s second stint as speaker, from 2019 to 2023. He took over as leader when she stepped down after Democrats lost their House majority in 2022, but rankled progressives by refusing to endorse proposals to create a Medicare for All healthcare system, and for not taking a strong stance against aid to Israel amid accusations it carried out a genocide in Gaza. Earlier this month, Indivisible, a nationwide progressive organizing group, released a poll that found only 28% of registered voters view Jeffries favorably.
He has recently sought to bridge those divides, and on Tuesday announced his support for lowering the age of eligibility for Medicare, and expanding its coverage to include vision and dental treatments, and to offer it to children. He has also called for “dramatic change” in the US relationship with Israel, though in July did not vote for an amendment that would havecut military aidto the Middle Eastern ally.
The speaker of the House is one of the most powerful figures in Congress, and has the power to decide which bills come to the floor of the lower chamber. Should Jeffries win election, he will be tasked with balancing the demands of an ideologically diverse caucus composed of liberals and centrists, as well as lawmakers from safe blue districts and others from areas that Trump won handily in the 2024 vote.
The leaders of the Congressional Progressive caucus cheered Jeffries’ nomination, while noting they expected him to collaborate on passing their preferred healthcare and immigration priorities.
“CPC leadership is working daily with Leader Jeffries to make sure the Democratic majority delivers on our mandate for bold change,” its chair, Greg Casar, and his top deputies said.
“We have made significant progress since the election to lay out a progressive agenda alongside leader Jeffries, and the CPC will work with him to pass the first year of Medicare For All, an end to for-profit immigrant detention centers, and so much more.”
Some newly elected Democrats said they had opted to oppose Jeffries, because they were not convinced he would champion their priorities as speaker,
Don Leonard, a newly elected Democrat representing an Ohio district Trump won two years ago, told CNN he would not vote for Jeffries unless he won commitments to end aid to Israel, and undo the supreme court’s Citizens United ruling, which allowed outside groups to spend unlimited amounts on elections.
Seven newly elected progressive Democrats – Darializa Avila Chevalier and Claire Valdez of New York, Adam Hamawy of New Jersey, Frederick Haynes of Texas, Melat Kiros of Colorado, Donavan McKinney of Michigan and Chris Rabb of Pennsylvania – announced after the vote that they had also opposed making Jeffries speaker, at least for now.
“Whether on Medicare for All, stopping ICE terror, getting money out of politics, or ending the genocide in Gaza, our constituents sent us to Congress with a mandate on these issues. We have worked to secure commitments from leader Jeffries in good-faith conversations,” the lawmakers said.
“While we have seen meaningful progress, there is still work to be done to ensure that the direction our party takes this coming Congress reflects what our constituents are demanding of leadership. Those conversations are ongoing. As such, our vote in caucus today was no.”
Over in the Senate, the party’s leader, Chuck Schumer, is facing a challenge from Senator Chris Van Hollen to lead the party next year, when Democrats will take control of the chamber after winning 56 seats in the midterms. That contest is set to be decided at a caucus vote scheduled for 1 December.
