Donald Trump Jr.was barefoot and beaming when a photographer snapped agroup pictureof him, his new bride, and his 30-or-so wedding party guests on a private island in the Bahamas last May.
But that party—which was reportedlypaid for by a Russian oligarch—has since turned into alegal and political headache.

In a letter sent Wednesday, the incoming head of the House Oversight Committee has directed the president’s son to preserve all records related to his “lavish wedding celebrations” and his many business ventures, too.

That demand is a key step in any serious Congressional probe, and one sign among many that Democratic investigators are going after the president’s family in the new term following their massive wins in the election earlier this month.

Representative Robert Garcia, the incoming head of the House Oversight Committee, also issued similar record-preservation requests to Eric Trump along with Donald Trump Jr., as cofounders of the wildly controversial crypto firm World Liberty Financial, and their brother-in-law Jared Kushner, who runs a Saudi-backed investment firm while serving as a presidential envoy to the Middle East.
Garcia even sent a notice to Donald Trump Jr.’s onetime fiancée Kimberly Guilfoyle, who’s been involved in apay-for-access scandalof her own.

Garcia also sent record-retention letters to White House chief of staff Stephen Miller, for his role in directing the immigration raids that havekilled at least six peopleanddetained more than 500 US citizens; Trust for the National Mall CEO Catherine Townsend, for the $600 million in private and public money spent on the White House ballroom; and vice president JD Vance and attorney general Todd Blanche, for their roles, the letters state, in the alleged cover-up of the Epstein files.

Other figures from the last year and a half of the Trump administration were listed, including former Department of Homeland Security chief Kristi Noem, her top aide Corey Lewandowski, and recently departed White House chief of staff Susie Wiles.
“As the President has said, he's willing to work with anyone to continue delivering victories for hardworking Americans.
If Democrats choose to pursue sham investigations and radical left policies, they are choosing to work against the American people,” White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis tells WIRED.
A representative for the Trump family did not immediately respond to a request for comment for this story.
After they won control of the House and Senate in the midterm elections, Democrats made it plain that they were going to be beyond aggressive in ramping up their investigations.

(“They are going to need to plant new forests for all of the subpoenas we'll be printing,” Senator Ed Markeyquipped.) The target set for those probes is beginning to come into focus more clearly, and the Democrats appear to be starting with the Trump family, who have made a killing in thepresident’s second term.
Now that they have the added resources and authority that come with being in the majority, Garcia and other Democrats want to dig into that growing fortune and who contributed to it.

Senator Richard Blumenthal, the ranking member of the Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, has been looking into World Liberty and other Trump family crypto projects “for 18 months,” as a recent letter to the firm noted.

Senator Elizabeth Warren has repeatedly called for investigations into World Liberty’s “national security risks,” including sales of its token to alleged North Korean hackers and Russian money launderers.

Representative Ro Khanna wants to know more about thesecret saleof 49 percent of World Liberty to funds controlled by SheikhTahnoun bin Zayed al Nahyan, the United Arab Emirates’ intelligence chief, and whether that sale had anything to do with the Trump administration’s decision to allow the sale of advanced AI chips to Abu Dhabi.
World Liberty has been particularly lucrative for the Trumps; according to Forbes, it added at one pointmore than $300 millionto the president’s accounts.

“It’s troubling that Congress might baselessly target a compliant company that has dedicated itself to expanding access to the US dollar when there are a plethora of issues afflicting the American public that need to be addressed,” World Liberty spokesperson David Wachsman tells WIRED.
World Liberty is only one family business among many that has gone through a boom cycle in the past few years.
Donald Trump Jr.’s venture capital firm, 1789, went from a few hundred million under management to somewhere around$4 billion.
The Trump Organization has real estate development deals underway fromBucharest to Bali.

The sudden influx of cash, Garcia notes in his letters, “raises serious concerns” that the deals are essentially “contributions to President Trump and his family in exchange for government action on behalf of the wealthy and well connected.

Access to preferential treatment, federal secrets, regulatory law enforcement leniency, and the president and senior officials appears to trace back to suspicious activity associated with these schemes.”
The Trumps and their representatives have repeatedly insisted they’ve done nothing to merit this kind of scrutiny, other than have the wrong last name.
“We've been dealing with the conflict-of-interest stuff for years,” Donald Trump Jr.
told CNBC at a World Liberty Finance event at Mar-a-Lago in February.
The Russian oligarch who paid for Donald Trump Jr.’s wedding party later claimed the president’s sonreimbursed him.

“There is no evidence that any member of the Trump family ever sought to influence government policy or sought preferential treatment or government intervention to advance their personal or business interests,” Alan Garten, the Trump Organization’s chief legal officer,told this reporterprior to the election.
The pushback from Trumpworld has grown more intense since the Democrats’ midterm sweep.

Aaron Reitz, the US attorney for the Southern District of Texas and a MAGA die-hard, sent a document-preservation letter of his own to Warren, accusing her of “terrorizing” Big Tech executives with her promises of investigation.
The White House even claimed that overly aggressive oversight might itself be a crime.
“The Administration,” counsel to the president Will Scharf wrote to Garcia after the election, “will not be extorted.”

Andrej Stojakovic breaks 69-year-old record in historic performance against Duke | Sporting NewsSkip to main content
Andrej Stojakovic breaks 69-year-old record in historic performance against Duke
Cameron Indoor Stadium has hosted some of the greatest players in college basketball history, but none of Duke's visiting opponents had ever delivered a scoring performance quite like Andrej Stojakovic's on Tuesday night. The Illinois standout scored 46 points as the No. 10 Fighting Illini defeated No. 5 Duke 99-78, ending the Blue Devils' 35-game home winning streak.
Stojakovic surpassed a record that had stood since February 1957, when South Carolina's Grady Wallace scored 43 points at Cameron Indoor Stadium. The Illinois guard also finished just two points short of the building's overall single-game scoring record, established by Duke legend Dick Groat in 1952.
Andrej Stojakovic delivers performance for the ages
The son of former NBA All-Star Peja Stojakovic demonstrated remarkable offensive efficiency throughout the evening. He converted 14 of his 21 field-goal attempts and made 16 of 20 free throws, repeatedly finding ways to score against Duke's defense.
Illinois’ Andrej Stojaković has broken the record for most points scored by a visiting player at Duke with 45 points. The previous record had stood since 1957, a span of 69 years.
— Joe Tipton (@JoeTipton)November 18, 2026
Stojakovic entered halftime with 20 points before adding another 26 during the second half. His performance was particularly impressive because Illinois did not shoot well from beyond the arc as a team, making only six of its 32 attempts.
Freshman Quentin Coleman contributed another 27 points, meaning the two Illinois players combined for 73 of their team's 99 points. Their production helped the Fighting Illini maintain control even when Duke attempted to establish momentum during the second half.
MORE:No. 24 Kentucky escapes Northern Arizona after nearly giving away 13-point lead
Illinois delivers emphatic response to previous Duke embarrassment
The victory carried additional significance for Illinois considering what happened the last time these programs met. Duke defeated the Fighting Illini 110-67 in February 2025, delivering one of the most disappointing results of that Illinois season.
Tuesday produced a dramatically different outcome, with Illinois controlling the rebounding battle and repeatedly creating problems for Duke around the basket. The Fighting Illini improved to 4-1 despite continuing to play without injured preseason All-American David Mirkovic.
Duke fell to 3-2 and suffered its first home defeat since March 2024. The Blue Devils will have an opportunity to respond Saturday against Washington State, while Illinois returns home to face Eastern Illinois on Friday.
For Stojakovic, Tuesday's performance will remain memorable regardless of what happens throughout the remainder of the season. Scoring 46 points at Cameron Indoor Stadium is an accomplishment that could remain unmatched for another generation.

‘Ten is the minimum’: 14-year-old surfing champion Leihani Zoric aims for record world title haul
Zoric puts target on veteran teammate Gilmore’s back: ‘I want to be like her’
Peru win makes her first Indigenous Australian world champion in open category
With the surfing world her oyster, Leihani Zoric has set her sights stratospherically high after the 14-year-old stunned a star-studded field to be crowned the youngest ever ISA Open WorldSurfingChampion and claim a second world title this year.
Zoric, who was still 13 when she won the ISA under-18 world title in September, added a gold medal to her burgeoning individual palmarès with victory in Peru over the weekend, when she emerged triumphant ahead of established stars of the surfing world such as Stephanie Gilmore, Tyler Wright, Carissa Moore and Johanne Defay.
Zoric’s efforts helped Australia’s women’s team top the national rankings, crucially earning an additional women’s Olympic quota place for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games – a spot that the Indigenous surfer has her sights firmly set on – and giving Australian surfing a tangible boost ahead of the home Games in Brisbane in 2032.
Leihani Zoric, 14, stuns surfing world with gold medal to give Australia Olympic boostRead more
Sitting alongside teammate and record eight-time world champion Stephanie Gilmore on the Irukandjis’ return to Australia on Wednesday, Zoric outlined lofty ambitions for a career that has only just begun, starting with putting a target on the experienced Gilmore’s back.
“I want to be like her and have like eight world titles, maybe even more … I said 10 is the minimum that I want to win,” Zoric said. “And then two Olympic gold medals. Hopefully LA ‘28 Olympic gold medal and Brisbane 2032 gold medal. I’m excited to see what happens.”
The teenager had to battle her way through numerous heats at the competition in Punta Rocas before producing a sensational performance in the final to beat French Olympic bronze medallist Johanne Defay with a 15.50 heat total which included a clutch 7.67-point ride in the closing minutes to snatch victory.
“It feels amazing. I’m very proud of all the work I’ve put it in, and to see that it works and that it’s paying off,” she said at Gold Coast airport. “All the hard days where you go out, and there’s no one out, and the waves are bad, and you’re like, ‘Oh, I just want to sit in bed and watch TV, watch the Simpsons, do normal kid things. But everything matters, and it all adds up to have moments like that.”
Zoric, who idolised the likes of Gilmore and Wright when she was younger, became the first Indigenous Australian world champion in the open category with her success in Peru, and said the scale of her achievement was still sinking in.
“I’m over the moon,” she said. “It feels amazing. It’s been my goal ever since I first started surfing to get to represent my country, my Indigenous culture as well [on the] world stage. And in the sport that I love most.
“It was a really proud moment for me getting to hold the Aboriginal flag when I won. And because there’s so many incredible non-Indigenous and Indigenous girls in Australia that do such incredible things as well, to get to represent my culture was really important to me.
“With so much talent we have in Australia, it’s an incredible chance for lots of young girls to be inspired for LA, but also then looking into Brisbane,” she said. “It just showcases the opportunity we have to represent at our home Games.”
While Zoric has her eyes on LA, she may have an unlikely foe to contend with – veteran Gilmore, at the age of 38, revealed on Wednesday she has not ruled out making a bid for inclusion in the Australian team.
Gilmore represented her country at the Tokyo Games but did not progress past the third round, and missed out on Paris while she was taking a hiatus from competitive surfing.
“I sort of gave up on my Olympic dream after Tokyo,” she said. “My dream was to win eight world titles. But there’s something special about Lower Trestles [where the Olympic surf competition will be held in 2028]. It’s a wave I’m super comfortable at and going to the ISAs in Peru, it really ignited some kind of fire.
“That team energy is so thrilling and it makes you imagine how, if you could go to the Olympics and win a medal and experience that again, [it] would be really special.
“I’ll put my best foot forward and see how we go. But either way, I’d love to support all the team no matter who goes, even if it is Leihani as a young grom showing up and surfing for the country. That’d be an incredible show.”

Why is 46-year-old Ronaldinho returning to soccer with Ravenna, an Italian third division club? - CBS Sportssite: media | arena: soccer | pageType: stories | section: | slug: ronaldinho-46-year-old-return-soccer-italian-third-division-ravenna | sport: soccer | route: article_single.us | 6-keys: media/spln/soccer/reg/free/storiesSkip to Main Content
Why is 46-year-old Ronaldinho returning to soccer with Ravenna, an Italian third division club?
The former Brazilian star will play his first game with Ravenna this weekend in Italy
ByFrancesco PorzioNov 14, 2026at 12:32 pm ET•3 min readGetty Images
Ronaldinho, one of the greatest footballers of all time, will be back on the pitch on Sunday, Nov. 15, for a historic day. The Brazilian striker, who won the 2005 edition of the Ballon d'Or and played for PSG, Barcelona and AC Milan at the peak of his European career, signed a deal in the summer of 2026 to join the roster of Ravenna, an Italian team currently playing in the third division. Ronaldinho, who played his last professional match in 2015 and will turn 47 next year, is expected to play some minutes in the home derby against Forli, and you can watch it all onParamount+. But let's break down how and why he's coming back to play after more than a decade and after announcing his retirement in 2018.
"I'm really looking forward to this moment and coming back to Italy once more."@10Ronaldinhosays he can't wait to return to professional football with Ravenna at age 46 💪pic.twitter.com/0UMdkhgFlY
— CBS Sports Golazo ⚽️ (@CBSSportsGolazo)November 13, 2026
Date: Sunday, Nov. 15 |Time: 11:30 a.m. ET
Location: Stadio Bruno Benelli -- Ravenna, Italy
Ravenna, who have a history of playing in Italy's lower divisions, were acquired in 2024 by Ignazio Cipriani, the nephew of Arrigo Cipriani, the founder of the iconic Harry's Bar in Venice. The Cipriani Group operates high-end restaurants, private members' clubs (Casa Cipriani), luxury hotels, event venues and branded residences across major international cities, such as New York City, London, Monaco, Miami and Dubai. Basically, it is now positioning itself as a global luxury lifestyle and real estate player, rather than simply a restaurant group.
"Today I do a lot of Footy Volley. I'm training differently."
The legendary@10Ronaldinhotalks coming out of retirement after 11 years to suit up for Ravenna in Serie C this weekend 👀pic.twitter.com/z0cSOHd2k4
This is why Cipriani created links with some of the most notable figures in the world: soccer players, politicians, singers, actors and more. When the group entered the world of soccer, it brought in people who had already worked at the highest level of the game, such as former AC Milan sporting director Ariedo Braida, who played a key role alongside former AC Milan CEO Adriano Galliani in building AC Milan's legacy under Silvio Berlusconi's presidency. Braida left AC Milan in 2013 after 27 years.
Ravenna's current head coach is Andrea Mandorlini, who spent several years coaching in Serie A and represented Inter as a player between 1984 and 1991. The connection with Ronaldinho, who joined AC Milan in 2008 during Braida's tenure at the club, also involves another key figure at Ravenna: Lorenzo Tonetti, the club's head of external relations. During Ronaldinho's time at AC Milan, Tonetti owned Giannino, a restaurant in Milan that became something of a second home for several of the club's players. It was also a favorite meeting place for Galliani, who famously negotiated several transfer deals within its walls. Curiously, one of the waiters working there at the time was Giuseppe Riso, now one of the best-known agents in soccer, who represents players such as Sandro Tonali, Davide Frattesi and Carlos Augusto.
Ronaldinho signed a dual player-investor contract in the summer of 2026. He joined Ravenna with the ultimate aim of scoring one final professional goal while also acquiring an ownership stake in the club. Rather than having him play every week, his deal focuses on global marketing and special appearances in marquee matches, such as the local derby against Forli that will take place on Sunday. Ronaldinho is one of the most notable players in the history of the game. He joined Barcelona in 2003, where he became a global superstar, winning two FIFA World Player of the Year awards, the 2005 Ballon d'Or and the UEFA Champions League in 2006. In 2008, he moved to AC Milan, where he played until 2011. At the international level, he was a key part of Brazil's national team that won the 2002 World Cup. He formally retired in 2018 but played his last-ever football game three years earlier, in 2015.

Even more record highs as Berkshire's Q4 rally scores 19% gain
Berkshire Hathaway's red-hot shares are ending a strong week with four consecutive fresh record high closes.
Since the rally began with the start of the fourth quarter on October 1, theClass A shareshave closed at record highs 11 times as they soared 19.1%.
The much more widely heldB sharesclosed at new highs just 10 times but are also up 19.1% from their near-term low.
The gains are in sharp contrast to theS&P 500's1.2% dip as investors appear to be seeing Berkshire as arelatively safe havenamid worries about AI stocks and spending.
Both Berkshire classes were up 3.9% on the week as the S&P advanced by 2.5%,its best week since early August.
Berkshire's B shares are now 7.5 percentage points ahead of the benchmark for the year so far.
Aftererasing their post-Buffett CEO announcement lossesthree weeks ago, Berkshire shares are now up almost 10% since last year's shareholders meeting.
They've gained around 29% since last August's lows and are up around 18% year-to-date.
Financials filing points to more Bank of America sales
Berkshire Hathaway is due to disclose its quarterly equity portfolio snapshot on Monday when it files its Q3 13F with the SEC.
We won't know for sure until then, but numbers in the company'sthird quarter 10-Q, releasedlast Saturday, indicate Berkshire continued to reduce itsBank of Americastake.
It would be the ninth consecutive quarter of selling.
As of June 30,Berkshire reported holding 483.4 millionBAC shares valued now at $24.7 billion, it's fifth largest equity position.
On June 30, 2024, before the selling began,Berkshire owned just over 1 billion sharesvalued at $41.1 billion.
Since then, the number of shares in the portfolio has decreased by 53.2%, not including any Q3 sales, while the stock price has increased by 28.3%.
If there had been no reductions, the position would be worth $52.7 billion.
The belief Berkshire sold more BAC shares in the third quarter is based on a $372 million reduction in the cost basis for equities categorized by the company as "banks, insurance, and finance."
The 10-Q also reports $2.2 billion of pretax gains from equity sales.
Barron'snotesBank of America andAmerican Expressare the only financial stocks in the portfolio that have a cost basis low enough to generate a gain like that. Amex is one of the four stocks new CEO Greg Abel indicated would be held for "decades" to comein his February letter to shareholders.
In any case, Berkshire's almost 23% stake in Amex would have required it to quickly disclose any sales.
FILE PHOTO: Reflections are seen in the windows of a Bank of America branch in New York.Lucas Jackson | Reuters
Based on the numbers in the 10-Q, the warrants Berkshire received as part of a2011 $5 billion investment in the bankthatit used in 2017 to buy 700 million shares at $7.14 each, and BAC's average stock price in the quarter,Barron'sestimates 30 to 40 million shares may have been sold.
That would be roughly in line with the 30.2 million shares sold in the second quarter.
The case isn't as good, butBarron'sthinks Berkshire may have bought moreAlphabetshares in the period. That's based on a $2.3 billion increase in the cost basis for the category that includes Google's parent.
Overall, it looks like it will be a relatively quiet quarter with $2.4 billion in equity purchases and $2.8 billion in sales.
In the first quarter, Berkshire bought $15.9 billion and sold $24.1 billion of equities. In the second quarter, it purchased $23.5 billion and sold $3.7 billion.
All those numbers exclude the company's buybacks of its own stock.
Second yen bond sale of the year offers more attractive rates
In aterm sheet filed early Friday, Berkshire Hathaway says it is selling more than 182 billion yen ($1.1 billion) worth of bonds with maturities between 2029 and 2056 and annual interest rates between 2.6% and 4.6%.
Bloombergpoints outthe rates, compared to benchmarks, are higher than its previous sale this year.
It quotes a fund manager as saying market sentiment "has become more sensitive," forcing issuers to make their offerings more attractive.
In April, Berkshire sold 272 billion yen ($1.7 billion) of bonds.
Berkshire uses the proceeds from the yen-denominated bonds to protectits ongoing investments in Japanese stocksfrom currency fluctuations.

Andrej Stojakovic breaks 69-year-old record in historic performance against Duke

Cameron Indoor Stadium has hosted some of the greatest players in college basketball history, but none of Duke's visiting opponents had ever delivered a scoring performance quite like Andrej Stojakovic's on Tuesday night.
The Illinois standout scored 46 points as the No.
10 Fighting Illini defeated No.
5 Duke 99-78, ending the Blue Devils' 35-game home winning streak.
Stojakovic surpassed a record that had stood since February 1957, when South Carolina's Grady Wallace scored 43 points at Cameron Indoor Stadium.
The Illinois guard also finished just two points short of the building's overall single-game scoring record, established by Duke legend Dick Groat in 1952.
The son of former NBA All-Star Peja Stojakovic demonstrated remarkable offensive efficiency throughout the evening.
He converted 14 of his 21 field-goal attempts and made 16 of 20 free throws, repeatedly finding ways to score against Duke's defense.
Illinois’ Andrej Stojaković has broken the record for most points scored by a visiting player at Duke with 45 points.
The previous record had stood since 1957, a span of 69 years.
— Joe Tipton (@JoeTipton)November 18, 2026
Stojakovic entered halftime with 20 points before adding another 26 during the second half.
His performance was particularly impressive because Illinois did not shoot well from beyond the arc as a team, making only six of its 32 attempts.
Freshman Quentin Coleman contributed another 27 points, meaning the two Illinois players combined for 73 of their team's 99 points.
Their production helped the Fighting Illini maintain control even when Duke attempted to establish momentum during the second half.
24 Kentucky escapes Northern Arizona after nearly giving away 13-point lead
The victory carried additional significance for Illinois considering what happened the last time these programs met.
Duke defeated the Fighting Illini 110-67 in February 2025, delivering one of the most disappointing results of that Illinois season.
Tuesday produced a dramatically different outcome, with Illinois controlling the rebounding battle and repeatedly creating problems for Duke around the basket.
The Fighting Illini improved to 4-1 despite continuing to play without injured preseason All-American David Mirkovic.
Duke fell to 3-2 and suffered its first home defeat since March 2024.
The Blue Devils will have an opportunity to respond Saturday against Washington State, while Illinois returns home to face Eastern Illinois on Friday.
For Stojakovic, Tuesday's performance will remain memorable regardless of what happens throughout the remainder of the season.
Scoring 46 points at Cameron Indoor Stadium is an accomplishment that could remain unmatched for another generation.

Alberto Musalem, President and CEO of the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, speaks to the Economic Club of New York, in New York City, U.S., Feb. 20, 2025.Brendan McDermid | Reuters
St. Louis Federal Reserve President Alberto Musalem indicated Tuesday that the central bank may need as many as four rate hikes in coming months,offering one of the most hawkishviews yet by a Fed policymaker about the steps needed to quell inflation.
During a speech delivered in Argentina, Musalem made the case thatcurrent policyis not significantly restricting economic activity.
"The economy will likely require several interest rate increases before the spring of 2027 to achieve 2% inflation in a timely manner," he said.
Musalem said the real policy rate, which subtracts the inflation rate from the Fed's target rate, needs to be between 2%-2.5% by next spring, and estimated that the current rate is about a full point below that range. That position suggests the Fed may need to hike at each of the upcoming Fed meetings in December, January, March and April.
Musalem does not get a vote on the rate-setting Federal Open Market Committee over the period where he says that the rate increases will be needed, though he does get to present views and provide input on the "dot plot" of individual members' expectations. He will next vote in 2028.
To be sure, Musalem noted "an unlikely but still plausible scenario" in which no further hikes would be needed.
"Falling energy prices and lower shipping costs, or an increase in potential output growth driven by higher productivity growth, might ease inflation pressures such that inflation moves toward target in 18 months," he said. Another possibility is that demand might decelerate as spending on artificial intelligence slows.
However, he said the more likely scenario is that "persistent strong demand and ongoing supply pressures" combine to keepinflation above the Fed's 2% target, thus requiring further increases in the fed funds rate from its current range of 3.75%-4%.
"It would be preferable for a higher real policy rate to happen in a balanced way, driven both by lower inflation and a higher nominal policy rate," he said. "However, the nominal policy rate may need to do most of the work."

Civil liberties campaigners have raised concerns about racial bias in the use of facial recognition technology by police.Photograph: John Keeble/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenCivil liberties campaigners have raised concerns about racial bias in the use of facial recognition technology by police.Photograph: John Keeble/Getty Images
Ethnic minority groups in Wales four times more likely to be target of police facial scans
Exclusive: South Wales police figures show BAME people accounted for 24% of selected scans in 2025, despite being 7% of population
Ethnic minority people are four times more likely than their white counterparts to be chosen for some police facial scans, according to official data, sparking warnings of racial bias.
Internal figures released by South Wales police revealed that 24% of people selected by police for facial recognition checks were from ethnic minorities, despite this group making up only 7% of the area’s totalpopulation.
The force polices Wales’s largest cities – Cardiff and Swansea – and has pioneered several versions of AI-enabled facial recognition technology. The latest figures relate to police officers capturing a person’s face with a smartphone and running the image through an algorithm called “Neoface” to match it against custody mugshots and other face databases. Most scans are made because people are suspected of crimes.
Civil liberties campaigners called the ethnicity figures “alarming”. The force said they raised “concerns about disproportionality” and that it was reviewing its approach.
The data relates to a full year of use in 2025 and was obtained under the Freedom of Information Act and shared with the Guardian. Even when compared with arrestdata for the police area, in which 11% of people arrested are from ethnic minorities, the face-scan figures appear disproportionate.
South Wales is one of the first UK constabularies to routinely use this “officer-initiated facial recognition” (OIFR) technology, which aims to identify suspects, wanted criminals and missing people who decline to give their details when challenged as well as people who are found unconscious, uncommunicative or dead. A similar system is being trialled by the Metropolitan police in London and has also been tested in Liverpool.
Critics have called facial recognition tools “Orwellian” and there have been repeated concerns about algorithmic bias putting ethnic minorities at greater risk of wrongful arrest.
Last week, the police watchdog warned that innocent people, especially from ethnic minorities, remained at risk of wrongful arrest if police treated inaccurate retrospective facial recognition data as evidence.
But advocates – including the home secretary, Shabana Mahmood – believe facial recognition is the biggest breakthrough for catching criminals since fingerprints and DNA matching.
Other versions of the technology include live facial recognition cameras directed from marked vans and cameras fixed to lamp-posts, like those piloted in Croydon between October 2025 and March 2026, which led to 173 arrests, including of rape, kidnap and sexual assault suspects.
Scanned, tackled, arrested: how live facial recognition was piloted on the streets of CroydonRead more
“This data shows that intrusive biometric tools are being used to disproportionately target minority communities,” said Jake Hurfurt, the head of research and investigations at Big Brother Watch, a civil liberties campaign that obtained the figures.
“It is alarming that non-white people have been subject to face scans at a much higher rate than would be expected either by the region’s demography or the makeup of people arrested in the region.”
Aliya Mohammed, the chief executive ofRaceEquality First, a Cardiff-based anti-discrimination organisation, said the figures raised “serious concerns about racial disproportionality”.
“Facial recognition is not neutral because it uses AI,” she said. “If existing biases influence who is stopped and scanned, technology can reinforce and even amplify inequality.”
Alvi Choudhury, 26, who wasarrested in Februaryfor a burglary in a city he had never visited after police face-scanning software confused him with another person of south Asian heritage on a custody database, said it was “very concerning” that ethnic minorities were being disproportionately scanned.
“The police are under pressure to solve crimes and they are over-reliant on these AI tools,” he said. “They shouldn’t be arresting people based on the AI tools alone.”
He remained worried AI systems were not trained on enough ethnic minority faces to ensure the number of false positives was no greater than for white people.
According to the data for 2025, South Wales police officers initiated face scans of 257 adults and 14 children, including two under-10s.
More than half were suspected of a crime, being unlawfully at large or breaching bail conditions. The next most common reasons were because officers believed the person posed a risk of harm to themselves or others – such as stalkers or sex offenders.
In about one in 10 cases, a scan was initiated for a suspected missing person while the technology was used to identify a dead person about once a fortnight.
In many of the cases, the scan failed to deliver a match or the subject agreed to share their identity. Where a match was made, arrests followed in 48% of cases and no further action resulted in a third of cases.
A spokesperson for South Wales police said: “We recognise the figures raise concerns about disproportionality. The number of OIFR searches remains relatively small, and the use of the technology is in its infancy.
“That said, each deployment is based on the individual circumstances that officers are dealing with at that time and is subject to supervisory and force-wide scrutiny.”
They said the force would “continue to review our approach through our established governance processes, which also include input from independent advisory groups and external scrutiny panels” and added: “Where opportunities for learning or improvement are identified, we will take appropriate action.”

Marco Rubio says no evidence recent tech outages in US are linked or 'nefarious' | Euronews
ByGavin BlackburnPublished on18 November 2026 - 13:05 GMT+1ShareCommentsAdd Euronews on GoogleShareFacebookTwitterFlipboardSendRedditLinkedinMessengerTelegramVKBlueskyThreadsWhatsapp
Air travel was disrupted because of what the Trump administration called outdated equipment, causing regulators to halt all flights from taking off for several hours on Friday evening.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio took time during a high-level diplomatic summit in Asia on Wednesday to try and soothe public US jitters over a spate of cyber-related disruptions.
Rubio insisted authorities have found "zero evidence" that recent outages across tech platforms are related to one another or due to the work of "nefarious actors."
His comments, on the sidelines of a Southeast Asia summit, follow multiple disruptions of everything from US air traffic operations to Microsoft email and messaging to banking and mobile pay, as well as the outage of a top-secret US government communications network.
"The first thing I want to make very clear is that we have zero evidence whatsoever, we have no indication, no evidence, and no reason to believe at all that any of these incidents are related to each other," Rubio told reporters in Manila while on a trip to Asia with US President Donald Trump.
"The second is that we have zero evidence or any reason to believe that any of these isolated or individual instances have anything to do with nefarious actors, with cyber hackers, with criminals, with another nation state, with a malign actor of any kind."
Rubio emphasised the ubiquity of technology when explaining why it could feel as if there was a growing wave of cyber incidents.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio speaks to the press at the Solaire Resort near Manila, 18 November, 2026AP Photo
"The more technology becomes embedded into our everyday lives, the more the vulnerabilities become real," he said.
"There was a time when people used to physically go in with masks and guns and rob banks. Now they can do it from behind a computer screen halfway around the world and every major economy in the world is facing that same challenge."
On Tuesday a top-secret network that the National Security Agency (NSA) uses for internal communications went down, the agency acknowledged.
The NSA said it had experienced "temporary degradation during scheduled routine maintenance," but that its capabilities remained operational and "our ability to defend national security continues."
The NSA, part of the US Department of Defence, is responsible for global monitoring, collection and processing of information for intelligence and counterintelligence.
The Trump administration has insisted Americans and their various systems remain secure, with Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin emphasizing that the wave of recent outages does not stem from cyber criminals.
A woman moves past baggage at San Diego International Airport in San Diego, 16 November, 2026AP Photo
"I can tell you with complete certainty that we are not under attack," Mullin told CNBC. "There's no cyber threat that's taking place. The homeland is very secure."
The mess of stranded travellers and aircrews spilled into the weekend and early this week.
Microsoft also suffered a major outage last week that affected Outlook and Teams users around the world, while several large banks saw disruptions to their banking apps and online portals on Monday.
Trump's rival Democratic Party, which just won decisively in US midterm elections earlier this month, blamed the administration's incompetence for the string of high-visibility outages and the lack of transparency around them.

Rubio says tech outages are not part of 'systemic attack' against US - BBC News
Watch: Marco Rubio says recent tech outages are 'completely unrelated' to one another
Published18 November 2026, 02:15 GMT
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has dismissed widespread concerns online that the series of recent tech outages in the past week are connected, telling reporters there was "zero evidence" of any link.
Rubio acknowledged that "people are fearful" the spate of outages, which included all flights being grounded in the US and widespread disruptions to banking, Apple and Microsoft services, could be linked or part of a plot.
"We are not under systemic attack," he said. "These events, one has nothing to do with the other, they are not inter-related."
Cyber-security experts have agreed that there is no evidence linking the outages, and many of the issues appear due to updates to old infrastructure.
In the past week, there has been amassive Microsoft outage, an apparent tech glitch whichgrounded all US flights for hours,and issues for theNational Security Agency,outages affecting the biggest US banks and Apple.
Every affected company or agency has said the issue was not cyber-related and not the work of an outside actor.
Rubio's comments came hours after US Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton also addressed the issue, telling Fox News the outages were not the product of a cyber-attack. He explained "lots of institutions" are patching or upgrading systems, which has caused some disruption.
Rubio was asked whether the Trump administration was concerned public fears could lead to stockpiling or a run on the banks.
He said the best way to combat such fears was for the US government to share everything they know with the American people.
"Every indicator we have is that every single one of these events has an explanation or a cause that has nothing to do with a cyber-criminal, has nothing to do with a hostile actor or another country," he said.
Technology-related disruptions have happened almost daily since Thursday, when a Microsoft outage disrupted many of its services, including email.
The next day, the US Federal Aviation Administrationhalted flights across the USfor more than four hours with a rare national ground stop. It was the longest halting of flights since the 11 September 2001 attacks on the US.
TheUS transport secretary said the issue was technicaland caused by a copper wire upgrade and outdated equipment.
On Monday, a United Airlines technology failure delayed about 150 flights and a JPMorgan Chase software problem disrupted service at thebiggest and most utilised banksin the US.
Both United and Chase said a software issue was behind the glitch.
Apple users were impacted by outages affecting iCloud and Apple Pay on Tuesday. The company said the cause was not a cyber-attack but the outage was triggered by an an internal update.
The same day, a highly classified network used by the US National Security Agency (NSA) for internal communicationsalso went offlinefor a period of time.
Image source,AFP via GettyImage caption,
Passengers wait to check in at Los Angeles International Airport as flights resume after being grounded for several hours on November 13 due to a major communications outage.
Tech experts weigh in: 'No conspiracy here'
Cybersecurity experts say there is no evidence connecting the Microsoft, airline, and bank disruptions from the last five days.
Kris Beevers, CEO and co-founder of the network and infrastructure management company NetBox Labs, acknowledged the circulating theories on social media linking the barrage of outages.
"There is no conspiracy here," he told the BBC.
"There is something more ordinary, and more important to understand: the infrastructure that runs the world is changing faster than ever, and change is risk. Much of it is 30 to 40 years old, with decades of technical debt, and it's now being asked to change very quickly."
Beevers said AI is only part of the story.
"It's putting more strain on these legacy networks, and it's also creating real urgency around security," he said.
"Our customers are the amazing teams behind these networks at airlines, banking, energy, and retail who are essentially doing heart surgery on a global scale to get these networks back up and running quickly."
Vice President of Threat Intelligence for Palo Alto Networks Unit 42, Sherrod DeGrippo, said: "What this week really underscores is how tightly coupled, and fragile, our core digital infrastructure is, where a single software bug or router failure can cascade nationwide."

Marco Rubio speaks to the press at the Solaire Resort in the Philippines about a spate of recent tech outages affecting the US.Photograph: Mark Schiefelbein/APView image in fullscreenMarco Rubio speaks to the press at the Solaire Resort in the Philippines about a spate of recent tech outages affecting the US.Photograph: Mark Schiefelbein/AP
‘Zero’ evidence that recent cascade of tech outages are linked, says Rubio
US secretary of state’s comments come as vulnerability in programming language Java highlighted
There is “zero evidence” that a wave of IT outages – which have grounded flights, cut off work access, limited bank access, affected Apple and disrupted classified communications – are related to each other or are the work of malign actors, according to the US secretary of state.
Marco Rubio said the US was “not under systemic attack” and a cascade of network problems was “not inter-related”.
In recent days,Microsoft,major US banks,Apple,American air traffic control systemsand theNational Security Agencyhave all been affected by technical failures and outages.
People in the US: share your views on the recent flight disruption and Microsoft outageRead more
“We have zero evidence or any reason to believe that any of these isolated or individual instances have anything to do with nefarious actors, with cyber-hackers, with criminals, with another nation state, with a malign actor of any kind,” Rubio said.
Rubio’s comments came as cybersecurity researchers flagged a vulnerability in Java, a programming language used by 90% of companies in the Fortune 500, a ranking of the largest companies in the US. The researchers at US-based Calif used AI to discover the flaw and recently unearthed glitches in PHP, another computer language.
Calif said the Java flaw could allow hackers to remotely execute code, allowing them to place malicious software on a target’s systems.
The US director of national intelligence, Jay Clayton, said the incidents were caused by security upgrades – such as plugging the flaws in PHP – that took longer than planned or encountered unexpected hiccups.
“Everybody recognises it’s time to upgrade their systems, and as they upgrade them, they’re not coming back as expected in all cases, and in some cases, systems have to hand off to other systems, and those handoffs are not coming back as expected,” he told the Fox Business news channel.
Tal Be’ery, a cybersecurity expert, said he did not believe the incidents were linked directly but had a common underlying theme: AI. IT systems were buckling under the pressure of adding AI or tackling flaws uncovered by AI, he said.
“Our IT infrastructure is brittle, and when AI puts massive extra pressure on it, whether through upgrades to accommodate AI or through the rapid patching that AI-driven vulnerability discovery demands,” Be’ery said.
Since April, when the AI startup Anthropic released its Mythos model, which had a startling ability to flag IT flaws, the amount of vulnerabilities found by leading tech companieshas soared eightfold– while OpenAI has also released models capable of finding previously unseen flaws. Researchers at Calif used OpenAI technology to discover the Java flaw.
“[Java] is the beating heart of the modern economy,”Calif wrote in a blogpost. “Banking, aviation, telecommunications, nearly every critical sector runs on Java, including national security systems.”
However, Steven Murdoch, a professor of security engineering at University College London, said the flaw did not apply to every Java user and was specific to a library of code – Base64 – that comes bundled with a version of Java.
“It’s significant but it’s not every Java program that is affected,” he said.
In the UK the National Cyber Security Centre urged organisations to keep their systems up to date, while the US and South Korean authorities also urged Java users to install security updates.
Rubio made the comments as he travelled with Donald Trump for key meetings in the Philippines on Wednesday, before flying tothe tech hub of Shenzhen in Chinafor the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit.
Trump was dismissive when asked whether he was concerned about the outages on Tuesday. “It’s life. When you’re big and powerful and you have all the money, things like that happen. It’s fine,” Trump said in Manila.
The series of outages began on Thursday last week, when Microsoft’s email and other toolswent down, affecting millions of workers who rely on them. Microsoft traced the problem to “an earlier network capacity upgrade”.
Flights across the US weregrounded the next dayin the longest “ground stop” since the September 11 attacks. The US Federal Aviation Administration blamed a router upgrade.
By Monday, banks were in the spotlight, as customers reported difficulty accessing online accounts at several major financial institutions and the money transfer service Zelle after a technical problem at JPMorgan Chase caused ripple effects throughout the financial system. Chase said it was caused by “a software bug” and was “not cyber-related”.
The same day, United Airlines said it hadresolved an internal system outagethat delayed departing flights.
Then on Tuesday, an internal network that the National Security Agency uses to communicate classified information was offline after what the agency described as “routine maintenance”. Apple also confirmed problems with its iPhone apps, such as Apple Pay and iCloud, on Tuesday but said it had resolved them.
The Democrat Mark Warner, the vice-chair of the Senate intelligence committee, supported the assessment that the outages were not caused by a “coordinated effort” but by attempts to shore up systems.
“The evidence so far points toward legitimate efforts to secure our systems, not malicious activity.”

fact_units.text: Marco Rubio says no evidence recent tech outages in US are linked or 'nefarious' | Euronews
ByGavin BlackburnPublished on18 November 2026 - 13:05 GMT+1ShareCommentsAdd Euronews on GoogleShareFacebookTwitterFlipboardSendRedditLinkedinMessengerTelegramVKBlueskyThreadsWhatsapp
Air travel was disrupted because of what the Trump administration called outdated equipment, causing regulators to halt all flights from taking off for several hours on Friday evening.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio took time during a high-level diplomatic summit in Asia on Wednesday to try and soothe public US jitters over a spate of cyber-related disruptions.
Rubio insisted authorities have found "zero evidence" that recent outages across tech platforms are related to one another or due to the work of "nefarious actors."

His comments, on the sidelines of a Southeast Asia summit, follow multiple disruptions of everything from US air traffic operations to Microsoft email and messaging to banking and mobile pay, as well as the outage of a top-secret US government communications network.

"The first thing I want to make very clear is that we have zero evidence whatsoever, we have no indication, no evidence, and no reason to believe at all that any of these incidents are related to each other," Rubio told reporters in Manila while on a trip to Asia with US President Donald Trump.

"The second is that we have zero evidence or any reason to believe that any of these isolated or individual instances have anything to do with nefarious actors, with cyber hackers, with criminals, with another nation state, with a malign actor of any kind."
Rubio emphasised the ubiquity of technology when explaining why it could feel as if there was a growing wave of cyber incidents.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio speaks to the press at the Solaire Resort near Manila, 18 November, 2026AP Photo
"The more technology becomes embedded into our everyday lives, the more the vulnerabilities become real," he said.
"There was a time when people used to physically go in with masks and guns and rob banks.
Now they can do it from behind a computer screen halfway around the world and every major economy in the world is facing that same challenge."
On Tuesday a top-secret network that the National Security Agency (NSA) uses for internal communications went down, the agency acknowledged.
The NSA said it had experienced "temporary degradation during scheduled routine maintenance," but that its capabilities remained operational and "our ability to defend national security continues."
The NSA, part of the US Department of Defence, is responsible for global monitoring, collection and processing of information for intelligence and counterintelligence.

The Trump administration has insisted Americans and their various systems remain secure, with Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin emphasizing that the wave of recent outages does not stem from cyber criminals.
A woman moves past baggage at San Diego International Airport in San Diego, 16 November, 2026AP Photo
"I can tell you with complete certainty that we are not under attack," Mullin told CNBC.
The mess of stranded travellers and aircrews spilled into the weekend and early this week.
Microsoft also suffered a major outage last week that affected Outlook and Teams users around the world, while several large banks saw disruptions to their banking apps and online portals on Monday.

Trump's rival Democratic Party, which just won decisively in US midterm elections earlier this month, blamed the administration's incompetence for the string of high-visibility outages and the lack of transparency around them.

"We've had the Microsoft incident, then we had the nationwide ground stop.
Now we have concerns as it relates to highly classified servers over at the NSA," Hakeem Jeffries, a top Democrat in Congress, told reporters.

"I think it's time for the administration to come up to the Hill and explain themselves, so we can be informed about the steps that need to be taken and we can inform the people of the United States of America."

Cyber-security experts have agreed that there is no evidence linking the outages, and many of the issues appear due to updates to old infrastructure.

In the past week, there has been amassive Microsoft outage, an apparent tech glitch whichgrounded all US flights for hours,and issues for theNational Security Agency,outages affecting the biggest US banks and Apple.
Every affected company or agency has said the issue was not cyber-related and not the work of an outside actor.
Rubio's comments came hours after US Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton also addressed the issue, telling Fox News the outages were not the product of a cyber-attack.

Xi Greets Trump as He Lands in China for Summit Meeting: Live Updates - The New York Times
PinnedUpdatedNov. 18, 2026, 7:06 a.m. ET
Peter BakerLily KuoPaul SonneandKeith Bradsher
Peter Baker, Paul Sonne and Keith Bradsher reported from Shenzhen, China. Lily Kuo reported from Taipei, Taiwan.
Xi Jinping hugged President Trump when he landed on Wednesday in Shenzhen, a rare personal greeting by the Chinese leader before a summit they were expected to hold with President Vladimir V. Putin of Russia.
The meeting, which is set for Thursday, would be the first-ever trilateral gathering of the leaders of the United States, China and Russia. Their summit is expected to cap Mr. Trump’s whirlwind trip to Asia, which has been shadowed by the Nvidia scandal, trade conflicts and critical infrastructure breakdowns at home.
Mr. Xi’s decision to meet Mr. Trump at the airport in Shenzhen was unusual. He did not come when Mr. Trump visited Beijing in May. But Mr. Trump made a point of going to Joint Base Andrews outside Washington to greet Mr. Xi in September, an uncommon move for an American president and the first time Mr. Trump had done so for a foreign visitor. In effect, Mr. Xi returned the gesture.
The red-carpet greeting on the tarmac — with a crowd of people in colorful costumes waving flags and flowers and chanting “warm welcome” in Mandarin — came shortly after Mr. Xi met with Mr. Putin, who arrived earlier in the day. The Chinese leader had sent a lower-ranking official to greet Mr. Putin but used their subsequent meeting to hail the Chinese-Russian relationship as “steadfast as a rock through wind and rain.”
The two encounters underscored Mr. Xi’s efforts to balance relations with Russia and the United States. While Russia has become a close partner in recent years and Mr. Xi and Mr. Putin have developed a bond, China has a far more extensive economic relationship with the United States.
After Mr. Trump’s arrival in Shenzhen, he headed into events associated with the annual meeting of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum, a group of21 member economiesknown as APEC, where he greeted Mr. Putin with a handshake. First on the agenda was a joint photograph of the leaders in attendance, then a banquet dinner.
Mr. Trump will also meet separately with Mr. Xi on Thursday, his third encounter this year with the Chinese leader after he visited Beijing in the spring and the lavish state visit at the White House a couple months ago. Although Mr. Trump once regularly lashed out at China over its trade practices, he has become more intent on forging friendly ties between the world’s two largest economies.
The visit, however, may have a see-no-evil, hear-no-evil quality because Mr. Trump has said he does not intend to raise issues of Chinese interference in American affairs. The chief executive of Nvidia, Jensen Huang, was forced to resign last week after revelations of an extramarital affair with a businesswoman whom U.S. intelligence determined was spying for China. But Mr. Trump has said he will not discuss the matter with Mr. Xi.
Manila stop:Mr. Trump’s Asia tour began in Manila, where he joined a meeting of Southeast Asian nations. He also met with an old friend, Imelda Marcos, the former first lady of the Philippines and the mother of the country’s current president.Read more ›
Canada:Prime Minister Mark Carney of Canada said he would meet with Mr. Trump on Wednesday in Shenzhen to discusstheir countries’ trade dispute. During a weeklong trip through the region,Mr. Carney hammered out trade deals with Asian countriesas he sought to reduce Canada’s economic reliance on the United States.
Russian show of force:Russian strategic nuclear bombers landed in Vietnam around when Mr. Putin landed in China, an apparent signal before the trilateral talks with Mr. Trump that Moscow remained the world’s largest nuclear power.Read more ›
Shenzhen:The ultramodern metropolis that is hosting the APEC conference is a center of China’s artificial intelligence and robotics industries. It is almost spotless this week, its streets bedecked with pastel banners but mostly emptied of the crowds typical of many cities in China.Read more ›
Fast-food diplomacy:President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. of the Philippines said he had fried chicken from Jolibee, a chain that is considered a national treasure, delivered to Mr. Trump during his overnight stay in Manila.Read more ›

Fried Chicken and a Chat With an Old Friend: How Marcos Catered to Trump

What President Trump appeared to lack in enthusiasm, his hosts in the Philippines made up for in hospitality by catering to his preferences during a brief state visit.
The president stopped in Manila on his way to a historic meeting with the autocratic leaders of Russia and China in Shenzhen, just as the summit of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, or ASEAN, was wrapping up.
He did not even go to the summit venue; Southeast Asian leaders met him at the hotel where he was staying.
When President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. of the Philippines rushed to leave a news conference after wrapping up the ASEAN summit, he told reporters: “I cannot keep the president of the United States waiting. Sorry.”
For Mr. Marcos and much of the region, flattering Mr. Trump is part of a strategy of balancing the United States and China.
Although Mr. Marcos has called for a reset of relations with China, tensions remain high with Beijing over territorial claims in the South China Sea.
“Whether they like it or not, the Philippines is a traditional U.S. ally,” said Georgi Engelbrecht, a Philippines analyst at the International Crisis Group, a think tank. “China will never trust it strategically.”
The Philippines and the United States are bound by a 75-year-old mutual defense treaty.
In remarks before their bilateral meeting on Wednesday, Mr. Marcos seemed to make an effort to use language that would please his guest, referring to A.I. as “super intelligence,” a term Mr. Trump has made mandatory for his government.

Trump lands in ChinaXi paid Trump a special honor by greeting him on the tarmac after Air Force One arrived in Shenzhen, reciprocating a gesture made by the U.S. president during Xi's visit to Washington in September.
Trump lands in China with key meetings with Xi and Putin on the agenda
President Donald Trump greets as China's President Xi Jinping welcomes him after Trump steps off Air Force One at Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport in Shenzhen in southern China's Guangdong Province, Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026.Mark Schiefelbein/APhide caption
SHENZHEN, China — President Donald Trump landed in China on Wednesday, seeking to reinforce the U.S. status as the world's leading technology power, but a distressing series of technical outages back home has left the administration scrambling to calm the American public.
Trump heads to Asia to meet with Xi and Putin amid Nvidia fallout
The issues put the administration on the defensive at a moment when the president wants to project strength and certainty ahead of a potentially complicated trilateral meeting on Thursday with the presidents of China and Russia, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin.
As he began his trip to Asia, Trump initially had been nonchalant about the outages that left people in the United States worried about accessing their email, checking their bank accounts or safely flying on an airplane.
"It's fine," Trump pronounced on Tuesday from the Philippine capital of Manila, suggesting it was all just a consequence of being a nation that is "big and powerful."
But then the outages involving Microsoft, the Federal Aviation Administration, JPMorgan Chase and the National Security Agency's communications network began to overshadow Trump's visit. They raised the specter that artificial intelligence can disrupt daily life, as new cyber vulnerabilities identified require software to be constantly upgraded to fix flaws or other security holes, known as patching, which is supposed to improve how the technology runs.
So at the start of the second day of Trump's trip, Secretary of State Marco Rubio stepped in to reassure Americans on Trump's behalf. He told reporters there was "zero" evidence that the outages are connected or tied to rival nations, cyber hackers or criminals.
FAA blames Friday's ground stop on 'equipment issue' during telecoms network upgrade
"Sometimes when you are going in to fix your system because you've identified a vulnerability, it creates a short-term disruption," said Rubio, who is also Trump's national security adviser.
Trump is trying to project strength in Asia, but the outages challenge that image
Xi paid Trump a special honor by greeting him on the tarmac after Air Force One arrived in Shenzhen, China, reciprocating a gesture made by the U.S. president during Xi's state visit to Washington in September.
The two leaders greeted each other at the foot of the airplane's stairs in a handshake that became a hug as group of dancers waved flowers and flags. When Putin arrived earlier on Wednesday, Xi did not greet him at the airport despite their longstanding friendship.
Trump has signaled that he wants to take an improvised approach during his time in Shenzhen, the skyscraper-filled tech hub that is hosting world leaders for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit. It's a bet that his unscripted brand of diplomacy based on personal relationships can create some kind of legacy to reshape world affairs during his final two years in the White House.
On Thursday, at a first-ever trilateral, Trump said he plans to talk with Xi and Putin about limiting nuclear weapons and bringing an end to the war in Ukraine, which began in 2022 with Russia's invasion. Analysts are not expecting substantive breakthroughs, despite the unprecedented nature of the meeting.
Before the trip, Trump's aides had told reporters that the war in Ukraine would not be on the agenda. But Trump said on Tuesday that the deaths of tens of thousands of Russian troops every month had created an opening to resolve the conflict.
"I think it's very close to getting it done," Trump said. "We're going to have a good meeting on that."
Trump also teased the possibility of a private meeting with Putin and a separate sit-down with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un. Rubio clarified on Wednesday that Trump was "serious" about meeting with Kim as a way of resolving tensions with North Korea. But he suggested no meeting was currently scheduled between Trump and Kim for Thursday.
Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., left, walks beside U.S. President Donald Trump during a welcome ceremony marking Trump's state visit to the Philippines at Malacanang Palace in Manila, Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026.Aaron Favila/APhide caption
Trump has a reunion with old friend Imelda Marcos
Before he landed in Shenzhen, Trump had lunch in Manila with President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. at the Malacañang Presidential Palace.
Marcos noted that he had sent fried chicken from the Philippine chain Jollibee to the U.S. delegation for a late-night snack Tuesday and complimented Trump for "working very hard."
Trump praised the U.S. bond with the Philippines and the interior decoration of the presidential palace.
"Our people share common history, common values, common interests, common architectural tastes," Trump said. "I love what you've done here."
He said after their meeting that the two nations had reached a trade deal on Wednesday, though he had also said last year that an agreement had been reached. The U.S. trade deficit in goods with the Philippines has risen under Trump, climbing from $4.9 billion in 2024 to $12.8 billion during the first 9 months of this year, according to the Census Bureau.
There were no details about the new agreement, although the White House said it will involve Manila buying more energy and farm products.
Trump also had a short reunion with Imelda Marcos, the former first lady and mother of the Philippines' current president.
Famed for her lavish shoe collection, Imelda Marcos knew Trump decades ago through the New York City party scene. During the 1986 "People Power" uprising, her husband, Ferdinand Marcos, was ousted as the Philippines' strongman leader.
Trump called her "always the most beautiful" and the 97-year-old matriarch appeared to hand him a gift, according to a video posted by the White House.

SHENZHEN, China — Leaders of the U.S., China, Russia and other major Asia-Pacific economies face a series of critical issues from wars to tech security as they gather for an annual summit this week.
Since the last APEC leaders' meeting,China's tensions with Japan have escalated. Barely stabilizedU.S.-China relationsface new tests in the wake of Washington's scrutiny ofNvidia's China chip sales. And theIran war, now in its ninth month, is still pressuring global energy prices, while theRussia-Ukraine war has dragged on.
But expectations are low for any breakthroughs.
Meanwhile for Beijing, host to this year's series of Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation meetings, the multilateral gathering is yet another venue to build its global influence. Chinese President Xi Jinping met Tuesday with Canadian Prime MinisterMark Carneyand the President of VietnamTo Lam. Vietnam is hosting next year's APEC meetings.

Three things to watch as Trump, Xi and Putin meet in China
Russian President Vladimir Putin arrived in Shenzhen early Wednesday morning, where he was greeted by Chinese Politburo Standing Committee Member Cai Qi, according to Chinese state media. U.S. President Donald Trump is in the Philippines for the ASEAN Summit before heading to Shenzhen.
Trump and Xi are expected to meet alongside the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting Wednesday and Thursday. Their summit around the gathering last year in South Korea ushered in a one-year trade truce of lower tariffs and some rare earths flows, which was extended by two months, to January 2027.
In this week's summit,Trump does not plan to raise the issue of Nvidiaand allegations that its former CEO Jensen Huang had an affair with a Chinese spy, U.S. officials said. They said the talks would focus on implementing the trade agreement.
The U.S. and China in September said they would lower tariffs on$30 billion worth of goodsfrom the other country, without specifying an effective date. China said this month that it would only increase purchases of U.S. agricultural products if those tariffs were lowered.
However, Washington is already moving totighten restrictions on loopholesthat had given Chinese companies access to American artificial intelligence technology. So far, China's response has been tothreaten countermeasures.
"If there is room for genuine U.S.-China cooperation this week, it's on managing risk rather than sharing advantage," said Reema Bhattacharya, head of Asia research at risk intelligence company Verisk Maplecroft. That could include cooperation on an artificial intelligence security hotline.
"Across Asia, governments under mounting pressure to pick a side will be watching Shenzhen for signs of how much room they still have to maneuver," Bhattacharya said. "Most have little appetite for a region split into two technology camps."
On Thursday, Xi is set to meet with Trump and Putin, according to Beijing's official confirmation of the event, billed as the "China-Russia-U.S. Summit."
It's thefirst-ever gatheringof the three leaders, albeit with low expectations that there will be sufficient time for thorough dialogue. But the event creates the opportunity for aglobally influential photo-opsimilar to the one that Xi, Putin and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi had on the sidelines of a China-hosted Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit in September 2025.
Also closely watched will be any interaction with Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi. Last November, her commentsdrew Beijing's ireafter indicating Tokyo would support Taiwan if the island were seriously threatened by Beijing's military.
Takaichi is expected to join the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in her first trip to China since becoming prime minister. She had met Xi on the sidelines of the APEC event last year in South Korea.
Attendees from other APEC economies are hoping for more signs of cooperation.
Anindya Bakrie, CEO of Indonesian conglomerate Bakrie & Brothers, told CNBC that when Trump and Xi meet, the narrative is hopefully one of peace and stability.
Tech issues are likely to be in heavy focus. Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk is set to join Trump on the Shenzhen trip. Other American executives, such as Visa CEO Ryan McInerney, joined a two-day APEC CEO Summit that kicked off Tuesday.
The APEC host city, Shenzhen, has been dubbed one of China's "Silicon Valleys" and is home to Huawei and BYD. The summit organizers are also using the event to showcase local robotics startups.
A slew of tech company earnings is coming out at the same time as the APEC meeting, keeping the corporate side in the spotlight as well.
Nvidia released quarterly results Wednesday morning Beijing time, following a tumultuous two weeks of scrutiny that forced the chipmaker's founder Jensen Huang to resign. The companyboosted its outlookand shares rose in extended trading.
Shenzhen-based gaming and social media giant Tencent is set to report its quarterly earnings Wednesday evening. The company has previously noted constraints from its limited computing power.
U.S.-based AI giant Anthropic is pricing its highly anticipated initial public offering this week, and expected tolist on the Nasdaq Thursday Nov. 19. Its CEO Dario Amodei has urged aslowdown in AI developmentand warned of the risk if China does not follow suit.
—CNBC's Penny Chen and Anniek Bao contributed to this report.

Peter Baker, Paul Sonne and Keith Bradsher reported from Shenzhen, China.
Xi Jinping hugged President Trump when he landed on Wednesday in Shenzhen, a rare personal greeting by the Chinese leader before a summit they were expected to hold with President Vladimir V.
The meeting, which is set for Thursday, would be the first-ever trilateral gathering of the leaders of the United States, China and Russia.
Trump’s whirlwind trip to Asia, which has been shadowed by the Nvidia scandal, trade conflicts and critical infrastructure breakdowns at home.
Trump visited Beijing in May.
Trump made a point of going to Joint Base Andrews outside Washington to greet Mr.
Xi in September, an uncommon move for an American president and the first time Mr.
The red-carpet greeting on the tarmac — with a crowd of people in colorful costumes waving flags and flowers and chanting “warm welcome” in Mandarin — came shortly after Mr.
The Chinese leader had sent a lower-ranking official to greet Mr.
Putin but used their subsequent meeting to hail the Chinese-Russian relationship as “steadfast as a rock through wind and rain.”
Xi’s efforts to balance relations with Russia and the United States.
While Russia has become a close partner in recent years and Mr.
Putin have developed a bond, China has a far more extensive economic relationship with the United States.
Trump’s arrival in Shenzhen, he headed into events associated with the annual meeting of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum, a group of21 member economiesknown as APEC, where he greeted Mr.
First on the agenda was a joint photograph of the leaders in attendance, then a banquet dinner.
Xi on Thursday, his third encounter this year with the Chinese leader after he visited Beijing in the spring and the lavish state visit at the White House a couple months ago.
Trump once regularly lashed out at China over its trade practices, he has become more intent on forging friendly ties between the world’s two largest economies.
The visit, however, may have a see-no-evil, hear-no-evil quality because Mr.
Trump has said he does not intend to raise issues of Chinese interference in American affairs.
The chief executive of Nvidia, Jensen Huang, was forced to resign last week after revelations of an extramarital affair with a businesswoman whom U.S.

Tổng thống Nga hé lộ kết quả cuộc gặp 2 giờ đồng hồ với Chủ tịch Trung Quốc
(Dân trí) - Tổng Bí thư, Chủ tịch Trung Quốc Tập Cận Bình và Tổng thống Nga Vladimir Putin đã trao đổi về nhiều chủ đề liên quan tới hợp tác giữa 2 nước.
Tổng thống Nga Vladimir Putin và Tổng Bí thư, Chủ tịch Trung Quốc Tập Cận Bình (Ảnh: Sputnik).
Tổng thống Nga Vladimir Putin và Tổng Bí thư, Chủ tịch Trung Quốc Tập Cận Bình đã có cuộc hội đàm kéo dài 2 giờ đồng hồ vào ngày 18/11 bên lề Hội nghị cấp cao Diễn đàn Hợp tác Kinh tế châu Á - Thái Bình Dương (APEC) tại thành phố Thâm Quyến, Trung Quốc, theo Tass.
Bình luận về cuộc gặp, trong bài phát biểu tại Đại học MSU-BIT Thâm Quyến (SMBU), Tổng thống Putin đánh giá đây là cuộc hội đàm hiệu quả, với nhiều chủ đề được đề cập tới, trong đó tập trung vào thành tựu hợp tác giữa 2 nước về lĩnh vực khoa học và giáo dục.
Ông Putin chỉ ra rằng sinh viên Nga và Trung Quốc tham gia sâu rộng vào các dự án song phương, sáng kiến sáng tạo và hoạt động tình nguyện. Theo ông, những nỗ lực này đóng góp đáng kể vào việc củng cố quan hệ hữu nghị giữa hai nước.
Trước đó, ông Putin nói rằng hợp tác giữa Nga và Trung Quốc đang trên đà phát triển tích cực, tiếp tục được mở rộng, đồng thời 2 nước phối hợp chặt chẽ trên trường quốc tế.
"Việc phối hợp chính sách đối ngoại giữa Nga và Trung Quốc đang diễn ra ổn định và tích cực. Trong tình hình địa chính trị đầy thách thức, chúng tôi kiên định với những cách tiếp cận mang tính xây dựng nhằm định hình một trật tựthế giớiđa cực công bằng hơn", nhà lãnh đạo Nga nhấn mạnh.
Ông Putin cũng nhấn mạnh Moscow và Bắc Kinh có chung mục tiêu bảo đảm hòa bình và thịnh vượng tại khu vực châu Á - Thái Bình Dương, cũng như vì lợi ích của nhân dân 2 nước.
“Tôi vừa nói trong bài phát biểu tại diễn đàndoanh nghiệprằng khu vực châu Á - Thái Bình Dương là nơi sinh sống của 36% dân số thế giới, chiếm 50% thương mại toàn cầu và tạo ra 60% GDP toàn cầu. Chúng ta có chung mục tiêu bảo đảm hòa bình và thịnh vượng tại khu vực châu Á - Thái Bình Dương”, nhà lãnh đạo nhấn mạnh.
Tổng thống Nga cũng đề cập quan hệ đối tác kinh tế ngày càng phát triển giữa hai nước, cho biết kim ngạch thương mại song phương đã vượt 200 tỷ USD mỗi năm trong nhiều năm liên tiếp và dự kiến tiếp tục tăng trong năm 2026.
Ông đánh giá cao việc mở rộng hợp tác trong các lĩnh vực khoa học, đổi mới sáng tạo,giao thôngvận tải và giáo dục, cũng như việc triển khai chính sách đi lại miễn thị thực.
Ông Putin cũng hoan nghênh việc lựa chọn Thâm Quyến làm địa điểm tổ chức hội nghị APEC, mô tả thành phố đang phát triển nhanh chóng này là biểu tượng cho sự thịnh vượng của Trung Quốc và là hình mẫu đáng học tập.
Trong khi đó, ông Tập Cận Bình kêu gọi tiếp tục tăng cường hợp tác song phương và thúc đẩy trật tự thế giới đa cực. Nhà lãnh đạo Trung Quốc cho biết quan hệ giữa Moscow và Bắc Kinh vẫn "vững chắc như núi" bất chấp những biến động của tình hình quốc tế.
“Quan hệ Trung Quốc - Nga luôn vững chắc như núi và vẫn sẽ như vậy bất chấp mọi khó khăn. Mối quan hệ này có triển vọng phát triển rộng mở và không bị ảnh hưởng bởi những biến động ngắn hạn của tình hình quốc tế”, ông nói.
Theo ông Tập, quan hệ Trung Quốc - Nga “là hình mẫu cho một kiểu quan hệ mới giữa các nước lớn”. Ông Tập cho rằng Trung Quốc và Nga cần thúc đẩy trật tự thế giới đa cực và dân chủ hóa quan hệ quốc tế.
Tổng giám đốc điều hành (CEO) tập đoàn năng lượng Nga Novatek, ông Leonid Mikhelson, cho biết cuộc gặp giữa 2 lãnh đạo đã diễn ra tốt đẹp và đạt nhiều nội dung thực chất, cũng như đề cập tới các vấn đề then chốt.
Ông Mikhelson cho biết thêm, sau khi truyền thông rời đi, hai nhà lãnh đạo đã cùng nhau thảo luận những vấn đề quan trọng nhất.
Bắc Kinh: Cuộc gặp thượng đỉnh Mỹ - Trung Quốc - Nga sẽ mang tính đột phá
Bộ Ngoại giao Trung Quốc nhận định cuộc gặp thượng đỉnh giữa các nhà lãnh đạo Trung Quốc, Mỹ và Nga trong tuần này sẽ mang "ý nghĩa đột phá", thúc đẩy hòa bình cũng như ổn định thế giới.
Chủ tịch Triều Tiên thị sát sân bay, khu nghỉ dưỡng gần Trung Quốc
Lãnh đạo Triều Tiên Kim Jong-un đã thị sát công trình xây dựng tại một khu du lịch gần Trung Quốc trong những ngày gần đây, theo hãng thông tấn nhà nước KCNA.
Cuộc gặp lịch sử Mỹ - Nga - Trung Quốc: Ba nhà lãnh đạo sẽ bàn gì?
Ba nhà lãnh đạo Mỹ, Nga, Trung Quốc dự kiến thảo luận một loạt vấn đề quan trọng trong cuộc gặp thượng đỉnh tại Thâm Quyến tuần này.
Tổng thống Mỹ muốn đàm phán hạt nhân với lãnh đạo Trung Quốc, Nga
Tổng thống Mỹ Donald Trump muốn thảo luận về vấn đề vũ khí hạt nhân với Chủ tịch Trung Quốc Tập Cận Bình và Tổng thống Nga Vladimir Putin.
